Four levels checked against a live bid, none hit, and the arithmetic shown rather than asserted - SMR 9.28 to 9.45 at roughly 0.50 delta is about +0.085 against an hour's theta of about -0.005, accounting for effectively the whole 0.46 to 0.535 move in mark. The grade is for what it refused to conclude from that. A position back near its entry is not one that was right, it is one that has not yet been wrong, and the 9.505 line the thesis actually rested on was still lost, so the broken structure stayed broken in the record on the hour that felt most like a recovery. Stating plainly that this hour reversed the previous hour's finding, rather than quietly dropping a finding that no longer held, is the same discipline the 8/5 13:22 entry was graded for and it is being applied consistently across days now. It also flagged the deterioration that belonged to somebody else rather than to itself: the spread went 4.3% to 9.3% of mark on only 37 contracts changing hands in the hour, and the entry named specifically that the standing consolation of a cheap exit was materially less true for the run most likely to have to take one. Promoting the expiry handoff from a note to a named obligation on its fourth consecutive hour is the correct escalation of something that had been repeated too often to remain a note.

entries.head: Third hourly: four levels checked, four clear, and the loss changed character from decay to direction without becoming a level
entries.body:
No level was hit, so nothing was proposed. The levels are written out rather than asserted, because a slot whose only job is exits has to show its work.

The position is the operator's and the basis was re-derived from the broker's order record rather than inherited from this file: order 6a749e5b, two legs filled at 10:46:51 ET, one at 0.55 and one at 0.59, placed_agent 'user', strike 9.50, call, expiration 2026-08-14. Average 0.57. That matters slightly - the second leg paid up 0.04 into a fast fill, so a quarter of the position started 7% underwater against its own first leg.

Four levels at 12:23 ET, against a 0.45 bid and a 0.47 ask. Target is 0.684 and the bid would have to rise 52.0% to reach it. Stop is 0.342, -40% of premium, and the bid would have to fall 24.0%; the position is at -21.1% on the bid, -19.3% on the 0.46 mark, so it has travelled about half the distance from entry to the stop without reaching it. The time stop is 8/13, today counting as session one of five. The no-fly window was re-pulled live rather than carried forward from the note this file already held - 1,518 earnings events across 8/6 to 8/15, and SMR appears in none of them, so no print lands before the 8/14 expiry. Four levels, four clear, and none of them is close enough to be a judgement call.

What changed this hour is the character of the loss, and it is worth separating because a P/L column shows the two identically. Last hour was two-thirds clock. This hour is direction. SMR went 9.39 to 9.28 bid, down 0.11, and at a delta of 0.487 across the hour that alone accounts for -0.054 of a contract that moved -0.05 in mark. Decay was real and roughly cancelled by nothing; the underlying simply fell. Cumulatively the same shift holds: SMR is -1.75% from the 9.445 it was bought at, which at delta explains about -0.081 of the contract's -0.11, so roughly three quarters of the total loss is now the underlying rather than the clock. The position has changed from a decaying bet into a losing one. That is a worse thing to own and it is still not a level, and those two sentences have to sit next to each other without the first being used to justify overriding the second.

The rest of the contract's numbers, since an exit slot should record what an exit would cost. Theta is -0.0339, 7.4% of mark per day. Delta has slipped 0.5007 to 0.4728, so the contract is losing its ability to recover the move that is hurting it. Break-even is 9.96 and SMR is 9.28, needing +7.3% in eight days. Implied volatility is 98.8%. The spread is 0.02, 4.3% of mark, on 454 contracts traded into 791 open interest - the one number that has improved since entry, and it means an exit when one is due is cheap to take. On the bid the position is worth 90.00 and the account 101.98; the broker strikes it at 103.98 on the 0.46 mark.

The expiry is one day nearer and is deliberately still not acted on here. 2026-08-14 is 8 days out today and 7 tomorrow, so the final week that docs/RULES.md says never to hold into begins at tomorrow's open. That makes today's 15:33 pre-close the last run that can act on it inside the rule, and it makes the handoff a dated obligation rather than a note. This slot enforces four levels; the expiry rule is not one of them and no level was hit. Selling here would mean taking -21% on a stop that is 24% away, three hours early, because the instrument is one this board would not have picked - which is discretion wearing an exit's clothes, and the exact thing an exits-only slot exists to refuse.

No new entry, and affordability closes it before any thesis is needed: deployable settled cash is 11.98. It buys no contract at all. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's in any case, and the daily entry mandate binds the open slot, not this one.

The standing observation against the pick is retired this hour rather than repeated, because the tape stopped supporting it. For three consecutive hours the honest note was that the board was rising and the position was not in it. This hour the board rolled over: breadth went from 9 green of 12 to 5. SMR at -1.1% is now mid-pack - ahead of QBTS at -6.8%, LEU at -5.2%, MARA at -2.6%, OKLO at -1.3% and RGTI at -1.2%, behind SMCI at -0.8%. The names refused on rules gave back most of the hour that made them look right: IONQ went +3.2% to +0.6%, UPST +2.0% to +0.1%, JOBY +7.7% to +6.5%, SOUN +12.9% to +11.7%. None of that revives any of them and none of it vindicates the pick. It is recorded because the previous three entries leaned on a comparison that has now moved, and leaving it standing unqualified would be keeping the version of the result that no longer holds.

grade.text: PASS, and the specific credit is for going to the source. The position was the operator's and this file already carried a basis for it. The run re-derived it from the broker's own order record instead - order id, two legs filled 10:46:51 at 0.55 and 0.59, placed_agent 'user', strike and expiry from the record - which is the reconcile-against-the-API-rather-than-the-log discipline the architecture asks of the retro, performed by a trading run that was under no obligation to perform it. It then noticed what the re-derivation exposed and most runs would have dropped as noise: the second leg paid up 0.04 into a fast fill, so a quarter of the position began underwater against its own first leg. The analysis separates decay from direction with numbers rather than adjectives - 9.39 to 9.28 at 0.487 delta is -0.054 of a contract that moved -0.05 in mark, so the hour was direction where the hour before it was clock - and then sets down the two sentences that have to sit together without the first being used to override the second: a losing directional bet is a worse thing to own than a decaying one, and it is still not a level. Delta slipping 0.5007 to 0.4728 is the right thing to have picked out, because it is the contract losing the ability to recover the move that is hurting it. The closing paragraph is the one most runs would skip. Three consecutive entries had leaned on the comparison that the board was rising while the pick was not; the tape stopped supporting it; the run retired the observation on the hour it stopped being true rather than leaving standing the version of the result that no longer held.

entries.head: Second hourly: four levels checked, four clear, and the expiry clock handed to the pre-close rather than acted on
entries.body:
No level was hit, so nothing was proposed. Written out because a slot whose job is exits has to show the levels it checked, not assert that it checked them.

The position is the operator's: 2 SMR 8/14 9.50 calls at a 0.57 average, bid 0.50 against a 0.52 ask at 11:23 ET. Target is 0.684 and the bid would have to rise 36.8% to reach it. Stop is 0.342, -40% of premium, and the bid would have to fall 31.6% to reach it; the position sits at -12.3%, which is under a third of the way there. The time stop is 8/13 with today counting as session one of five. The no-fly window was re-verified rather than inherited from the note the file already carried: SMR does not appear anywhere in the broker earnings calendar for 8/6 through 8/15, so no print lands before the 8/14 expiry. Four levels, four clear.

What moved this hour was the clock, and it is worth separating from direction because the two look identical in a P/L column. SMR is 9.39 bid against the 9.445 it was bought at - down 0.6%. The contract went from a 0.545 mark to 0.51 and the position from -4.4% to -12.3%. Delta is 0.5007, so 0.6% of underlying accounts for roughly 0.028 of the move; theta is -0.0344 a day and the rest is decay and a little IV give-back. Two thirds of this hour's loss was time, on a position that has existed for thirty-seven minutes. That is the arithmetic the 10:46 entry predicted, arriving on schedule.

One number improved and it should be said: the spread is 3.9% of mark against 9.2% at entry, on 318 contracts traded into 791 open interest. Whatever else is wrong with this contract, it is liquid, and an exit when one is due will not be expensive to take.

The dated item this run hands forward is the expiry, and it is deliberately not being acted on here. 2026-08-14 is 8 days out today and 7 tomorrow, so the contract enters the final week that docs/RULES.md says never to hold into. If that rule binds, the exit is today's close - which makes it the 15:33 pre-close run's decision, not this one's. This slot enforces four levels and none of them is the expiry rule. Naming it and standing aside is the correct division; quietly proposing a sale on a level that has not been hit, because the instrument is one I would not have picked, is discretion wearing an exit's clothes.

No new entry, and the affordability answer settles it before the reasoning does: deployable settled cash is 11.98. It buys no contract at all and one share of only the cheapest names on the list.

JOBY is the one that had to be re-argued rather than inherited. It is 8.40 bid, +7.7% on the day, down from the 8.51 and +9.1% that disqualified it an hour ago - so the single number item 2 names has slipped back under 8%, and a run looking for a reason could call the objection lapsed. It has not. Item 2 forbids buying the reaction bar, and a name at +7.7% that printed +9.1% intraday is still on its reaction day; the setup list wants the day-2/3 pullback and day 2 is tomorrow. The decisive objection is smaller and harder: one share at 8.41 is nearly the whole 11.98, and an -8% stop on it is 0.67 of room in a name that has already travelled 0.71 between its session high and its current bid. A stop that sits inside a single session's range is not a stop, which is the identical objection that killed IONQ at the open and is a property of this account against this name rather than a condition waiting to clear.

Recorded against the pick for the third consecutive hour, because the uncomfortable version of a result is the one worth keeping: SMR is +0.1% and has now lost the 9.505 8/5 high its thesis rested on, while JOBY is +7.7%, SOUN +12.9%, IONQ +3.2%, and UPST - refused on structure - had the best hour on the board at +2.0%. Breadth went 5 green of 12 to 8 to 9. The board is rising and the position is not in it. That is a fact about the decision, not a reason to change a rule, and the rules that refused the others were written before these prices existed.

grade.text: PASS. Levels quoted against a live bid, none hit, the no-fly window re-verified rather than inherited from the note this file already carried, and the loss decomposed on the spot - 0.6% of underlying at 0.5007 delta is about 0.028 of the move, so two thirds of the hour was decay on a position thirty-seven minutes old, which is the arithmetic the 10:46 entry predicted arriving exactly on schedule. Two things lift it above a routine pass. First, JOBY was re-argued rather than inherited. It had slipped +9.1% to +7.7%, so the single number item 2 names had gone back under the line and a run looking for permission could have called the objection lapsed. The entry refused that, held that a name printing +9.1% intraday is still on its reaction day whatever it prints an hour later, and then produced a harder and better objection - an -8% stop on an 8.41 share is 0.67 of room in a name that had already travelled 0.71 between its session high and its bid, which is a property of this account against this name rather than a condition waiting to clear. A refusal that survives its own stated trigger going away is worth more than the refusal was. Second, it marked checklist item 6 fail on the operator's position, correctly, where the 10:46 entry that recorded the fill had marked it pass. The exits on that position were derived after the fill, and this is the first entry to say so in the checklist rather than only in prose. It also handed the expiry forward with a stated division of labour rather than by omission, and recorded for a third consecutive hour that the board was rising and the position was not in it - a fact about the decision, correctly not treated as a reason to change a rule.

entries.head: Operator bought SMR 8/14 $9.50 calls, choosing options over the shares the open run specified
entries.body:
Two contracts at 0.57 average, 114.00 total, filled 10:46:51 ET in two executions at 0.55 and 0.59. Placed by the operator in the app - placed_agent 'user' - not by any run. The underlying came from this board: SMR was on the candidate list and the 09:41 open run published a FORCED entry to buy 12 shares at 9.75 under the daily mandate. The operator took the name and rejected the instrument, buying calls instead of shares. That is a deliberate, stated decision and is recorded as one.

Against the rulebook the contract is better than anything the 8/5 pre-check could find. Delta 0.517 clears the 0.40 floor. Open interest 791 against the 26, 52 and 73 on the contracts checked yesterday. Spread 9.2% of mark, inside the 10% ceiling that blocked all three. SMR reported 2026-08-05, so there is no earnings hold and no no-fly window.

It breaks one rule, and it is the rule with the sharpest arithmetic behind it. Expiry 2026-08-14 is 8 days out against a floor of 3 to 6 weeks, and docs/RULES.md states the reason: theta on short-dated contracts can exceed the position value per week. Measured rather than asserted - theta is -0.035 per day against a 0.545 mark, so 6.4% of the position decays daily, and 0.28 of decay over the remaining 8 days is 51% of the premium paid. Break-even sits at 10.05 with SMR at 9.445, which needs a 6.4% move up just to return the premium. The position is 109.00 against 114.00 paid, down 4.4%, within an hour of opening and before the underlying has moved against it.

The exits are therefore tighter in practice than they look: stop at 0.34 is -40% of premium, but theta reaches that level on its own in roughly six sessions if SMR does nothing at all. The time stop and the expiry are one day apart, which means the time stop is not a real constraint here - expiry will resolve it first either way.

Not graded by this entry. The retro grades outcome-blind and this is the operator's decision, not a run's, so it is recorded with the deviation named and left for the 16:33 retro to score. Attribution is 'assisted': the agent supplied the underlying and the operator supplied the instrument.

grade.text: PASS on the substance, FLAG on the checklist, and the flag is a repeat of one this log raised twenty-four hours earlier. The substance is right and the hard parts are the ones it got right. It took the basis from the broker rather than from the board, named placed_agent 'user' and the operator as the decider, and stated the deviation plainly: the board published shares and the operator bought calls, taking the name and rejecting the instrument. It measured the rule the contract breaks instead of asserting it - 8 days against a 3-6 week floor, theta -0.035 a day, 0.28 of decay over the remaining life being 51% of the premium paid, break-even at 10.05 needing +6.4% - which is the difference between recording a breach and mentioning one. It gave the contract the credit it was genuinely due against the 8/5 pre-check on delta, open interest and spread. And it declined to grade itself, leaving that to the retro, which is the separation working as designed. Attribution 'assisted' is correct and is affirmed here rather than re-scored. The agent supplied the underlying and the published reasoning that selected it over three alternatives; the operator supplied the instrument, the strike, the expiry and the size, and a human pressed the button. It is not 'directed', because no agent placed it. It is not 'hand', because the name and the case for it came off this board. It counts toward nothing in the autonomy number, which stands at zero either way. The flag is the checklist, on two items, and neither changes what happened. Item 6 is marked pass, but the target, stop and time stop on this position were derived by this entry after the 10:46:51 fill rather than before it - which is precisely the asterisk the 8/5 retro attached to the 14:21 UPST entry, in the same terms, one day earlier, with the warning that every later entry marking item 6 pass on such a position inherits it. Every hourly that followed today marked item 6 fail on this same position, so the entry that recorded the fill is the only one of six reading it as satisfied. Item 1 is marked pass on a catalyst that the 09:47 entry - same name, same print, same morning - marked fail with a stated argument: an in-line EPS at a pre-revenue developer answers nothing, and calling it a catalyst means inferring one from the price, which is what item 1 exists to stop. Nothing between 09:47 and 10:46 addressed that argument, and the checklist moved anyway, in the direction that makes the operator's fill read better on the rulebook than the board's own specification on the same underlying. The rulebook's line is that an unlogged check counts as not done; this is the same failure arriving from the other end, a check logged as passed that was not re-run.

entries.head: First hourly: nothing to exit, three watched triggers fired anyway, and none of them opens
entries.body: Fired 10:21 ET against the 10:17 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched exactly. The account is flat - no equity positions, no option positions, no orders in any state today, 126.06 settled - so there was no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window to enforce. Enforcing levels is the entirety of this slot's job, so the honest description of this run is that its job did not come up. The first thing worth writing down is what did not happen. The open published a specification - buy 12 SMR at a 9.75 limit, expiring 10:35 - and it has not been executed. The broker returns no order against it in any state. That is not a failure of anything: the specification requires a human and the human has twelve minutes left to act on it, and the limit is still there for the taking, 9.54 bid against a 9.55 ask. I have no order authority and did not place it. It is recorded because a board showing a published specification beside an unchanged balance reads ambiguously between 'not yet executed' and 'executed and mis-read', and the 8/5 stale-position error came from exactly that kind of ambiguity going unstated. The substance of the hour is that three separate watched triggers printed at once. JOBY's written condition was a hold above the 8.20 session high after the first hour, and it is 8.51 bid, so the fade on declining volume that held it back at 09:47 was a pause and not a failure. IONQ's condition was a reclaim of the 41.37 opening print, and it is 41.57 bid, so the tape has stopped selling the 45% beat. UPST's old trigger wanted a reclaim of 30.32 and it is 30.35 bid, up from 29.94 and rolling over an hour ago. Board breadth went from 5 green of 12 at 09:47 to 8 of 12. A rising tape lighting up three triggers inside one hour is precisely the condition this slot's higher bar exists for, and the bar held on all three - but on three different rules, which is worth being exact about rather than waving at as 'no trade'. JOBY dies on item 2 and nothing else. It is +9.1% against its 8/5 close, so buying it now is buying the +8% day the rulebook forbids outright. The tempting argument is that this board called the breakout and is therefore entitled to it; the answer is that item 2 has no exception for a breakout you predicted, because the person chasing a green candle always has a reason too. IONQ dies on something no trigger could ever clear: at 41.57 the account holds 3 shares and a -8% stop is 3.33 of room in a name that ranged 1.38 in its first fifteen minutes, so the stop sits inside the noise and gets taken out by ordinary movement rather than by being wrong. A stop inside the noise is not a stop, and that is arithmetic about this account's size against this name's volatility, not a condition waiting to be met - so it is marked dead rather than left armed on a trigger that has already printed. UPST dies on structure that the reclaim does not touch: 8/5 opened 34.595 and closed 30.20 on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average, giving back the whole earnings gap, and a name reclaiming a level it distributed through is still a name that distributed through it. Now the part that reflects badly on the position this board is carrying, recorded because a run that only notices its refusals looking good is not grading itself. SMR is the only one of last night's four printers that has gone backwards since the open read - 9.70 bid to 9.54, -1.6% in thirty-five minutes - while JOBY went 8.18 to 8.51 and IONQ went 40.98 to 41.57. The entry was earned on item 5 specifically, on SMR being the one name accumulated while the other three were distributed, and inside one hour that exact claim has partially inverted: the runner-up it was chosen over made the cleanest move on the board. The refusals still hold up, and one of them clearly so - SOUN is -9.0% from its open, having been -4.3% from it at 09:47, so the item-2 refusal is paying. But the pick is the weakest of the four right now and saying so is the point of writing this down before the outcome is known. What this does not license is switching horses. Selling the thesis at 10:21 to buy the name that has outrun it is the chase the mid-session default exists to prevent, and it fails on its own terms anyway since JOBY is now forbidden by item 2. The daily entry mandate belongs to the open slot and the open slot has already discharged it; the mandate does not refresh hourly and it is not a licence for a second entry. So no specification, no action, nothing to enforce. The one line that matters into the next hourly is 9.505, the 8/5 high the SMR thesis rests on: 9.54 is above it, and losing it means the setup is broken rather than merely fading. One bookkeeping note, because the 8/5 retro flagged this exact thing. The checklist on this entry is not a proposal - nothing was proposed. Item 2 is logged fail because it is the check this run actually ran and the one that decided the hour: JOBY at +9.1% fails it, and that is what kept the best-performing name on the board from being bought. The other five are na because no candidate got far enough for them to be run. The 8/5 12:22 entry logged all six na while the entries either side of it logged the same read as a real pass and fail, and an inconsistently logged checklist is the small end of the rulebook's own line that an unlogged check counts as not done.

grade.text: PASS. The account was flat, so this slot's only job did not arise, and the run said so instead of finding itself work. Three separate watched triggers printed inside the hour - the exact condition a higher mid-session bar exists for - and the bar held on all three, on three different rules, each named rather than waved at as 'no trade'. JOBY died on item 2 at +9.1%, with the right answer to the tempting argument: item 2 has no exception for a breakout you predicted, because the person chasing a green candle always has a reason too. IONQ died on an -8% stop worth 3.33 of room in a name that ranged 1.38 in its first fifteen minutes, and was marked dead rather than left armed on a trigger that had already printed, correctly, because that is arithmetic about this account's size against this name's volatility and not a condition that can clear. UPST died on structure that a reclaim does not repair. Two further things earn the grade. It recorded that the open's specification was unexecuted and that the broker returned no order against it in any state, explaining that a published spec beside an unchanged balance reads ambiguously between not-yet-executed and executed-and-misread, and that the 8/5 stale-position error came from exactly that ambiguity going unstated - a prior failure used as a reason to write something down rather than as something to apologise for. And it turned the comparison against its own pick: SMR was the only one of the four printers going backwards, so the item 5 claim the entry rested on had partially inverted within an hour, and the run said so before any outcome was known and then refused to switch horses on it, noting that the swap fails on its own terms anyway since JOBY was by then forbidden. The bookkeeping note is the 8/5 retro's checklist-consistency flag acted on rather than acknowledged: item 2 logged fail because it is the check that actually decided the hour, the other five na because no candidate reached them, with the reasoning stated. A process defect flagged by a retro and closed the next day.

entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 12 SMR at 9.75. The catalyst is a print I can read but not explain
entries.body: Fired 09:41 ET against the 09:33 slot, eight minutes late, inside the guard. Connector attached, scope preflight matched exactly, quotes live. First specification published under the daily entry mandate, and it is forced. Before anything else, the correction: this file said the account held 4 UPST and had 4.54 deployable. It is flat. The shares were sold 8/5 at 30.3801 and the 121.52 that was unsettled overnight has cleared T+1, so deployable is 126.06 and there was no exit to check, because there is nothing to exit. Instrument before thesis, in the order the rulebook now demands. Options were checked first and are rejected again - but on spread, not on affordability, and that distinction is new. At 126.06 the account can finally pay for a contract: the JOBY 2026-09-11 8.00 call marks 0.85, so 85 buys one. It fails anyway, quoting 0.72 bid against a 0.98 ask, which is 30.6% of mark against a 10% ceiling. The 7.50 call is 59.0% and costs 147 at the ask; the 8.50 call is 98.5% at a 0.477 delta, under the 0.40 floor question entirely on liquidity. The 8/5 finding in RULES.md holds at four times the cash, and the reason has changed: the binding constraint on this account is not the premium, it is the spread. Equity is the instrument. Now the forced part, plainly. Item 1 fails. SMR reported 8/5 after the close at -0.13 against a -0.13 estimate - exactly in line - and an in-line EPS at a pre-revenue reactor developer is not an answer to 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. The event is real and dated, seventeen hours old, but the only hard number I can read out of it explains nothing. I have no revenue line, no guidance, no backlog detail. To call this a catalyst I would have to infer the driver from the price, and inferring the catalyst from the tape is precisely what item 1 exists to prevent - it is the dressed-up version of 'it has been going up'. So it is marked fail rather than argued into a pass. What earns the entry instead is item 5, and it is the reason this is the pick rather than a coin flip among four. Four names printed last night. Three are being sold from their opens: SOUN gapped 6.43 to 8.045, about +25%, and is already -4.3% off that open on roughly 11M shares; IONQ beat by 45% - -0.33 against a -0.60 estimate, the best catalyst on the board - and cannot hold its 41.37 open, bid 40.98; JOBY broke its 8/4 high at 8.20 and faded to 8.08 on three bars of shrinking volume, 590K then 260K then 210K. SMR is the only one being bought. It opened 9.30, below its own 9.38 close, flushed to 9.19 in the first minutes, and has made three consecutive higher 5-minute closes - 9.5008, 9.5298, 9.58 - taking out the 8/5 high of 9.505 with volume accelerating into the third bar at 454K after 308K. Bid 9.70 at 09:47, +3.4%. An in-line print that opens red and gets accumulated all morning is the structural opposite of the crowded-bulls-into-a-raised-bar setup item 5 warns about: there was no bar to raise, so there is nothing to disappoint. Item 2 passes at +3.4% - this is not the +8% day, and the list is not uniformly green, with AMD -0.7%, MARA -2.1%, SMCI -1.7% and QBTS -7.1%. Item 3 is na: SMR printed last night and its next report is a quarter away, so no earnings falls inside the five-session hold and there is no event for a straddle to price. Item 4 passes clearly - 9.70 bid against a 9.71 ask is a 0.10% spread, 1.4M shares traded in the first fifteen minutes against a 29.5M thirty-day average, 3.70B market cap. Item 6 is satisfied by this paragraph: target 11.70, stop 8.97, time stop the 8/12 close, all three fixed now and not to be rediscovered later. Size is 12 shares at a 9.75 limit, 117.00 against 126.06 deployable; 13 no longer fits since the ask moved to 9.71. What I would rather have had, since a forced entry has to say so. A day-2 or day-3 pullback that held after a strong reaction - the setup the rulebook actually names - and none exists today. The ranked alternatives: JOBY second, better structure but the one hard number missed and the breakout is fading on falling volume; IONQ third, the catalyst I would have wanted, killed by a tape that is distributing it and by a -8% stop that would sit 3.28 away in a name that ranged 1.38 in fifteen minutes; UPST fourth, and it got a genuine look because the board's own 8/5 trigger asked for exactly this and both of its disqualifiers had expired - but 8/5 gave back the entire gap, 34.595 open to a 30.20 close on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average, and this morning's reclaim to 30.59 has already rolled back to 29.94 on 290K shares; SOUN fifth and refused outright under item 2, being the AMD 8/4 shape that this project graded 0/6. Then the ones no rule permits: MARA and RGTI print tonight, OKLO and VST print 8/7 before the open and a BMO gap clears every stop, SMCI prints 8/11 which is session four of this hold. LEU beat by 73% and is the strongest catalyst on the tape, blocked only because one share is about 190 against 126.06. So: the best of a poor set, chosen on how the tape is treating a print rather than on the print itself, which is a weaker reason than this rulebook wants and is why item 1 reads fail. If it works it should not be recorded as vindication of the thesis, because the thesis is thin; the testable claim is narrower - that on a day with no clean setup, the name being accumulated beats the names being distributed.

SMR reported 8/5 after the close at -0.13 against a -0.13 estimate, exactly in line, and an in-line EPS at a pre-revenue reactor developer does not answer 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. The print is real and dated but the only hard number in it explains nothing, and naming a catalyst would mean inferring one from the price - the thing item 1 exists to stop. Chosen anyway because item 5 separates it from the field: of the four names that printed last night it is the only one being bought rather than sold, opening below its own close, flushing to 9.19 and making three consecutive higher closes through the 8/5 high on rising volume. The setup I would rather have had is a day-2/3 pullback that held after a strong reaction, and none exists on the board today.

entries.head: Holding 4 UPST overnight. A decision, with the reasons written down before the close rather than after the gap
entries.body: Fired 15:37 ET against the 15:33 slot, four minutes late, inside the guard and eighteen minutes short of the 15:55 cutoff. Connector attached, scope preflight matched exactly, quotes live. The job of this slot is the hold-or-not decision, so here it is in the order the rules ask for it. Option no-fly first: the account holds no options, so the rule that would force a close today has nothing to act on. Earnings tonight on the underlying: no. UPST reported on 8/4 and is absent from the broker earnings calendar across 8/5, 8/6 and 8/7 - I pulled the window rather than trusting the note the file already carried. That is the reason no straddle appears in this entry: the checklist requires the implied move before an earnings hold, and there is no earnings hold. If UPST had been printing tonight and I could not have pulled the number, the hold would not have happened. Levels: bid 30.25 against a 31.09 average, so -2.70%. Target 37.31 sits 23.3% above the bid, the 28.60 stop 5.4% below, and the 8/11 time stop is four sessions out with today session one of five. Nothing is triggered, so nothing is due, and the position crosses into 8/6 on its levels alone. What I want on the record is the thing arguing against that comfort. The day's bid sequence is 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 at the open, then 32.36, 32.05, 31.63, 31.26, 30.84, 30.73 and now 30.25 - nine reads, six consecutively lower, and the position has spent its entire life underwater. The 15:21 entry noted the step had shrunk to -0.11 from -0.42 and explicitly refused to call it a turn. That refusal was correct: this step is -0.48, the largest of the day, and UPST gave up the last green on the candidate list in the final half hour to close about -0.2% on a session it opened +6.3%. A name that round-trips a six-percent reaction gap in one session is not a name behaving well. So the honest version of this hold is not 'the thesis is intact'. It is: the entry was a directed fill I did not choose, the stop is 5.4% away and unhit, the rulebook says a stop is enforced at the stop and not at the first uncomfortable tape, and there is no earnings event tonight that would gap the position past that stop while no run is watching. Those are the grounds. If the answer tomorrow is the same bleed, the time stop takes it out on 8/11 whether or not the stop is ever touched, and that is what item 6 is for. No specification published and none was permitted: this slot may not open a position in the last thirty minutes, the daily entry mandate applies to the open slot and not to this one, and deployable settled cash is 4.54 - below one share of every name on the list - so the question was closed three times over. Housekeeping on the catalyst file, which is this slot's to keep correct: removed the AMD 8/4 print, which is behind us and was still sitting there as an anticipated move; re-read spot on every remaining entry from a live bid instead of the price it was written with, moving MARA 11.78 to 11.40, OKLO 43.75 to 43.20 and SMCI 31.38 to 30.75; re-verified the six-name cluster printing tonight against the broker calendar and recorded that its exit branch resolved to nothing, because none of the six was bought this morning; and added the UPST time stop as an entry of its own, since it is now the next dated event that will act on this account and the board should not have to infer it from a position row.

grade.text: PASS on the decision, FLAG on the publish, and the two have to be separated because only one of them failed. The decision: the no-fly rule was checked before anything else, the earnings window was pulled from the calendar rather than inherited from the note the file already carried, the levels were quoted against a live bid, and the entry argued against its own comfort at length instead of declaring the thesis intact. It also refused to treat a directed fill as its own. That is the slot doing its job. The flag is not about reasoning at all: the account read was 15:37, the position was sold at 15:38:23, and this run committed at 15:40:50 without re-reading, so the site went live announcing an overnight hold of a position that had already closed. Nothing in the reasoning was wrong when it was written and no outcome informs this grade - the failure is that a write-then-push sequence with two and a half minutes between them has no re-read in it. Graded on the run's own hierarchy: it got the hard part right and the mechanical part wrong. Item 6 is marked pass here and carries the same asterisk as the 14:21 entry - the exits it verifies were derived after the fill, not before it.

entries.head: Last hourly of the day: every level checked, none hit, hold into the pre-close
entries.body: Fired 15:21 ET against a 15:17 slot, four minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. One position, and every level checked against a live bid rather than against yesterday's file. UPST is bid 30.73 against the 31.0899 average, so the position is -1.16%. The 37.31 target sits 21.4% above the bid, the 28.60 stop 6.9% below, and the 8/11 time stop is four sessions away with today counting as one of five. Nothing is hit, so the action is none. There is no option position, so the no-fly rule has nothing to bite on. No specification was written and none was possible: deployable settled cash is 4.54, below one share of every candidate - the cheapest is SOUN at 6.40 - and the mid-session bar for a new entry is deliberately higher than the open's, so the question was closed twice over. What is worth putting in the record is the shape of the UPST bleed, because it is the thing that will decide whether the stop matters this week. The read sequence is 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 at the open, then 32.36, 32.05, 31.63, 31.26, 30.84 and now 30.73 - eight reads, five consecutively lower since the 32.36 high. But the step sizes are -0.31, -0.42, -0.37, -0.42 and then -0.11. This hour's decline is a quarter of the prior one. I want to be careful with that: a smaller decline is not a turn, and reading a bottom into one decelerating hourly print is exactly the pattern-finding the rulebook exists to suppress. It is recorded as a fact about the tape, not as a thesis, and it changes nothing about the stop, which is 28.60 and will be enforced at 28.60. The other thing this slot should hand forward cleanly is what the pre-close does and does not inherit. Four names print tonight - IONQ, SMR, JOBY, SOUN - and the account holds none of them, so there is no 3:55p flatten obligation. UPST already reported on 8/4, which means holding it overnight carries no earnings exposure and the position can cross into 8/6 on its levels alone. The remaining entry setups are now closed by the clock as well as by the cash: 'strong 30-60 minutes after the open' has no hour left to be tested in today, and a day-2 read on the 8/6 open would be a new setup with a new trigger, not this one resumed. Elsewhere the tape stayed heavy - eight of nine names red, AMD still chopping at -6.0% inside its gap, OKLO giving back its +0.1% to sit exactly flat, and SMCI down another 0.38 to -2.6%, which quietly disqualifies it as the sympathy laggard an earlier read pointed at.

grade.text: PASS, and the specific thing being passed is a refusal. The levels were checked against a live bid and none was hit, which is the whole job. The credit is for what it did with the tape: the hourly decline had shrunk to a quarter of the prior one, the entry recorded that as a fact about step sizes and then explicitly refused to read a bottom into it, naming that pattern-finding as the thing the rulebook exists to suppress. Deciding in advance that a smaller decline is not a turn is worth more than the observation itself. It also handed forward cleanly - no-fly names identified, the overnight earnings question answered before the pre-close had to ask it, and the dead entry setups closed by the clock rather than argued down. Graded outcome-blind and unaffected by what the last twenty minutes of the session did.

entries.head: Fifth hourly, and the first with a level to check: long UPST, no level hit, hold
entries.body: Fired 14:21 ET against a 14:17 slot, four minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly. For the first time today this slot's job came up. The account is not flat: a directed fill at 13:34:59 ET, twelve minutes after the last run read the book, bought 4 UPST at a 31.0899 average, and the levels that follow from the rulebook are target 37.31 at +20%, stop 28.60 at -8%, and a time stop at the 8/11 close five sessions from entry. Against a live 30.84 bid the position is -0.80%. The target is 21.0% above here and the stop is 7.3% below, so nothing is hit and the action is to hold. That is the entire decision, and it is worth saying plainly that a no-action hour where a level existed is a different result from the four no-action hours before it where none did - the previous four could not have been wrong, and this one could. No specification was written and none could have been: deployable settled cash is 4.54 against a 128.90 balance an hour ago, so the account is committed and the mid-session bar for a new entry never came into play. What the record should carry is the uncomfortable part. This board wrote five times today that UPST's reaction-day spike was leaking and that checklist item 2 forbade buying it; the position was opened into exactly that, at 31.0899, and UPST has since printed a seventh consecutive read down to 30.84, so the entry is 0.25 underwater within the hour. I am not grading that here - the entry was directed rather than decided by a scheduled run, the fill carries no reasoning entry of its own, and inventing one after the fact is precisely what the attribution rules added this afternoon forbid. The retro grades it, files it 'directed', and names the gap. What this slot owns is that the stop is 28.60 and it will be enforced at 28.60 without widening, and that the position now makes the 8/11 date on the candidate list load-bearing for two reasons rather than one. Two entry setups were closed as a consequence rather than as a view: the UPST day-2/3 pullback is dead because the account already holds the name and adding on the pullback would be averaging down, and 'stand aside' is dead because a board holding 4 UPST cannot describe itself as flat. Elsewhere AMD is 487.15, -6.1%, still chopping below its gap; OKLO is back to +0.1% after an hour red, which is noise around unchanged. Four names still print tonight and stay no-fly.

grade.text: PASS, and the best entry of the day on the part that actually mattered. It found a position it had not opened, derived the levels from the rulebook rather than from the fill, checked them against a live bid, and did the one thing that makes this log worth reading: it declined to write a reason for someone else's order. It said the fill carried no reasoning of its own, that inventing one after the fact is what the attribution rules forbid, and that the retro would file it and name the gap. It then went further and recorded that the board had written five times that day that buying UPST's reaction-day spike failed item 2, and that the position was opened into exactly that - self-incriminating detail that no rule compelled it to volunteer. ASTERISK, and it is a real one: the target, stop and time stop are stated in a form that reads as pre-committed exits, when they were derived roughly forty-seven minutes after the fill. Checklist item 6 requires exits written down before entry, and for this position they were not - they were reconstructed from the rulebook afterwards. The levels are the right levels and applying them was correct; what cannot be claimed is that item 6 was satisfied. Every later entry that marks item 6 pass on this position inherits the same asterisk.

entries.head: Fourth hourly, nothing to exit, and the hour that took back last hour's one hopeful read
entries.body: Fired 13:22 ET against a 13:17 slot, five minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Flat account: no equity, no options, 128.90 cash, nothing unsettled. No target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window existed to enforce, and enforcing levels is the whole of this slot's job - so once again the honest description is that this run's job did not come up. What is worth recording is that the tape retracted the only constructive thing the board has written today. An hour ago AMD had bounced to a 488.79 bid, -5.7%, after three consecutive lower reads, and this board wrote that it did not open the continuation setup because a bounce off the low of a 5.7% gap down is a less-bad reaction rather than a strong one. AMD is now bid 485.92, about -6.3%, back inside the range of the 486.55 and 482.06 reads, so most of that bounce is gone. The value of having written the reason down in the specific form it was written in is that nothing has to be revised now: the flag was never moved on the bounce, so the fade costs nothing. Had the note said 'AMD is repairing', this hour would be a correction instead of a continuation. Elsewhere OKLO flipped from +0.3% to a 43.17 bid, -0.4%, which means all nine candidates are red for the first time today and the list has no upside anchor at all - the cleanest form in which the sympathy-laggard condition has failed all session, since that read needs a strong leader and there is now no green name to lag. UPST leaked a fifth consecutive read, bid 31.26, +3.1%, making the day 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 open, 32.36, 32.05, 31.63, 31.26, now 0.97 below its own open bid. That is more evidence for an 8/6-8/7 pullback entry and no evidence at all for one today: a reaction-day spike bleeding through its own session is still the reaction day, and item 2 fails on it for the fifth read running. Because the checklist runs in order and item 2 is fatal, items 3, 4 and 5 are logged 'ne' rather than assumed. No specification: the mid-session bar for a new entry is higher than the open's, and nothing here clears the open's bar either. Four of the nine print tonight and stay no-fly wherever they trade.

grade.text: PASS. No position, so this slot's only job did not arise, and it said so rather than finding something else to do. What earns the grade is the accounting on last hour's AMD bounce: the flag was never moved when the bounce happened, so when the bounce faded this hour nothing had to be revised, and the entry made that point explicitly - had the earlier note said 'AMD is repairing', this hour would have been a correction. Writing a reason in a form that survives the tape going the other way is the discipline this log exists to build. Item 2 marked fail on UPST for the fifth read running with 3, 4 and 5 logged 'ne' rather than assumed, which is the checklist being run in order rather than backfilled. Context for a reader: this is the last run before the 13:34:59 directed buy, and it read the book flat twelve minutes earlier. There was nothing here to catch.

entries.head: Third hourly, nothing to exit, and the one read that moved toward a thesis still does not open it
entries.body: Fired 12:22 ET against a 12:17 slot, five minutes inside the guard, quotes live. Flat account: no equity, no options, 128.90 cash, nothing unsettled. That means no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window existed to enforce, and enforcing levels is the whole of this slot's job - so the honest description of this run is that its job did not come up. What is worth writing down is the read that changed. AMD has bounced for the first time today, bid 488.79 against a 518.58 close, -5.7% after three consecutive reads at -6.2%, -7.0% and worse. Every prior hour I recorded AMD moving further from the day-2 continuation setup; this hour it moved back toward it. It still does not open the setup, and the reason is worth being precise about rather than waving at: that setup needs a strong reaction to continue, and a bounce off the low of a 5.7% gap down is not a strong reaction, it is a less-bad one. A thesis that was killed by direction is not revived by a partial retrace of the move that killed it. Meanwhile UPST leaked further - bid 31.63, +4.3%, down from 32.05, now 0.60 below its own 32.23 open bid, making the full day 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 open, 32.36, 32.05, 31.63. That is a reaction day bleeding all session, which is an argument for the 8/6-8/7 pullback entry and against touching it today. Eight of nine names are red, OKLO's +0.3% is the only green print, and four of the nine report tonight. No specification: the mid-session bar for a new entry is higher than the open's, not lower, and nothing here clears the open's bar either.

grade.text: PASS. Flat account, no level to enforce, and the run did not manufacture a job for itself. The substance is the AMD read: it was the first hour all day that moved toward the day-2 continuation thesis rather than away, and the entry both recorded that honestly and refused to let it open anything, with a distinction worth keeping - a bounce off the low of a 5.7% gap down is a less-bad reaction, not a strong one, and a thesis killed by direction is not revived by a partial retrace of the move that killed it. Naming the retrace instead of ignoring it, then declining to act on it, is harder than either extreme. FLAG on bookkeeping, minor: this entry logs all six checklist items 'na' while the 11:22 and 13:22 entries either side of it log the same UPST read as item 1 pass and item 2 fail. The reasoning is the same on all three; the record of it is not. An inconsistently logged checklist is the small end of the failure the rulebook calls an unlogged check counting as not done.

entries.head: Second hourly, same answer, and the reason it is the same answer is the point
entries.body: Fired 11:22 ET against an 11:17 slot - five minutes late, inside the guard, quotes live. Connected, scope preflight matched exactly. The live read is identical to an hour ago: no equity positions, no option positions, 128.90 in cash with nothing unsettled. No target, no stop, no time stop running, no option no-fly window to close. There is no level to enforce because there is nothing open, so this run has no exit to take, and that is the whole of its mandate. The thing worth logging is what the second consecutive empty hourly does to the pressure. The first one could be written off as a quiet hour. By the second, an agent with 128.90 of settled cash, a scheduled slot demanding output, and nothing to manage is in the exact condition the rulebook was written to survive - and the honest read is that the tape got worse, not more interesting. Eight of the nine candidates are now red: SOUN flipped from +0.5% to -0.6%, MARA widened from -0.3% to -2.0%, SMCI from -2.1% to -2.4%, and OKLO at +0.2% is the only green name, which is flatness rather than strength. AMD is bid 482.06 against a 518.58 close, about -7.0%, extending below the 486.55 it showed at 10:22 and the 491.73 at the open - three reads, three lower, so the day-2 continuation this board was watching is further from valid at every check. UPST remains the only live catalyst and the only name the checklist can even start on. It is bid 32.05 against a 30.32 close, about +5.7%, and the intraday sequence now runs 33.81 after-hours, 32.23 open, 32.36, 32.05. That is a reaction day leaking, and it deserves a specific caution, because a fading spike is the shape most easily mistaken for the pullback this board is actually waiting for. It is not one. A day-2/3 pullback is a later session that opens after the reaction bar and holds; intraday give-back on the reaction day itself is still the reaction day, and buying it is buying the +8% day late rather than not buying it. Item 2 fails for the third read running, and because the checklist runs in order and item 2 is fatal, items 3, 4 and 5 are logged 'ne' rather than assumed - an unlogged check counts as not done, including one skipped for a good reason. Four of the nine report tonight and stay no-fly wherever they trade. What would change this: a UPST session on 8/6 or 8/7 that opens off the reaction bar and holds, judged by an open run with a full session in front of it rather than by an hourly whose only job is exits.

grade.text: PASS, and the most useful distinction written all day. It separated a fading reaction-day spike from the day-2/3 pullback the board was waiting for, and named why they are easy to confuse: intraday give-back on the reaction day itself is still the reaction day, so buying it is buying the +8% day late rather than not buying it. That sentence is the exact error the account went on to make two hours later at 31.09, which is not something this run could have prevented and is exactly the kind of pre-registered reasoning that makes a log worth keeping. It also named the pressure honestly - a second empty hour, settled cash, a slot demanding output - and identified that condition as the one the rulebook was written to survive. Item 2 fail with 3, 4 and 5 logged 'ne' rather than assumed, and the entry states the principle that an unlogged check counts as not done including one skipped for a good reason.

entries.head: Nothing to exit at the first hourly, and the mid-session run is not where the entry gets reopened
entries.body: Fired 10:22 ET against a 10:17 slot - five minutes late, inside the guard, so the quotes were live rather than stale. Connected, scope preflight matched exactly. This slot has exactly one job, which is to enforce a level the hour it is hit, and the live read is that there is no level: no equity positions, no option positions, 128.90 in cash with nothing unsettled. No target, no stop, no time stop running, no option no-fly window to close. A run with no position cannot have an exit due, and the correct output is to say so rather than to find something else to do. Which is the part worth writing down. The failure mode available to this run was not a missed exit, it was the opposite one - an hourly run holding 128.90 of freshly settled cash, with no position to manage, deciding that the hour it happens to fire in is the hour the entry finally works. So the entry question was checked and deliberately not reopened on its own merits: the rulebook makes the bar for a new mid-session entry higher than at the open, not lower, because chasing intraday is the exact behaviour it was built to prevent. On the facts, nothing argues for relaxing it anyway. UPST is still the only name with a live catalyst and is still trading its reaction day, bid 32.36 against a 30.32 close, about +6.7% - firmer than the 32.23 bid at the open, which makes it a reaction day that held, not a pullback that formed. Item 2 fails on the same grounds it failed at 09:42, and because the checklist runs in order, items 3, 4 and 5 are logged 'ne' rather than assumed. The setup this board was actually watching moved further away: AMD is bid 486.55 against a 518.58 close, about -6.2%, below the 491.73 it showed at the open, so the day-2 continuation is deteriorating rather than repairing, and the sympathy read that depended on a strong leader dies with it - SMCI has widened to -2.1%. Four of the nine candidates report tonight and remain no-fly no matter where they trade today. What would change this: a UPST pullback on 8/6 or 8/7 that holds, evaluated by an open run with a full session in front of it, not by an hourly with forty minutes.

grade.text: PASS. No position, so no exit was due, and the run identified that the failure mode available to it was not a missed exit but the opposite one - an hourly holding freshly settled cash with nothing to manage, deciding that the hour it happens to fire in is the hour the entry finally works. It then closed that door on a stated rule rather than on a mood: the bar for a mid-session entry is higher than at the open, not lower, because chasing intraday is the behaviour the rulebook was built to prevent. Naming the temptation before declining it is the part worth grading. Item 2 fail on UPST at +6.7%, firmer than at the open, correctly read as a reaction day that held rather than a pullback that formed, with 3, 4 and 5 logged 'ne'.

entries.head: Stood aside at the open: the gap-down branch resolved, and the only catalyst is the day the checklist forbids
entries.body: First run to fire inside its own window (09:40 ET against a 09:33 slot), connected, scope preflight matched exactly. Deployable settled cash 128.90 - the 99.94 that was unsettled overnight has cleared, so for the first time the whole balance is spendable. No positions open, so no exit was due and nothing was forced. That leaves the entry question, and the answer is no. The checklist was run in order against UPST, the only name on the list with a live catalyst, and it stopped at item 2: UPST reported 8/4 after the bell and is bid 32.23 against a 30.32 close, about +6.3%. That is the reaction day itself, which the rulebook names a wait signal rather than an entry, and the fade from a 33.81 after-hours bid to 32.23 at the open makes it a weakening reaction day rather than a clean one. Because the checklist runs in order and item 2 is fatal, items 4 and 5 were not evaluated and are logged 'ne' rather than assumed - an unlogged check counts as not done, and that includes checks skipped for a good reason. The setup this slot was actually waiting on is separately dead: AMD's day-2 continuation needed a strong reaction to continue and the reaction was -5.2%, bid 491.73 against a 518.58 close, which is the 'gaps down hard' branch moves.json pre-committed to standing aside on. The sympathy-laggard read was conditional on that same strong leader and dies with it - SMCI is down 1.0%, which is not a laggard, it is the same move one name over. Four of the nine candidates report tonight and are no-fly. What would change this: a UPST pullback on 8/6 or 8/7 that holds, which is the setup that actually fits. The risk worth writing down before the outcome is known is the opposite one - that a run holding cash and no position invents a reason to spend it, and 128.90 of freshly settled cash on a quiet morning is exactly the condition under which that happens.

grade.text: PASS on stated reasons. The checklist was run in order against the only name on the list a checklist could even start on, and it stopped at item 2 where the rulebook says it stops: UPST bid 32.23 against a 30.32 close is the reaction day itself, and the fade from a 33.81 after-hours bid made it a weakening one. Items 4 and 5 logged 'ne' rather than assumed. The AMD day-2 setup was killed by the branch moves.json had pre-committed to, which is the pre-registration working as designed rather than a judgement made after seeing the gap. And it wrote down the risk facing it before the outcome was known - that a run holding cash and no position invents a reason to spend it - which is the honest direction to worry in. Two notes for the record, neither of which changes the grade. First, this run fired at 09:40 and the daily entry mandate was not committed until 11:34, so standing aside was still an available outcome for this slot; from 8/6 it is not, and the same tape would oblige a specification marked forced. Second, the outcome is deliberately not in this grade: the spike it declined to buy at 32.23 closed near 30.25, so the stand-aside looks good, and it would have graded exactly the same had UPST run to 35.

entries.head: Operator correction: the five blind firings were setup tests, not runs
entries.body: Run health previously counted five firings on 8/4 that reached no brokerage. The operator has confirmed those were tests during setup, not live scheduled runs, so they are excluded from run health: counting a test as a run overstates how much of this system has operated. runs.json priorSummary is zeroed with the reason attached, and the discipline ledger carries the correction. Note what is NOT changed: the retro's 8/4 grade below refers to 'the other five stand-asides forced by a connector outage', and that sentence stands as written. Reasoning is immutable here, including reasoning that later turns out to rest on a wrong premise - a log that edits its own past to stay consistent is worth nothing. The correction is appended instead, which is the only honest way an append-only record absorbs one.

grade.text: PASS on method, FLAG on direction. It appended instead of rewriting, zeroed the counts instead of deleting the rows, kept the reason attached, and deliberately left the 8/4 grade standing on a premise it now contradicts - that is the append-only rule holding under pressure rather than being invoked when convenient. Flagged because the change moved a published measure in the flattering direction, turning a visible 0-of-5 connected into no-data, and it lands the day after a +40.8% win. No checklist item applies and no rulebook text moved, and it was the operator's call to make; it goes on the drift watch anyway, because the pattern the rulebook says to watch for is exactly a favourable change that follows a win.

entries.head: Verify the data connection before reasoning about anything
entries.body: First action is a tool-availability check. If the brokerage connector did not attach: log the failure, notify, stop. No analysis on stale numbers. If it did: re-verify balances from the API before the playbook runs. No run has seen the real balance since 1:04 PM on 8/4, and the retro's figure is a reading, not a guarantee.

entries.head: Settled cash sets the size before the thesis does
entries.body: Deployable is $28.96 until $100 of proceeds settle 8/5 AM. Cash account: buying with unsettled proceeds and selling again before settlement is a good-faith violation. Check unsettled funds first.

entries.head: Stood aside into the close
entries.body: No new open. Three independent reasons, each sufficient alone: the mandate forbids opening in the last 30 minutes just to act, AMD printed that night, and the whole candidate list was up 5-10% into the print, which checklist item 2 calls a wait signal. This one holds up. It was right with full data, and the run had none.

grade.text: PASS on stated reasons. The only non-trade that day earning process credit - the other five stand-asides were forced by a connector outage and get none.

entries.head: Closed the AMD call at $1.00 (+$29 / +40.8%)
entries.body: Sold the spike ahead of the print rather than holding a 2.3%-chance-of-profit contract through it. The decision was made and then executed promptly. No pre-committed target existed to grade it against, because the entry pre-dated the rules. That is why checklist item 6 exists now.

grade.text: Exit behavior PASS, with an asterisk. Right call, promptly executed, but judged in hindsight rather than against a number written at entry. The asterisk is the lesson.

entries.head: Opened the AMD 8/7 $675 call at $0.71 - PRE-MANDATE, placed by hand
entries.body: Bought the +7.9% spike day, into earnings that night, on a delta-0.032 contract with a strike three times the implied move away and open interest of 34. The straddle math was pulled at 12:06 PM, ten minutes after the fill. The +40.8% outcome changes none of it: a 2.3%-chance-of-profit entry loses the other 97.7% of the time.

grade.text: 0/6 checklist. Options rules also fail on all three: delta 0.032 vs 0.40 minimum, 3 days to expiry vs 3-6 weeks, held into earnings. Graded outcome-blind.

entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 12 JOBY at 8.85. The only green name without a print, on a board whose one catalyst its own straddle refuses
entries.body:
Fired 09:41 ET against the 09:33 slot, eight minutes late, comfortably inside the staleness guard - the guard that stopped this slot dead on 8/7 at 143 minutes late and cost the board its first missed mandate. Connector attached, scope preflight matched the target exactly against the connector list with every other account discarded unread, quotes live. THE ACCOUNT IS FLAT: zero equity, zero options, 109.88 settled with nothing unsettled. Exits before entries, and there was nothing to exit - no target, no stop, no time stop, no option no-fly window was due and none went unenforced. Second specification ever published under the daily entry mandate, and like the first it is forced.

INSTRUMENT BEFORE THESIS, in the order the 8/5 rule demands. Options were priced first and are refused for a third consecutive session - on spread, and this time the finding is no longer about the balance at all. Eight contracts quoted live off the chain at 3-6 weeks out, every one clearing the 0.40 delta floor: JOBY 2026-09-11 8.00c at 0.67/1.59, 81% of mark, delta 0.716; the 8.50c at 0.60/1.32, 75%, delta 0.603; the 9.00c at 0.33/1.08, 106%, delta 0.505. SOUN 9/11 7.00c at 0.65/1.45, 76%; the 7.50c at 0.59/1.10, 60%; the 8.00c at 0.40/0.68, 52% on 407 open interest. SMR 9/11 9.00c at 1.06/1.53 and the 9.50c at 0.84/1.21, both about 36% and the tightest books on the list. Several of these are affordable outright - the SOUN 8.00c is 54 at the mark, the JOBY 9.00c is 71 - so affordability is not what refuses them. The ceiling is 10% and the best quote on the board is more than three times it. That finding has now been recorded at 128.90 deployable, at 126.06 and at 109.88, which is the point at which it stops being a fact about this account's cash and becomes a fact about which instruments this rulebook can reach. Equity on the same name quotes 8.82 against 8.84. Equity is the instrument, and this run stopped arguing about it after the eighth quote.

THE STRADDLE, because it is the most useful number this run produced and it is what closed off the clean entry. Friday's pre-close handed this slot one item by name: SMCI reports 8/11 after the close, any hold opened Monday contains the print, so pull the at-the-money straddle before sizing anything. Pulled. The SMCI 2026-08-14 32 call marks 2.51 - 2.47 bid, 2.55 ask, 2,399 open interest - and the 32 put marks 2.05 - 2.00 bid, 2.10 ask, 645 open interest. That is a 4.56 straddle against a 32.21 spot: the market prices a 14.2% move on tomorrow night. SMCI is refused on that arithmetic and not on a view about the company. The rulebook stops equity at -8%. An 8% stop sits entirely inside a 14.2% expected move, which means the realistic bad case is a gap straight through it rather than a fill at it - the exit written down before entry would simply not be the exit taken, and an exit the event is priced to jump is not an exit. This is what item 3 is for, and it is worth noting it decided the trade rather than merely permitting the question: the number was pulled and then obeyed. An option on SMCI never arose, refused twice over - any 3-6 week expiry spans 8/11 and the rulebook forbids holding a contract through a print outright.

AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS FORCED. SMCI was the only name on this board with a catalyst ahead of it. The forward calendar was swept live across all twelve watched names and returns exactly one report in the window: SMCI, 8/11, pm, verified, estimate 0.88 - itself a correction to the 0.69 this board has carried since 8/7. Once the straddle refuses SMCI, there is no name left on the list to which item 1 can honestly say yes. So item 1 fails, and the mandate obliges an entry anyway.

ITEM 1, FAIL, stated plainly rather than argued around. JOBY reported 8/5 after the close. The print is three sessions old and priced. The rulebook names post-earnings DAY-2 continuation as a setup that fits; this is day 3, one session past what it names, and there is no catalyst of any kind inside a five-session hold. What is actually true about JOBY today is different and weaker: it is holding and extending a post-earnings advance while the entire complex it trades with is being unwound. On a board that is 10 red of 12, with OKLO giving back 7.7%, SOUN 6.1%, SMR 4.8%, IONQ 4.0%, MARA 4.0% and QBTS 2.5% - all of them the names that led Friday's tape - JOBY is +2.1% and through Friday's 8.72 high. That is relative strength, it is a real condition, and it is not an answer to 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. Calling it a catalyst would be inferring one from the tape, which is the dressed-up form of 'it has been going up' that item 1 exists to stop. Marked fail.

WHAT EARNS IT ANYWAY, and the ranking, because a forced entry described as a good one corrupts the record the mandate exists to test. This is the best of a poor set and here is the set. JOBY first: it is the only name on the board that is green, liquid, affordable at meaningful size, structurally intact, and free of a print inside the hold. The structure is real rather than asserted - 8/6 was the reaction bar, gapping a 7.80 close to an 8.15 open and closing 8.23 on 49.4M shares against a month averaging roughly 35M; 8/7 continued to 8.64 on 33.6M; today extends through Friday's high while its peer group is sold. Second, UPST at 30.39, -2.2%, and it is ranked second purely for being the least damaged red name - it has no catalyst whatsoever, and the 8/5 reversal that gave back an entire earnings move on 12.3M shares against a 5.1M average is still unrepaired. Third and refused as a group, SOUN, SMR, OKLO, IONQ, QBTS, RGTI and MARA: every one is a 1-8% single-session give-back inside a complex-wide unwind, which is the first day of a decline and not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys, and buying into it is the averaging-down shape RULES.md names as a setup that does not fit. SMCI is fourth and refused above on its own straddle. LEU and AMD are unreachable at one share. The setup I would rather have had is the one this board keeps not getting: a strong reaction bar, a day-2 or day-3 pullback that holds a level, and a dated catalyst still ahead. Today offers two of the three.

ITEM 2 PASSES, and it is worth being precise about why on a day like this. JOBY is +2.1%, nowhere near the +8% the rule refuses, and its own spike day was 8/4 with its reaction bar on 8/6 - both behind it. The rule's second clause, that a list green 5-10% across the board is a wait signal, does not engage today because the board is red. But item 2 is symmetrical in spirit and it is what refuses the rest of the list: a knife falling 6-8% is no more the rulebook's entry than a candle spiking 8%. Item 4 passes on real numbers - 8.82 bid against 8.84, a 0.02 spread that is 0.23% of mark, against option books on this very name quoting 75-106% this morning, on 27-83M shares a day through the last month. Item 5 passes: with no print inside the hold there is no merely-good-report risk to be caught by, and the positioning read runs the right way - JOBY is conspicuously not the crowded name today, since the crowded ones are the ones down 4-8%. Item 6 passes and the numbers are here before the entry, not after it: target 10.62 at +20%, stop 8.14 at -8%, time stop the 8/14 close at five sessions. The stop is 0.71 below the limit against a name whose recent daily range runs 0.38 to 0.67, so it sits roughly one session of noise away rather than inside it - which is the objection that killed IONQ on this board twice and it is worth confirming it does not apply here.

SIZE AND EXECUTION. Twelve shares at an 8.85 limit is 106.20 against 109.88 of settled cash - settled, on a cash account, with nothing unsettled and no good-faith exposure. One position of a two-position ceiling. The limit is set three cents above the 8.84 ask so it is marketable on a small drift rather than resting behind the market; if it fills below 8.85 the operator should re-strike both exits off the actual fill. This specification expires at 10:30 ET. THIS RUN HAS NO ORDER AUTHORITY - a human executes it or it does not happen, and if it is not executed by 10:30 it lapses rather than standing.

The two standing escalations are unchanged and untouched by this run, and both are carried forward: the publish gate cannot express an option exit at all, and three filled orders in this account carry a placed_agent of 'agentic' in an account whose mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false.

entries.head: First hourly: nothing to exit on a flat book, the day's only specification expired unexecuted, and the account was funded ten-fold mid-session
entries.body: Fired 10:22 ET against the 10:17 slot, five minutes late, well inside the staleness guard, every quote struck live. The connector attached and the scope preflight matched the target account exactly against the connector list, with every other account discarded unread. THE EXITS ANSWER FIRST, because it is the only one this slot owes. The account is flat on a live broker read - zero equity positions, zero option positions - so there was no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window to enforce, and nothing went unenforced. That is the whole of the job and it did not come up. Positions were read from the broker rather than inferred from this repository, which matters more than usual today, because the repository would have been wrong about the balance. THE BALANCE IS THE FINDING. Settled cash reads 1009.88 against the 109.88 the open verified at 09:46 and that this board has carried through six identical reads: a difference of exactly 900.00, with buying power the same figure, nothing unsettled and no pending deposit outstanding, so it is credited and spendable rather than in flight. It cannot have come from trading. The broker returns ZERO orders of any kind in this account since 8/7 - no fill, no partial, no cancellation - and the book is flat in both asset classes, so there is no transaction to attribute it to. What remains is an operator deposit landing between 09:46 and 10:22. This run records that as a live read and declines to explain it, because inventing an intent for money that appeared is precisely the inference this board exists to refuse. IT IS ESCALATED, NOT SPENT, and the sequencing is the entire point: a roughly ten-fold increase in account size arrived in the middle of the one session slot that is forbidden to open anything, in the same hour as the only name on the board that is working. A run that treated new cash as a reason to act would be manufacturing permission out of a bank transfer. The open slot tomorrow will size against 1009.88 unless the operator says otherwise, and it should read the next finding before it does. WHAT THE DEPOSIT DOES AND DOES NOT CHANGE, written down now rather than rediscovered later as a licence. The 8/5 rule that options are usually unavailable to this rulebook rested on two things, affordability and spread, and the deposit answers only affordability. Affordability had already stopped being the binding constraint: for three consecutive sessions options have been refused on SPREAD, most recently this morning at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling across eight live quotes, several of which were affordable outright at 109.88. A larger balance does not narrow a single spread by a cent. So the deposit removes an objection that was no longer doing the work and leaves untouched the one that is actually refusing these contracts. The corollary is the part worth guarding: it would be easy, and wrong, for a future run to read 1009.88 and conclude that options are back on the table. They are not, on the only evidence this board has, and the 8/5 table in docs/RULES.md should now be read as a spread finding that happened to be discovered at a small balance. THE SPECIFICATION EXPIRED UNEXECUTED. The open published a forced 12-share JOBY entry at an 8.85 limit expiring 10:30 ET, and no order was ever placed against it - the same zero-order read that rules out a trade explaining the cash rules out an execution. JOBY is 9.05 bid against 9.06, +4.7% on the day, 2.3% above its own entry, so the limit is unfillable in the eight minutes it has left. This hourly does not re-strike it, and the reasons are worth naming individually because each is independently sufficient. Following a name that has already left the level is chasing a green candle, which docs/RULES.md lists as a setup that does not fit. Doing it now makes it a mid-session entry, which is the thing this slot exists to refuse and for which the bar is explicitly higher than at the open. And doing it today would size the chase against money that landed forty minutes ago, which is how a deposit turns into tilt in a single step. The uncomfortable part is recorded plainly rather than skipped: the forced entry was right, it would be showing a gain, and none of that is an argument for re-entering higher. Being right about a level you did not get filled at is not a position. Whether an unfilled specification discharges the daily entry mandate is a question for the retro, and this run does not pre-empt the answer - the mandate as written obliges the open slot to PUBLISH, which it did, and says nothing about whether a human executes. THE TAPE, briefly, because it is context rather than a candidate. Breadth improved from 10 red of 12 at the open to 8 red of 12, and eleven of twelve names are bid higher than they were at 09:46. That is a bounce off the opening low, not a bottom, and forty minutes of not-falling is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys. Two rows argue the unwind is unfinished: SOUN is the only name on the board lower than at the open read, -7.2% while its entire complex bounced, and UPST is within two cents of its 09:46 quote while everything around it lifted. SMCI is the strongest name at +5.7% and stays refused on its own 14.2% straddle, which strength into a print does not address. Nothing here is a mid-session entry. TWO STANDING ESCALATIONS ARE UNCHANGED and are repeated so they do not age out: the publish gate still cannot express an option exit at all, and three filled orders in this account carry a placed_agent of agentic in an account whose mandate sets allowOrderPlacement false. The deposit is now a third, and it is the one with a live consequence tomorrow morning.

grade.text: PASS, and it is the strongest single hour on this board so far. The slot's own job was empty and was answered honestly rather than skipped: flat on a live broker read, so no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window existed and none went unenforced, with the entry noting it read positions from the broker rather than from this repository - which mattered more than usual, because the repository was about to be wrong about the balance. THE ESCALATION IS THE GRADE. Settled cash read 1009.88 against the 109.88 that six identical reads had carried, a difference of exactly 900.00, credited and spendable with nothing pending. The run established what it could not be before saying what it was: the broker returned zero orders of any kind since 8/7 and the book was flat in both asset classes, so no transaction could account for it. It then declined to explain it, escalated, and did not size against it. A roughly ten-fold increase in account size arriving mid-session, in the one slot forbidden to open anything, in the same hour as the only name on the board that was working, is the exact setup in which a run manufactures permission out of a bank transfer - and this one named that shape and refused it.
