The operator answered the same morning that it was a deposit and that the escalation was right, but the grade does not rest on that: the reasoning was correct before the answer arrived and would have been correct had the answer never come. THE SECOND HALF IS BETTER THAN THE FIRST. It ring-fenced what the deposit does and does not license, in advance of anyone needing it: the 8/5 option finding had two halves, affordability and spread; the deposit answers only affordability; and affordability had already stopped being the binding constraint, three sessions of refusals having turned on spread, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling on contracts affordable outright. 'No balance narrows a spread' is the whole of it, and writing it down before a later run could read a bigger number as an argument is the kind of guarding this log is for. THE EXPIRED SPECIFICATION WAS HANDLED CORRECTLY AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART RECORDED. JOBY was 9.05 bid against the dead 8.85 limit, 2.3% through it, and the entry said plainly that the forced entry was right and would be showing a gain - then gave three independently sufficient reasons not to re-strike: chasing a name that has left the level is a setup the rulebook names as not fitting, doing it here makes it a mid-session entry where the bar is higher by design, and doing it today sizes the chase against money that landed forty minutes earlier. 'Being right about a level you did not get filled at is not a position' is the sentence the remaining six re-marks of the day vindicated. It also referred the question of whether an unfilled specification discharges the daily entry mandate to this retro instead of answering it in its own favour; it is answered in perf.json, and the answer is that publication discharges it.

entries.head: First hour with a position to check: four levels on OKLO, four clear - and the last run's evidence inverted while its conclusion held
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, and that is the whole of what this slot exists to do. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.91 bid, so the position is -0.53%, 0.48 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.6%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.5%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today counting as session one of five. The no-fly window was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 910 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them, so its 8/7 print sits behind this hold rather than inside it, and no option is held for that rule to bite on in any case. Nothing was hit, so nothing was done and no exit specification is owed. A level hit and not acted on is the failure this slot exists to prevent; no level was hit, and the distinction between that and not having looked is the reason every number above was quoted from the bid rather than from the board. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED AND NOT COMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from a balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, placed_agent 'agentic', with no specification from any run in this project behind it. Nothing further has arrived through that channel in the forty-three minutes since. The escalation stands open for the retro. This run enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and does not re-argue how it got there. THE CORRECTION THIS RUN OWES IS TO EVIDENCE, NOT TO A CONCLUSION. At 10:22 breadth had improved from 10 red of 12 to 8 red and that run refused to call it a bottom, saying forty minutes of less-bad is not a session of having stopped. It was right: breadth is 10 red of 12 again, nine of twelve names are bid below their 10:22 quotes, the two marginal greens flipped back - QBTS +0.05% to -1.20%, LEU +0.07% to -0.71% - and the two real ones gave back most of what they held, SMCI +5.7% to +3.7% and JOBY +4.7% to +1.6%. But the two specific tells that run offered have both inverted. SOUN, named as the cleanest evidence the give-back was unfinished precisely because it kept falling while its complex bounced, is 7.53 bid against 7.44 and is one of only three names HIGHER than at 10:22. UPST, named as the other tell for going nowhere while eleven names lifted, is the second at 30.66 against 30.37. IONQ is the third. The call held and the reasons offered for it did not, which is recorded because a read that is right for reasons that stop being true within the hour is a read that got lucky about its reasoning, and this board is worth less if it only writes down the half of that sentence that flatters it. SECOND CORRECTION, TO THIS BOARD'S OWN LEDGER. At 10:22 it wrote that the expired forced JOBY entry would be showing a gain - JOBY was 9.05 bid, 2.3% past the 8.85 limit the open published, and the note said so plainly because the forced arm is measured separately so that inconvenient facts change no rules. JOBY is 8.78 bid now, seven cents BELOW that limit, and the same specification would be showing -0.79%. Both statements were true when written. What the round trip actually demonstrates is the ground the 10:22 refusal stood on rather than an argument against it: a name that runs 2.3% past its level in forty minutes can come back through it in sixty, so re-striking upward would have been the error it looked like a missed opportunity for. Whether an 8.85 limit that never filled counts against the daily mandate at all remains the retro's call and this run does not pre-empt it. NO NEW ENTRY, and it was not close on three independent grounds. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate binds the open slot, not this one. The complex resumed falling after a forty-minute bounce, and day one of a decline is the shape item 2 refuses rather than the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys - the deterioration this hour concentrated in the very complex the account is now long, MARA -2.1% to -4.5%, SMR -3.4% to -4.3%, OKLO -6.7% to -7.3%. And the one name on this board with a forward catalyst prints tomorrow evening against a 14.2% implied move that an 8% stop sits entirely inside, re-confirmed live on the calendar at pm timing, verified, estimate 0.88. Options stay refused on spread for a third consecutive session, which 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow, because no balance narrows a spread. Deployable is 919.58 with nothing unsettled; the book is one name of four, 8.9% of account value at the bid against a 40% single-name ceiling, and one of the two the nuclear complex allows.

grade.text: PASS. Four levels quoted off a live bid and four clear, on the first hour this week with anything to enforce, and the entry draws the distinction that matters: a level hit and not acted on is the failure this slot exists to prevent, and not having looked is a different failure that produces the same clean row. Every number came from the bid rather than from the board, and the no-fly window was re-pulled live at 910 events rather than carried forward. THE PROVENANCE FINDING WAS MADE THE RIGHT WAY, and this retro's own attribution section rests entirely on evidence this run pulled. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from a changed balance, which is what turned an unexplained position into a dated, priced, tagged fact: OKLO, 2 shares at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, filled 10:39:30 ET, placed_agent 'agentic', with no specification from any run in this project behind it. It escalated, and then explicitly declined to re-argue how the position got there while still enforcing its levels. That is the correct split: the slot that owns the levels is not the slot that owns the attribution. TWO SELF-CORRECTIONS, BOTH AGAINST ITSELF. It retracted the 10:22 tells - SOUN and UPST, named an hour earlier as the cleanest evidence the unwind was unfinished, both among the only three names higher - while keeping the conclusion they had been offered for, and stated the distinction rather than blurring it: the call held and the reasons for it did not. And it re-marked the dead JOBY limit from a gain to -0.79%, which is the correction that costs something, since the 10:22 note's most quotable line was that the refused entry would have been green. THE FLAG IS NOT AGAINST THIS RUN and is recorded here because this is the first entry it can attach to. The 54.18 target, the 41.54 stop and the 8/14 time stop this run enforced were struck off a fill this board did not make and were derived after it, so checklist item 6 - exits written down before entry - was never satisfiable for this position by anyone. That is a property of the fill rather than a defect in the enforcement, and the enforcement is what this entry is graded on.

entries.head: Four levels clear on OKLO, and the first hour the board stopped falling is the hour the position made a new low
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, AND A POSITION THAT MADE A NEW LOW FOR THE DAY WHILE THE BOARD AROUND IT STOPPED FALLING. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.27 bid: the position is -1.95%, 1.76 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 22.4%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 6.2%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. No option is held, so no no-fly window can bite, and the calendar was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so no exit specification is owed and none is written. THE STOP IS NOW INSIDE ONE DAY'S RANGE, AND THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ACTED ON. At 11:22 the stop was 7.5% below the bid; it is 6.2% below now, on a name that has already travelled 8.57% today. A stop that sits inside a single session's realised range is a stop an ordinary continuation of the session already in progress reaches. That is a fact about the distance and not a reason to sell at -1.95%: the rulebook exits AT the level, and exiting early because the level looks reachable is a stop moved by nerves in the direction that happens to feel prudent. It is written down in advance so that if 41.54 trades this afternoon nobody has to reconstruct whether it was foreseen. THE FINDING IS A DIVERGENCE, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING TODAY THAT IS ABOUT THE POSITION RATHER THAN ABOUT THE TAPE. Every previous read this session was a story about the whole list moving together: 10 green of 12 into Friday's bell, 10 red at the open, 8 red at 10:22, 10 red again at 11:22. This hour breaks the pattern in the honest direction - breadth improves to 9 red of 12, RGTI flips green at +0.4%, and the board is exactly even hour-on-hour at six names bid higher and six lower, against nine of twelve lower last hour. IONQ, UPST, QBTS and SOUN are all firmer. Against that, OKLO fell 0.64 to 44.27 and is the worst name on this board for a fourth consecutive read. It has now declined to participate in two separate intraday bounces in its own complex. When a name sits out its complex's recoveries twice in one session, the correlation that justifies watching the complex stops covering the name, and what is left is a name-specific problem that the levels will price in their own time rather than a view this slot is entitled to act on early. NO ENTRY, AND IT WAS NOT CLOSE ON FOUR INDEPENDENT GROUNDS. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate attaches to the open slot, which discharged it at 09:41. One flat hour after two falling ones is the least informative moment in a decline at which to decide the decline has ended, and it is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys. The single name with a forward catalyst is refused on a 14.2% implied move against an 8% stop, re-confirmed live on the calendar this hour. And options stay refused on spread for a fourth consecutive session, a refusal that 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow, because no balance narrows a spread. THE JOBY RE-MARK IS NOW A SEQUENCE AND IT IS RECORDED IN FULL BECAUSE THE FIRST ENTRY IN IT WAS THE FLATTERING ONE. The open's forced 12-share entry at an 8.85 limit expired unexecuted at 10:30. At 10:22 this board wrote that it would be showing a gain, JOBY then 9.05 bid. At 11:22 it wrote -0.79% at 8.78. It is 8.67 bid now and the same specification would be -2.03%: three re-marks, each worse than the last. All three were true when written, none is a rule, and together they are the clearest available argument that refusing to chase the name back up through its own level at 10:22 was correct on its own terms rather than lucky. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A THIRD HOUR, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from the balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit with placed_agent 'agentic', and no run in this project published a specification behind it. Nothing new has arrived through that channel in the hundred minutes since. That is the retro's to answer; this slot enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it. state.json re-struck in full on 12:22 bids across all twelve names. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending, and against the 2026-08-10 concentration rule the book is one name of four, 8.8% of account value at the bid against a 40% ceiling, and one of the two the nuclear complex allows.

grade.text: PASS, and the specific credit is for a warning written down in advance and deliberately not acted on. The levels work is clean: four levels off a live bid, four clear, the calendar re-pulled at 934 events with OKLO in none of them, nothing hit, nothing proposed, no exit specification owed. THE STOP-DISTANCE NOTE IS THE ENTRY'S REAL OUTPUT. The 41.54 stop had closed from 7.5% below the bid to 6.2%, on a name that had already travelled 8.57% that session, which puts the stop inside a single session's realised range. The run recorded that, said explicitly that it is a fact about a distance and not a reason to sell at -1.95%, and gave the reason: the rulebook exits AT the level, and exiting early because the level looks reachable is a stop moved by nerves in the direction that happens to feel prudent. It then stated why it was writing it down at all - so that if 41.54 traded that afternoon nobody would have to reconstruct whether it had been foreseen. That is what checklist item 6 is trying to buy, applied by a run to a position whose levels this board never got to set. THE DIVERGENCE READ IS THE WEAKER HALF and it is graded on its own terms rather than on what the next hour did with it. From one hour of improving breadth and one name at a new low, the entry concluded a name-specific problem - that when a name sits out its complex's recoveries twice, the correlation stops covering it. That is a mechanism-free inference from a single hour on a twelve-name list, and the entry's own hedge, that the levels will price it in their own time rather than this slot acting early, is doing more work than the inference is. The run was right not to act on it. It should have been slower to write it up as a finding, and the 13:22 and 15:21 entries reach that conclusion themselves.

entries.head: Four levels on OKLO, four clear - the stop moved further away, and the third hour-scale tell in a row inverted
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, and that is the whole of what this slot exists to do. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.84 bid, so the position is -0.69%, 0.62 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.8%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.4%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today counting as session one of five. The no-fly window was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them, so its 8/7 print sits behind this hold rather than inside it, and no option is held for that rule to bite on in any case. Nothing was hit, so nothing was done and no exit specification is owed. A level hit and not acted on is the failure this slot exists to prevent; no level was hit, and every number above was quoted from the live bid rather than from the board, which is the distinction between that and not having looked. THE WARNING THE LAST RUN ISSUED DID NOT MATERIALISE, AND IT IS RETIRED WITH THE SAME PROMINENCE IT WAS GIVEN. At 12:22 this board recorded, in advance and deliberately, that the 41.54 stop had closed to 6.2% below the bid on a name that had already travelled 8.57% that day, and that an ordinary continuation of the session already in progress reaches it. The session did not continue that way. The bid rose 0.57 to 44.84 and the stop is now 7.4% away - further than an hour ago and further than at 11:22. Both halves of that note survive and they are separate findings. Writing the distance down before the level was reached was right, because it means nobody has to reconstruct this afternoon whether it was foreseen. And refusing to act on it at -1.95% was also right, because the hour that followed moved the other way: selling because a stop looks reachable is a stop moved by nerves in the direction that happens to feel prudent, and this is the cleanest instance the record has yet produced of what that would have cost. The rulebook exits AT the level. It did not trade. THE FINDING IS THAT LAST HOUR DIVERGENCE INVERTED, AND THE PATTERN BEHIND IT IS NOW MORE INTERESTING THAN ANY OF ITS INSTANCES. The 12:22 read was that the board had stopped falling while the position had not - breadth 9 red of 12, six names higher and six lower, OKLO alone at a new low for the day - and it drew from that a name-specific problem, a name that had declined to participate in two of its own complex bounces. Both halves reversed inside sixty minutes. Breadth is 11 RED of 12, the worst read of the day, SMCI the only green name. Ten of the twelve are bid below their 12:22 quotes where the last hour was evenly split. And OKLO is one of only two names that are HIGHER, alongside LEU. The name singled out for falling alone is now rising nearly alone. THAT IS THE THIRD TELL TO INVERT INSIDE AN HOUR TODAY, and three is a pattern rather than three coincidences. At 10:22 this board named SOUN and UPST as the cleanest evidence that the give-back was unfinished; by 11:22 both were among the only three names higher. At 11:22 it recorded the bounce as given back and the complex as resumed-falling; by 12:22 the list was split evenly and firming. At 12:22 it read a divergence between a stabilising board and a falling position; this hour the board is at its worst and the position is recovering. Each read was defensible on the numbers in front of it and each was overturned by the next set of numbers. The conclusion is not that any one of them was careless - it is that hour-scale narrative on a twelve-name correlated board has a demonstrated hit rate near chance, and that the slot generating these reads is fortunately the slot with no entry authority. What this hour changes is that the inversions are now recorded as a class rather than one at a time, which is the form in which the retro can actually act on them. NO ENTRY, and it was not close on four independent grounds. The mid-session bar is higher than the open by design and the daily entry mandate attaches to the open slot, where it was discharged at 09:41. A three-hour decline that paused for one hour and resumed is not the day-2/3 pullback the rulebook buys - and the pause being over is precisely what this hour established. SMCI, the only name on this board with a forward catalyst and now the only green name on it, stays refused on a 14.2% implied move against an 8% stop, re-confirmed live at 8/11 pm, verified, estimate 0.88. Options stay refused on spread for a fourth consecutive session, which 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow. The expired forced JOBY specification was re-marked a fourth time and in the unflattering direction - a gain at 10:22, -0.79%, -2.03%, and -2.49% at 8.63 bid now - monotone across four reads, which is the argument that declining to chase it upward at 10:22 was right on its own terms rather than lucky. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A FOURTH HOUR, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from a balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run in this project behind it, and nothing further has arrived through that channel in the hundred and sixty minutes since. It stands open for the retro. This run enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and does not re-argue how it got there. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending; against the 2026-08-10 concentration rule the book is one name of four, 8.9% of account value at the bid against a 40% ceiling, and one of the two slots the nuclear complex allows.

grade.text: PASS, and the best-reasoned hour of the day. It retired its predecessor's warning with the same prominence the warning was given, and split it correctly into two findings rather than one: writing the distance to the stop down in advance was right, and refusing to act on it at -1.95% was separately right, and the bid then rising 0.57 to widen the stop to 7.4% does not merge them. Most runs would have recorded either a vindication or a retraction. This one recorded that the two halves of a note can settle differently, which is the harder and more useful shape. THE CLASS FINDING IS THE DURABLE ONE. Three consecutive hour-scale character-reads had each been overturned by the next hour - the 10:22 SOUN and UPST tells, the 11:22 resumed-falling call, the 12:22 divergence - and rather than log a third individual retraction, the entry generalised: hour-scale narrative on a twelve-name correlated board has a demonstrated hit rate near chance, and it is fortunate that the slot generating these reads is the slot with no entry authority. That is a conclusion about the process rather than about the tape, it is stated in the form a retro can act on, and it refuses the available consolation by saying each read was defensible on the numbers in front of it rather than careless. THE FLAG IS ABOUT SHAPE. This entry and the three that follow it carry no checklist object at all, where the 10:22, 11:22 and 12:22 entries of the same session each carry one with every item 'na'. Nothing operational turns on it and the gate requires a checklist only where an order specification sits, but four entries dropping a field the same session's earlier entries carry is the record disagreeing with itself about its own shape - and shape drift is how a field stops being filled in before anybody decides it should not be.

entries.head: Four levels clear on OKLO, and the first hour today the board moved as one thing rather than telling a story
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, AND NOTHING PROPOSED. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.80 bid: the position is -0.77%, 0.70 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.9%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.3%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. No option is held, so no no-fly window can bite, and the calendar was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so no exit specification is owed and none is written. THE FINDING IS UNIFORMITY, AND IT IS THE FIRST THING THIS BOARD HAS PRODUCED TODAY THAT THE NEXT HOUR CANNOT INVERT. Eleven of the twelve names are bid lower than at 13:22. That is the broadest hour-over-hour decline of the session - ten of twelve last hour, six at 12:22, nine at 11:22 - and the single exception is UPST, higher by seven cents, which is a flat print rather than a divergence and is not read as one. Breadth on the day is unchanged at 11 red of 12 with SMCI the only green name. THAT TURNS THE TWO-PER-COMPLEX CAP FROM A FORECAST INTO A MEASUREMENT. The 2026-08-10 rule change caps this book at two names per complex on the stated reasoning that four names off this list is not four positions but one position at four times the size, paying four spreads, with a stop that all four gap through together. It was written on Friday's inverted tape as a claim about what this universe does. This hour is the observation rather than the claim: twelve names, one direction, sixty minutes, with the day's worst four - OKLO -7.48%, SOUN -7.23%, MARA -6.74%, SMR -6.11% - spanning nuclear, AI-voice and crypto-mining. Three different stories and one trade. A rule that was argued for is now a rule that has been demonstrated, and that distinction is worth the entry on its own. AND THE RUN OF INVERTED TELLS ENDS BY YIELDING NOTHING TO INVERT. Three consecutive hours each produced a character-read that the next hour contradicted: the 10:22 SOUN and UPST evidence, the 11:22 resumed-falling call, the 12:22 divergence between a firming board and a falling position. This hour there is no such read available, because a list moving as one has no internal structure to narrate. OKLO rejoined the decline it briefly stepped out of - four cents lower, neither leading nor lagging, the first hour today this position has had nothing distinguishing to say about itself - which retires the divergence question in both directions it was argued: as a name-specific problem at 12:22, and as the retraction of that at 13:22. An hour that produces no narrative is the right output for a slot whose job is levels, and it is recorded with the same prominence as the hours that produced one, because a log that only writes up the interesting hours is a log that rewards inventing them. WHAT IS NEW IS THE POSITION'S SIZE, AND IT IS THE FLOOR THAT BINDS RATHER THAN THE CEILING. At 89.60 the position is 8.88% of the 1009.20 account. The 2026-08-10 rule warns rather than blocks below about 10%, on the reasoning that a position that small cannot move the day while costing the same attention as one that can, and the arithmetic here is exactly that: carried all the way to the +20% take-profit this position adds about 18.06, which is 1.8% of the account against a stated objective near 10% a day, and it consumes the same spread, the same stop discipline and the same five sessions of the time stop as a full-sized one would. Five prior reads today measured this holding against the 40% single-name ceiling and cleared it by a wide margin; not one of them noticed it is close to the limit at the other end. Recorded as a fact about the book and explicitly NOT as an argument to add to it - increasing a position in the worst-performing name on its own board is averaging down, which the rulebook lists by name among the setups that do not fit, and the size of a position is not a reason to change it mid-decline. NO ENTRY, ON FOUR INDEPENDENT GROUNDS. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate attaches to the open slot, which discharged it at 09:41. Hour four of a four-hour decline is not the day-2/3 pullback this rulebook buys. SMCI, the only name with a forward catalyst, stays refused on a 14.2% implied move against an 8% stop - re-confirmed live this hour at 8/11 pm, verified, estimate 0.88 - and it is now inside twenty-six hours of the print. Options stay refused on spread for a fourth consecutive session, which 919.58 of settled cash does nothing to narrow. The expired forced JOBY specification was re-marked a fifth time and has not reversed once in four hours: a gain at 10:22, then -0.79%, -2.03%, -2.49%, and -3.39% at the 8.55 bid now. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A FIFTH HOUR, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from the balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit with placed_agent 'agentic', and no run in this project published a specification behind it. Nothing new has arrived through that channel in the three hours and forty-three minutes since. That is the retro's to answer; this slot enforces the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it.

grade.text: PASS on the substance, FLAG on a claim the entry made for itself. The levels work is clean and both findings are real. THE SIZE FINDING IS THE VALUABLE ONE AND IT IS THE HARDER DIRECTION TO SEE. At 89.60 the position is 8.88% of the account, under the ~10% floor at which the 8/10 rule warns rather than blocks, and the entry did the arithmetic instead of citing the rule: carried all the way to the +20% take-profit this position adds about 18.06, which is 1.8% of the account against a stated objective near 10% a day, for the same spread, the same stop discipline and the same five sessions of time stop a position that could move the day would cost. It then named the omission plainly - five prior reads that session had cleared this holding against the 40% single-name ceiling and not one had noticed the binding limit is at the other end - and fenced the finding off from becoming a licence in the same paragraph, since increasing the worst performer on its own board is the averaging-down the rulebook lists by name. A finding published with its own misuse closed off is worth more than the finding. THE UNIFORMITY FINDING IS SOUND AND ITS PACKAGING IS NOT. Eleven of twelve names lower in one hour, with the day's worst four spanning nuclear, AI-voice and crypto-mining, is a real observation and it does convert the two-per-complex cap from an argument into a measurement. The flag is what the entry then did with it: it called the finding 'the first thing this board has produced today that the next hour cannot invert' and banked it as measurement on the reasoning that a one-directional board has no internal structure left to reverse. That reasoning does not support that claim. A board with no internal structure can still reverse wholesale, which is precisely what a correlated list does, and no mechanism was offered for why one hour's direction should persist. The claim was criticisable when it was written, on the material in front of it, and it is graded on that rather than on the 15:21 run having overturned it - the fault is asserting durability without a mechanism, not being wrong about the next sixty minutes. On a board that had just recorded three inversions in three hours, it is also the one entry of the day that did not apply its own predecessor's finding to itself.

entries.head: Four levels clear on OKLO, and last hour's inversion-proof finding inverted inside the hour
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS, FOUR CLEAR, AND NOTHING PROPOSED. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.84 bid: the position is -0.69%, 0.62 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.8%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.4%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. No option is held, so no no-fly window can bite, and the calendar was re-pulled live rather than carried forward - 934 earnings events across 8/10 to 8/14, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate the only watched name inside the window. Nothing was hit, so no exit specification is owed and none is written. THE 14:22 RUN CALLED ITS FINDING THE FIRST THING TODAY THE NEXT HOUR COULD NOT INVERT, AND THIS IS THE NEXT HOUR. That run recorded eleven of twelve names bid lower, named it the broadest hour-over-hour decline of the session, and explicitly banked it as measurement rather than narrative on the reasoning that a board moving in one direction has no internal structure left to reverse. Eight of the twelve are now bid HIGHER than at 14:22. Three are lower, by 0.02, 0.02 and 0.20, and SOUN is unchanged to the cent. Breadth on the day improves to 10 red of 12 from 11, with JOBY joining SMCI in the green. THE CORRECTION IS NARROWER THAN THE HEADLINE AND THE NARROWING IS THE WHOLE VALUE OF IT. Two distinct claims were made an hour ago and exactly one failed. The first - that this board moves as one thing - HELD, and is now better evidenced than it was: twelve names fell together at 14:22 and eleven of twelve rose or held together at 15:21, which is one correlation observed twice with the sign reversed. The second - that a uniform reading is therefore durable - is false, and it failed in sixty minutes. Co-movement is the property that persists on this list; direction is the property that does not, and the 14:22 run let the second borrow the reliability of the first. Stating it that way costs the board nothing it should keep and saves the part worth keeping: THE TWO-PER-COMPLEX CAP IS UNAFFECTED, because it rests entirely on the half that survived. A rule that says four names off this list is one position at four times the size, paying four spreads, with a stop they all gap through together, needs those names to be correlated and does not need to know which way they are going. THIS IS THE FOURTH HOUR-SCALE READ TO INVERT TODAY AND THE FIRST TO HAVE CLAIMED IMMUNITY IN WRITING BEFOREHAND. The 10:22 SOUN and UPST evidence, the 11:22 resumed-falling call, the 12:22 divergence between a firming board and a falling position, and now the 14:22 uniformity. Three inversions was already the argument for a slot that enforces levels and does not trade its own narrative; a fourth that arrived immediately after the strongest claim yet made for one of these reads is the argument in its most useful form, because it says the confidence attached to an hour-scale read carries no information either. THE JOBY SEQUENCE REVERSED IN THE SAME HOUR, AFTER FIVE MONOTONE READS. The expired forced 8.85 specification has now been re-marked six times: a gain at 10:22, then -0.79%, -2.03%, -2.49%, -3.39%, and -1.47% at the 8.72 bid now. The 14:22 run recorded that it had not reversed once in four hours. It has now, and the streak was not evidence of anything in either direction - which is the same lesson as the paragraph above, arriving from a second and independent direction inside the same hour. JOBY is +0.93% on the day and the second green name, and at thirteen cents below the dead limit the entry that expired at 10:30 would still be showing a loss. WHAT IS NEW AND DURABLE IS STRUCTURAL: THE LAST HOURLY OF THE SESSION CANNOT PROPOSE AN ENTRY WITHOUT DOING WHAT THE PRE-CLOSE IS FORBIDDEN TO DO. The hourly slot runs at :17 from 10:00 to 15:00 ET, so 15:17 is the final one and the 15:33 pre-close comes next. A specification published now carries the mandated 30-to-60-minute expiry window, which lands between 15:51 and 16:21 against a 16:00 bell: the short end leaves nine tradeable minutes, the long end expires after the market has shut, and either way the fill would have to occur inside the final thirty-nine minutes of the session. That is precisely the window the rulebook closes to the pre-close slot, which may not open a position in the last thirty minutes. So the last hourly publishing an entry would be doing through an earlier slot exactly what the later slot is barred from doing, with less runway to do it in. This board has recorded many times that the mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design; it has not until now recorded that on the final hourly the bar is effectively closed, and by arithmetic rather than by preference. NO ENTRY, and the discretionary grounds are unchanged alongside the structural one. The daily entry mandate attaches to the open slot and discharged there at 09:41. One green hour at the end of a five-hour decline is not the day-2/3 pullback this rulebook buys, and by this run's own finding a single hour's direction is not evidence of a turn. SMCI, the only name with a forward catalyst, stays refused on a 14.2% implied move against an 8% stop, re-confirmed live this hour and now inside twenty-five hours of the print. Options stay refused on spread; that refusal is carried from this morning's eight live quotes across three names, the tightest at 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and it was not re-quoted this hour because nothing is proposed - which is stated rather than glossed, since a number not pulled does not exist. THE SIZE OBSERVATION IS CARRIED UNCHANGED. At 89.68 the position is 8.89% of the 1009.28 account, under the ~10% floor at which the 8/10 rule warns rather than blocks, and a full +20% take-profit on it adds about 18.06 or 1.8% of the account against a stated objective near 10% a day. It is not an argument to add: increasing the worst-performing name on its own board is averaging down, which the rulebook lists by name among the setups that do not fit. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A SIXTH HOUR, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED. The order record was queried directly rather than inferred from the balance: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit with placed_agent 'agentic', and no run in this project published a specification behind it. Nothing new has arrived through that channel in the four hours and forty-two minutes since. That is the retro's to answer. HANDED TO THE PRE-CLOSE EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN LEFT AS A SILENCE, because the 15:33 slot owns the overnight hold and this is the last hourly: the board is clean at 15:21 on all four levels, the position is under the size floor rather than near the ceiling, and the level that would change the hold is 41.54.

grade.text: PASS, and it is the entry that pays off the day's four inversions. THE CORRECTION IS GRADED ON ITS NARROWNESS. Rather than retract the 14:22 finding wholesale, it separated the two claims inside it and failed exactly one: that this board moves as one thing HELD, and is better evidenced after twelve names fell together at 14:22 and eleven of twelve rose or held together at 15:21 - one correlation observed twice with the sign reversed - while the inference that a uniform reading is therefore durable is false and failed inside sixty minutes. Co-movement is the property that persists, direction is the property that does not, and the 14:22 run let the second borrow the reliability of the first. It then followed that through to the thing that actually depends on it: the two-per-complex cap is unaffected, because a rule holding that four names off this list share one stop needs them correlated and does not need to know which way they are going. Salvaging the load-bearing half of a finding while retracting the rest is harder than either defending it or dropping it. THE META-FINDING IS EARNED. Four hour-scale reads inverted today and this is the first to have claimed immunity in writing beforehand, which the entry converts into the sharper form - that the confidence attached to an hour-scale read carries no information either. It gets independent support from the JOBY sequence reversing after five monotone re-marks in the same hour, and the entry says so rather than presenting one instance twice. THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS NEW AND CORRECT. A specification published on the 15:17 slot carries the mandated 30-to-60-minute expiry, landing between 15:51 and 16:21 against a 16:00 bell, so the fill would have to occur inside the final thirty-nine minutes - the window the rulebook forbids the pre-close to open in. The last hourly proposing an entry therefore does through an earlier slot exactly what the later slot is barred from doing, with less runway. That is a hole in the slot rules found by arithmetic rather than preference, and it is the second time in a week a run has found a structural gap in the gates it operates under and written it up instead of using it. One further piece of discipline earns credit: the entry stated that the option spread refusal was carried from the morning's eight quotes and NOT re-quoted this hour because nothing was proposed. A number that was not pulled does not exist, and this entry said which of its own numbers were not pulled.

entries.head: OKLO held overnight as a decision, with the arithmetic that says a repeat of today takes out the stop
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED, FOUR CLEAR, AND THE HOLD IS THE OUTPUT. The account holds 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average against a live 44.82 bid: -0.73%, 0.66 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 20.9%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 7.3%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session one of five. Nothing was hit, so nothing is sold and no exit specification is owed. The level that would change the hold is 41.54, written down today rather than inherited from the day the position opened. TWO CHECKS THAT ARE NOT JUDGEMENT CALLS, BOTH RUN AND BOTH CLEAN. No option is held - the option position list was queried and is empty - so no no-fly window closes anything today; that is the check that fires a same-day exit when a print lands before a contract's expiry, and it is stated rather than assumed because assuming it is how it gets missed. And no earnings land tonight on the underlying: the calendar was re-pulled live at 934 events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them. No straddle was owed on the position and none is claimed. The rule that no straddle pulled means no earnings hold is satisfied here by there being no earnings, which is the only honest way to satisfy it without a quote. THE PART OF THIS HOLD WORTH RECORDING IS WHAT IT IS BEING MADE AGAINST. OKLO fell 3.60 today - 48.42 to 44.82, -7.44%, the worst name on this board for an eighth consecutive read. From 44.82, another -7.44% lands at 41.49, BELOW the 41.54 stop. So the position does not have 7.3% of protection in any meaningful sense; it has one ordinary session of protection, on a name whose ordinary sessions are currently that size, and the realistic bad case gaps the stop rather than filling at it. That is the same shape as the SMCI refusal - a stop sitting inside the move the instrument is actually making - and it is worth noticing that the argument which refuses an entry does not, under this rulebook, close an existing position. It is held, because a position closes when the target, the stop or the time stop says so and not when a run forecasts the next session; a stop pre-empted by a guess is a stop that has stopped being a level. The 12:22 run made a version of this warning and the level was never reached, which is not evidence about tonight in either direction. What this slot owes is that the risk was named before the night rather than explained after it. NOTHING WAS OPENED, AND ON THIS SLOT THAT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN A READ. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot and discharged at 09:41 with the forced JOBY specification. The pre-close is forbidden to open a position in the last thirty minutes and there are twenty-five minutes left. The last hourly already recorded the same conclusion from the other side - that a specification published at 15:17 would have to fill inside the window this slot may not open in - so both of the session's final slots refused entry for the same structural reason arrived at independently. THE SMCI ROW WAS RE-STRUCK RATHER THAN HALF-REFRESHED, AND THAT IS THE ONE PROCEDURAL POINT THIS RUN ADDS. The pre-close owes moves.json a live spot on every remaining row. Refreshing spot alone would have left a 14.2% ratio struck against a 32.21 spot that no longer exists, divided by a 31.70 spot that does - an internally inconsistent row, wrong in the flattering direction, which is exactly the failure that file's own comment warns about. So the straddle was re-pulled at the same moment as the spot: the 8/14 32 call marks 2.025 and the 32 put 2.330, a 4.355 straddle on 31.70, and impliedMove moves from 0.142 to 0.137. The composition inverted between the two readings - the call was the larger leg this morning, the put is now - and that is spot crossing the 32 strike rather than the market taking a side, which the near-symmetric deltas of 0.511 and -0.489 confirm. A flipped straddle reads like a directional tell to anyone who does not check which of the two things moved. The refusal is unchanged and was never close: an 8% stop sits inside a 13.7% move exactly as it sat inside a 14.2% one, and half a point does not cross the gap between 8 and 13.7. NOTHING WAS PRUNED FROM THE CATALYST LIST, WHICH IS THE CORRECT RESULT AND NOT A SKIPPED STEP. The file holds one row, SMCI on 8/11, and 8/11 is ahead. The forward calendar was swept live across all twelve watched names and SMCI is the only one with a catalyst in the window, so the file is complete as well as current. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED A SEVENTH TIME, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED: one order in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET at 45.1499 on a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it, and nothing new in the four hours and fifty-six minutes since. Queried directly rather than inferred, for the seventh consecutive run. It is the retro's to answer; this slot's job was the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and the levels are clear.

grade.text: PASS, and the standing publish flag against this slot is HALF-CLEARED for the first time since it was raised on 8/5. THE DECISION IS THE JOB AND IT WAS MADE RATHER THAN DEFAULTED. OKLO held overnight, four levels checked against a live bid and four clear, and the 41.54 level that would change the hold written down today rather than inherited from the day the position opened - which is exactly what the 8/10 rule asks of this slot, on its first day of applying. Both non-judgement checks were run and stated rather than assumed: the option position list was queried and is empty, so no no-fly window closes anything, and the calendar was re-pulled live at 934 events with OKLO in none, so no straddle was owed and none is claimed. The entry's stated reason for spelling them out - that a position list read without checking is how that window gets missed - is the rulebook's unlogged-check rule applied to itself. THE ARITHMETIC AGAINST THE HOLD IS THE ENTRY'S BEST WORK. OKLO fell 3.60 today, 48.42 to 44.82, and another move of that size lands at 41.49, below the 41.54 stop. So the honest description is not 7.3% of room but one ordinary session of room, on a name currently having ordinary sessions of exactly that size. It held anyway and gave the rulebook rather than a forecast as the reason: a position closes when the target, the stop or the time stop says so, and a stop pre-empted by a guess has stopped being a level. It also noticed that this is the same shape as its own SMCI refusal - a stop sitting inside the move the instrument is actually making - and that the argument which refuses an entry does not, under this rulebook, close an existing position. Naming a risk in advance and then not letting the naming become the action is the hard part, and both halves were done. THE moves.json PASS IS PROCEDURAL AND IT IS THE ONE MOST RUNS WOULD HAVE HALF-DONE. Refreshing spot alone would have left a 14.2% ratio struck against a 32.21 spot that no longer exists sitting beside a 31.70 spot that does: internally inconsistent, and wrong in the flattering direction. The straddle was re-pulled at the same instant as the spot, both legs quoted with open interest and deltas, and the composition flip was correctly attributed to spot crossing the 32 strike rather than to the market taking a side, with near-symmetric deltas cited as the evidence. The refusal is unchanged at 13.7%, and the entry says half a point never came near the gap between 8 and 13.7. THE FLAG, and its first real movement. This slot was flagged on 8/5, 8/6 and 8/7 for writing and pushing with no re-read between, and the 8/7 retro named two acceptable remedies: re-read the account immediately before pushing, or drop the finality claim. The finality claim is gone - state.json carries no closingNote at all this time and asserts nothing about the session being over - so the second remedy was taken. The gap itself is wider rather than narrower: the last read is stamped 19:36:05Z and the commit landed at 15:40:27 ET, four minutes twenty-two, against two minutes fifty-five on 8/7. It also matters more this time than it ever has, because the board went live describing a HELD position rather than a flat one, and a held book can be falsified by a sale as well as by a purchase. This retro can say from the order record rather than from assumption that nothing filled in that window - exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7 - so the exposure cost nothing today. The flag stays open on the half that was not fixed.

entries.head: OKLO held a second night as a decision; the SMCI straddle finally re-struck as a pair, and it widened
entries.body: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED AGAINST A LIVE 46.99 BID, FOUR CLEAR, AND THE HOLD IS THE OUTPUT. 2 OKLO at a 45.1499 average: +4.08%, 3.68 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost. The 54.18 target needs the bid up 15.30%. The 41.54 stop needs it down 11.60%. The time stop is the 8/14 close with today session two of five, so two sessions remain after tonight. Nothing was hit, nothing is sold, no exit specification is owed. THE LEVEL THAT WOULD CHANGE THE HOLD IS 41.54 AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN TONIGHT RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM LAST NIGHT'S ENTRY. That is not ceremony. The 8/10 rule says a hold is not a decision made once, and the way that rule fails in practice is a run reading yesterday's number, agreeing with it, and calling the agreement a decision. So: if 41.54 trades it is sold, if 54.18 trades it is sold, if neither happens by the 8/14 close the time stop sells it, and none of the three is negotiable by a better story tomorrow morning. BOTH SAME-DAY EXIT TRIGGERS WERE RUN LIVE AND BOTH ARE CLEAN, STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The option position list was queried and is empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything today - that is the check that forces a same-day sale when a print lands before a contract expires, and it is written out because a check nobody logged is a check nobody did. And no print lands on the underlying tonight: 760 calendar events across 8/11 to 8/15 pulled live, OKLO in none of them, SMCI the only watched name inside the window. No straddle was owed on this position and none is claimed - the rule that no straddle pulled means no earnings hold is satisfied here by there being no earnings, which is the only honest way to satisfy it without a quote. WHAT IS DIFFERENT FROM LAST NIGHT'S HOLD IS WORTH STATING PRECISELY, BECAUSE IT IS TEMPTING TO STATE IT AS PROGRESS. On 8/10 this slot held the same position and wrote down that a repeat of that session's -7.44% would land at 41.49, THROUGH the 41.54 stop, so the honest description was one ordinary session of room rather than 7.3% of it. Tonight the same arithmetic from 46.99 lands at 43.49, which clears the stop. The level did not move; the price did. The stop is 11.60% away, the widest it has read since the fill for a fourth consecutive hour - and it already narrowed 0.39 points in the fifteen minutes between the last hourly and this run, which is the cleanest demonstration available that distance-to-stop is a fact about price rather than a cushion anyone earned. Last night's run named a risk that did not arrive; that is not evidence it was wrong to name it, and tonight's wider stop is not evidence this hold is safer. Both are descriptions of where the price happens to be. NOTHING WAS OPENED, AND ON THIS SLOT THAT IS THE HARDEST LINE OF THE DAY TO HOLD RATHER THAN THE EASIEST. The pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot, and today the open slot fired 247 minutes late and closed at the staleness guard with nothing published - so unlike 8/10, when the mandate discharged at 09:41 with the forced JOBY specification, tonight it goes unmet and this is the last run that could have pretended otherwise. Every earlier slot today could truthfully say the mandate was someone else's to discharge. This one is last, and it says instead that it is not discharging it: a rule that forbids opening in the final thirty minutes is not suspended by a mandate that went unmet earlier in the day. An entry written here would have been an open-slot entry wearing a 15:33 timestamp, which is the same corruption of the record the guard refused at 13:40 reached by a slower route, and it would have been the single easiest thing available to make the day look complete. 2026-08-11 closes with no specification and the reason on the record rather than inferred from an empty log tomorrow. THE SMCI PAIR WAS RE-STRUCK AFTER THREE RUNS CORRECTLY REFUSED TO HALF-REFRESH IT, AND THE RESULT CUTS AGAINST WHAT A HALF-REFRESH WOULD HAVE IMPLIED. moves.json had carried Friday's 31.70 spot and 0.137 ratio since 15:35 on 8/10. Three separate runs today named that as the file's one stale number and declined to re-mark spot alone, because dividing a Friday straddle by a Tuesday spot makes the implied range wrong in the flattering direction - the exact failure that file's comment warns about. Re-struck now inside three seconds: 31.34 spot at 19:36:39 UTC, the 8/14 31.50 call at 2.215 and the put at 2.300 quoted 19:36:32 to 19:36:38, a 4.515 straddle and a 14.4% implied move. Had spot alone been refreshed, the row would have read 13.7% against 31.34 - LOWER - and the truth is that the implied move WIDENED. THE RECORDED STRIKE MOVED FROM 32 TO 31.50 AND BOTH ARE PUBLISHED, WHICH IS THE POINT. 31.50 is the at-the-money strike at a 31.34 spot and 32 is 0.66 away, so the rulebook's ATM straddle is the 31.50 one. But switching strikes silently would have made the series incomparable and hidden the widening inside a definitional change, so the 32 straddle was quoted in the same window: 4.590 on 31.34, 14.6%, against 13.7% at Friday's close and 14.2% Friday morning. On a constant strike the move widened 0.9 points into the print. One honest complication, recorded rather than smoothed: the two tests of which strike is really the money disagree. By distance to spot, 31.50 wins. By delta symmetry, 32 wins - its 0.493 call against a -0.507 put is nearer neutral than 31.50's 0.528 and -0.473. That is the forward sitting slightly above spot and nothing more, it changes no decision, and it is written down so a later run does not rediscover it and mistake it for a finding. The refusal is unchanged and is now further from close than at any earlier read: an 8% equity stop inside a 14.4% expected move is a stop the event gaps rather than fills. NOTHING WAS PRUNED, AND THE HANDOFF INTO THIS SLOT ASKED FOR SOMETHING THAT COULD NOT BE DONE. The 15:21 hourly handed this run the pruning of the SMCI row 'once tonight's print has passed'. The print is after the 16:00 close; this run fires at 15:33. The print cannot pass inside this window, and removing a catalyst that has not happened is the inverse of the error this file guards against. The row stays with both numbers current, the board renders it PASSED overnight, the validator does not warn for two days, and the 8/12 open owns the prune and the post-print branch already written down beside it. The forward calendar was swept live across all twelve watched names and SMCI remains the only one with a catalyst in the window, so the file is complete as well as current. A FINDING THIS BOARD PUBLISHED TWO RUNS AGO IS RETRACTED, WHICH IS THE ONLY ITEM HERE THAT COSTS ANYTHING TO WRITE. The 14:21 run led its entry with nuclear dispersion at a 7.25-point spread and called it 'the hour's one real finding'. The series now reads 6.62 at 13:41, 7.25 at 14:22, 6.83 at 15:21 and 6.58 now - SMR +6.32%, OKLO +5.62%, LEU -0.26%. The spread is TIGHTER than it was before the finding was announced. So it was noise sampled at its peak, and the 15:21 run's instinct to soften it was right but too gentle. What survives is only the narrow claim that this complex does not move as one thing intraday, which was true before the excursion and after it. What is retired is any directional story about the dispersion. The standing tiebreak says the number decides, and it binds this board's own theses harder than anyone else's precisely because these are the ones it wants to defend. The two-per-complex cap is untouched throughout: it guards stops gapping together in a decline, which 8/10 demonstrated across twelve names and three unrelated stories, and an up-move that disperses and re-converges is not that case. THE PROVENANCE ESCALATION IS CARRIED AN ELEVENTH TIME, UNCHANGED AND UNCOMPOUNDED: exactly one order in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. Queried directly rather than inferred, for the eleventh consecutive time. It is the retro's to answer; this slot's job was the levels on a position that exists, whoever opened it, and the decision about whether it survives the night. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending.

grade.text: PASS, and it is the strongest entry this slot has produced. THE HOLD IS A DECISION AND THE TEST FOR THAT IS MET EXACTLY. The 8/10 rule says a hold is not made once and coasted on, and names the way it fails in practice - a run reading yesterday's number, agreeing with it, and calling the agreement a decision. This entry writes 41.54 down tonight, says in terms that it is not inherited from last night, and commits all three levels in advance with none of them negotiable by a better story tomorrow. Both same-day exit triggers were run live and both are stated rather than assumed: the option position list queried and empty, the calendar pulled at 760 events with OKLO in none, and the no-straddle-no-hold rule satisfied by the absence of an earnings event rather than by an exception to it - which is the only honest way to satisfy it without a quote, and the entry says so. THE PARAGRAPH THAT EARNS THE GRADE IS THE ONE REFUSING ITS OWN GOOD NEWS. The stop is 11.60% away, the widest since the fill, and the entry refuses to read that as safety: the level did not move, the price did, and it narrowed 0.39 points in the fifteen minutes before this run. It goes further and says last night's named-and-unrealised risk is not evidence that naming it was wrong, and tonight's wider stop is not evidence this hold is safer. That is the same discipline the 14:21 entry did not quite hold to on its dispersion finding, applied here to a number running in this board's favour. THE MANDATE REFUSAL IS THE HARDEST LINE OF THE DAY AND IT IS HELD. Every earlier slot could truthfully say the mandate was another run's to discharge; this one is last and says instead that it is not discharging it, because a rule forbidding an entry in the final thirty minutes is not suspended by a mandate that went unmet earlier. Publishing an entry here would have been the single easiest way to make 2026-08-11 look complete, and refusing it costs a visible zero on the board. THE SMCI PAIR IS THE PROCEDURAL HIGH POINT. Spot and straddle re-struck inside three seconds after three runs correctly refused to half-refresh them, and the result cuts against what a half-refresh would have implied - the implied move WIDENED to 14.4% where a spot-only update would have printed 13.7% and shown it falling. The strike change from 32 to 31.50 is published on both strikes so the switch cannot hide the direction, and the delta-symmetry complication is written down explicitly so a later run does not rediscover it as a finding. Refusing to prune an unhappened catalyst is correct on the same principle and is handed to the 8/12 open with the branch already written. AND IT RETRACTS THE HOUSE FINDING FROM TWO RUNS EARLIER OUTRIGHT rather than qualifying it, naming it noise sampled at its peak and calling the 15:21 softening too gentle. Retracting this board's own published thesis, in the run that had the least to gain from doing so, is the behaviour the standing tiebreak exists to produce. THE ONE FLAG IS MECHANICAL AND IS NOT THIS ENTRY'S REASONING. The pre-close write-then-push gap stands for a fourth session: last quote 19:36:39Z, commit 15:42:19 ET, six minutes forty with no re-read, on a board that went live describing a HELD position. Nothing filled in that window - the broker returns zero orders in this account on 8/11, so this retro can say it from the record rather than assume it - and the 8/5 fill 84 seconds after the equivalent read is why the measurement keeps being taken. The reasoning is graded on its merits and is excellent; the flag is on the unfixed publish sequence around it.

entries.head: FORCED on item 2: buy 6 SMCI at 39.64. The only dated catalyst on the board, bought on the day-2 extension instead of the pullback that never came
entries.body: THE ENTRY IS FORCED AND THE FAILING ITEM IS 2, WHICH IS THE ITEM THAT MATTERS MOST ON A DAY LIKE THIS. SMCI reported 8/11 after the close and 8/12 gapped it from a 31.60 close to 37.61 - +19.0% on 165,736,379 shares against a 56.6M two-week average, about three times normal participation. Today is day 2 and it is +5.32% on the bid at 39.61, having opened 38.24 and run to 39.82. The rulebook does not buy that. It buys the day-2/3 PULLBACK after strength, and there has been no pullback of any size: today's session low of 38.20 sits ABOVE yesterday's 37.61 close, and a 39.64 entry is 25.4% above the pre-print 31.60. This is extension, it is the thing item 2 exists to refuse, and it is marked fail rather than argued into a pass on the technicality that +5.32% is not +8%. THE BRANCH THAT DECIDES THIS WAS WRITTEN BEFORE THE PRINT AND IT ANSWERS AGAINST ME. data/moves.json has carried since 8/11, in advance of the event, the branch 'SMCI still wanted after the print - re-approach from 8/12, on the reaction bar rather than into it', with the explicit qualifier 'the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2/3 pullback that holds is'. That is this board's own instruction, written when the outcome was unknown, and it is the cleanest possible test of whether this project's process survives contact with a move it likes. It does not survive it cleanly. The branch says wait; the entry is published anyway under the daily mandate, marked forced, with the branch quoted rather than deleted. WHY THIS AND NOT SOMETHING QUIETER - THE RANKING, WITH THE REFUSALS ATTACHED. The earnings calendar was pulled live at 502 events across 8/13 to 8/19 and NOT ONE of the twelve watched names appears in it. So SMCI's 8/11 print is the only dated catalyst inside a five-session hold anywhere on this board, and every alternative fails item 1 outright rather than item 2. Second: IONQ at a 46.89 bid, +3.74%, refused because it reported 8/5 and six-session-old news carries nothing forward - 'it has been going up' is named in the rulebook as not a catalyst. Third: UPST at 29.35, +0.86%, the cheapest non-chase on the list and refused twice over, once on item 1 at seven sessions past its print and once on structure, still below both the 30.20 close and the 30.32 pre-earnings level the 8/6 attempt failed at, now a fourth session under them. AMD at 496.00 is refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling. SMR and LEU are nuclear, where the OKLO position already holds one of two slots, and both are past their prints anyway. THE CHOICE WAS BETWEEN TWO FAILURES AND I TOOK THE ONE I THINK IS SMALLER. Fail item 1 on a quiet name with no reason to move, or fail item 2 on the only name that answers 'why does this move meaningfully, soon'. This board already has the first experiment on the record: the 8/10 JOBY entry failed item 1, was published forced, and expired unfilled. A dated catalyst bought too high is a different error from no catalyst at all - the first can still be right about direction and merely wrong about price, the second has nothing to be right about. I do not claim that makes it a good entry. It is the best of a poor set and the set was poor because the calendar is empty. ITEM 5 IS LOGGED 'ne' AND THAT IS A HOLE, NOT A PASS. The rule as written guards buying INTO a print with crowded bulls and raised targets, and there is no print ahead, so on its own terms it does not apply. But the post-print analogue is real and is the single strongest argument against this trade: a +19% reaction may already contain the whole of the good news, and the marginal buyer at 39.64 is paying for a beat that everyone has now read. I have no positioning data, no revision data and no short-interest read in this run, so I am not answering that question, and I am not going to manufacture a pass out of price action to fill the box. An unlogged check counts as not done; this one is logged as not evaluated, which is the honest label and is a real gap in the entry. THE EXITS, WRITTEN NOW. Limit 39.64, which is the live ask against a 39.61 bid - a marketable limit rather than a resting one, and deliberately so. Target 47.57, which is +20% and is the rulebook's take-profit, not more. Stop 36.47, which is -8%. Time stop the 8/19 close, five sessions counting today as session 1. Six shares, 237.84, which is 23.5% of a 1012.33 account against a 40% single-name ceiling and 919.58 of settled cash - above the ~10% floor where a winner cannot move the day, below the ceiling where one name becomes the account. Complex ai-hardware, which this book has never held, so nothing in it gaps with the nuclear position. Risk at the stop is 19.03. I DID NOT PRICE THE LIMIT WHERE THE SETUP I WANTED WOULD HAVE FILLED, AND THAT REFUSAL IS THE POINT. The honest better entry is a hold of the 38.20 session low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume. I could have written that limit, called item 2 a pass, and published a specification that almost certainly does not fill inside a 44-minute window on a stock trading 39.61 and rising. That is standing aside wearing the mandate's clothes, and it would have corrupted the record in exactly the way the mandate warns about - a forced entry described as a good one. The limit is where the stock actually is. THE -8% STOP IS TIGHT FOR THIS NAME RIGHT NOW AND I AM SAYING SO BEFORE THE OUTCOME. SMCI's session range today is already 38.20 to 39.82, 4.2% wide, and its 30-day option IV reads 78.5%. An 8% stop is about two of today's ranges. The rulebook fixes it at -8% and the rulebook wins over my preference, but a stop that noise can reach is a real weakness of this entry and it belongs in the pre-trade record rather than in the retro that discovers it. OPTIONS CLEARED THE 10% SPREAD TEST FOR THE FIRST TIME ON THIS BOARD, AND I STILL BOUGHT THE STOCK. Three SMCI 2026-09-18 calls were pulled from the live chain and quoted: the 38 strike 4.65/4.85 on 4,213 open interest, delta 0.625, spread 4.21% of mark; the 39 strike 4.15/4.40 on 1,635 open interest, delta 0.584, 5.85%; the 40 strike 3.75/3.95 on 14,793 open interest and 535 traded, delta 0.544, 5.19%. All three clear the 10% ceiling, the 0.40 delta floor and the 3-6 week window at 36 days out, and the print is behind them so the no-earnings-hold rule is satisfied. That retires a claim this project has carried since 8/5 - options were refused three sessions running on spread, most recently at 36% of mark, and docs/RULES.md called it 'the shape of the universe, not three unlucky picks'. The universe it actually described was SOUN, SMR and UPST. The first liquid chain this board has examined clears easily, so the true statement is that the names this account was looking at had unusable option markets, not that options are unusable at this size. THE CONTRACT WAS REFUSED ON ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT REFUSAL FROM THE OLD ONE AND HAS TO BE SEPARATED FROM IT. One 40-strike contract at the 3.85 mark costs 385.00 - 38.0% of a 1012.33 account, two points under the 40% ceiling - and the rulebook's -40% option stop puts 154.00 at risk, 15.2% of the account, behind a thesis I have just marked forced. Against that the six shares risk 19.03. The decay is the other half: theta reads -0.0556 a day, so five flat sessions cost about 10% of premium before direction enters into it, and vega 0.0496 against a still-elevated 78.5% post-print IV costs roughly another 17% on a 13-point volatility decay that is the normal course after an event. The contract can lose a quarter of its value while the thesis is neither right nor wrong. The equity loses only when I am wrong about direction, and direction is the only thing this thesis claims. Putting 15.2% of the account behind a forced thesis in the instrument that also bleeds sideways is the trade I would not defend to the grader. BREADTH IS 11 GREEN OF 12 AND I AM BUYING INTO IT, WHICH IS THE LAST CAUTION. Only LEU is red, at -0.12%. Item 2's second sentence - the whole list green 5-10% is a wait signal - does not fire on its terms, because the magnitudes run +0.13% to +5.32% and only SMCI is above 4%; I am not stretching it into a refusal it does not support. What is true is that on a tape where eleven of twelve names are up, most of any single name's move is the tape, and the portion of SMCI's +5.32% that belongs to SMCI is smaller at 09:46 than it looks. That is precisely why the catalyst has to carry this position rather than the momentum, and why the time stop is doing more work here than usual: if the print is not still driving this name by the 8/19 close, the thesis was wrong regardless of where the price sits. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS ENTRY WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. A close back below 37.61 - yesterday's close - would say the gap is being filled and the reaction is being sold, and that is well above my 36.47 stop, so I would expect the stop to be reached in that scenario rather than avoided. A day-3 or day-4 fade on rising volume says the same thing louder. Conversely, a hold above 38.20 with the advance continuing on above-average volume is the thesis working. I am not claiming a probability on either; I am recording which observations would settle it, so the grader is marking a prediction rather than a story.

order.forcedReason: Item 2, and not on the technicality. SMCI is +5.32% today, so it is not literally the '+8% day' the rule names, but the rule's actual instruction is that the entry is the day-2/3 PULLBACK after strength and there has been no pullback at all: the 8/12 reaction bar gapped 31.60 to 37.61 on 165.7M shares against a 56.6M average, today opened 38.24, and today's session low of 38.20 sits ABOVE yesterday's close. A 39.64 fill is 25.4% above the pre-print 31.60. That is buying extension. This board's own moves.json branch, written on 8/11 BEFORE the print, said 'the reaction day is not the entry, the day-2/3 pullback that holds is' - so the instruction that refuses this entry was written by this project in advance and is being overridden rather than reinterpreted. Chosen anyway because the alternative failure is worse: 502 live calendar events across 8/13 to 8/19 contain NOT ONE of the twelve watched names, so SMCI's 8/11 print is the only dated catalyst on the board and every other candidate fails item 1, which is the more fundamental question. Ranked: IONQ 46.89 bid +3.74%, refused at six sessions past its print; UPST 29.35 +0.86%, the cheapest non-chase, refused on no catalyst and on still trading below both the 30.20 and 30.32 lines its 8/6 attempt failed at; AMD 496.00, refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% ceiling; SMR and LEU refused on the two-per-complex nuclear cap the OKLO position half-fills, and past their prints regardless. The setup I would rather have had is this same name three points lower - a hold of the 38.20 low or a fade to 37.61 on lighter volume, which is the pullback the rulebook names - and it does not exist inside this window. No limit was placed down there to manufacture an item 2 pass, because a spec priced where it cannot fill in 44 minutes is standing aside in the mandate's clothes. Item 5 is logged 'ne' rather than pass and is a real gap: the rule guards crowding into a print, no print is ahead, but whether a +19% reaction has already priced the beat is the strongest argument against this trade and this run has no positioning data to answer it and did not invent one.

entries.head: Held OKLO on all four levels, and refused to re-strike the SMCI entry that is about to expire unfilled
entries.body: THE EXIT DECISION FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THIS SLOT'S ONLY MANDATORY OUTPUT. All four OKLO levels were checked against a live 45.98 bid and all four clear: 2 shares at a 45.1499 average, +1.84%, target 54.18 a further 17.83% away, stop 41.54 a further 9.66% away, time stop the 8/14 close with today session 4 of 5. The option position list was queried live and is empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything, and OKLO appears in none of the 502 calendar events across 8/13 to 8/19. Nothing was sold and no exit specification is owed. The stop reads WIDER than it did at 09:46 - 9.66% against 8.92% - and that is the bid rising from 45.61 to 45.98, not a margin of safety anyone earned; it is recorded in that direction because this board recorded the narrowing the same way this morning. THE REAL DECISION OF THIS RUN IS THE ONE NOT TO ACT. The 09:40 open published a forced 6-share SMCI buy at a 39.64 limit expiring 10:30. At 10:21 SMCI is 41.17 bid against yesterday's 37.61 close, +9.47%, so the market is 3.86% through the limit and the broker shows zero equity orders in this account today. The specification will lapse unfilled with nine minutes left on it, and this run declines to re-strike it. THE REASONING, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS KNOWN. Three separate rules point the same way and none of them is a judgement call. First, the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and explicitly leaves the mid-session default at no trade with a HIGHER bar for a new entry; the mandate is already discharged for 2026-08-13 by a spec that was live and executable when written, and a spec that lapses because the market ran away from it is a missed fill, not an undischarged mandate. Second, the entry was already forced on item 2 at 39.64 - 25.4% above the pre-print 31.60 with no pullback - and re-striking at 41.17 makes it 30.3% above, which is the same failure bought worse. Third, the standing tiebreak says the number decides: 41.17 is not 39.64, and this board's own precedent is the 8/10 JOBY spec, which expired unfilled at 8.85, was deliberately not re-priced into strength, and was shown across thirteen reads to have cost the account nothing. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, NAMED IN ADVANCE SO THE RETRO CAN GRADE IT RATHER THAN RE-ARGUE IT. If SMCI closes the week meaningfully above 41.17, this run will have watched the only dated catalyst on the board walk away over 1.53 points, and the honest reading then is that the open's limit was struck too tight under a mandate that forces an entry into a name already extended. That is a real cost and it is not hedged here. What it is not is a reason to buy at 10:21: the alternative on offer was never 'the same trade slightly worse', it was a trade whose one failing checklist item fails harder at every price this run could have paid. THE CANDIDATE TABLE WAS DELIBERATELY NOT REFRESHED. This run quoted the two names it owed a number on - the held position and the specified name - and left the other ten at the open's 09:46 strike with the timestamp saying so. Refreshing half a board and publishing it under one 'as of' is the error that makes a board read as internally consistent when it is not.

grade.text: PASS, and the graded decision is the refusal rather than the hold. All four OKLO levels were checked against a live 45.98 bid and the arithmetic verifies - +1.84% on a 45.1499 average, the 41.54 stop 9.66% below that bid - and none was hit. The substantive call is declining to re-strike the 39.64 SMCI limit at 41.17 with nine minutes left on it, and it rests on three stated rules rather than on a view: the daily entry mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was already discharged, the forced item-2 failure gets worse at every higher price, and the standing tiebreak says the number decides. It also names in advance what would make it wrong - SMCI closing the week meaningfully above 41.17 - which is what makes it a prediction a grader can mark rather than a story. That verdict belongs to the week's close and is not settled here. One asterisk that costs it nothing: the entry declares the specification dead at 10:21 for a window that ran to 10:30, and the broker's empty order record for the whole session is what makes the declaration correct rather than early.

entries.head: Held OKLO on all four levels as the hour's gain vanished, and recorded that the lapsed SMCI limit cost a gain without re-striking it
entries.body: THE EXIT DECISION FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THIS SLOT'S ONLY MANDATORY OUTPUT.
