entries.head: FORCED on item 1: buy 8 UPST at 30.59. Nothing on the board has a catalyst, so the entry goes to the one setup the rulebook names by title rather than to a third-day extension this board refused five times yesterday at lower prices
entries.body:
THE MANDATE IS DISCHARGED AND THE FAILURE IS ITEM 1, ON EVERY CANDIDATE RATHER THAN ON THIS ONE. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-20 and not one of the twelve watched names appears in it. There is no dated catalyst anywhere on this board. So item 1 does not distinguish between candidates today - it fails on all of them - and the choice was never 'which name has a reason to move', it was 'which name is the least bad thing to own for five sessions without one'. That is worth stating plainly, because it is a weaker position than yesterday's, where at least one name answered item 1.

WHAT UPST HAS INSTEAD OF A CATALYST IS A SETUP THE RULEBOOK LISTS BY NAME. 'Breakout pullbacks' is one of three setups under 'Setups that fit'. On 8/13 UPST opened 29.19, ran to a 31.35 high and closed 30.97 on 4.85M shares against a 4.30M thirty-day average - a +6.4% session that reclaimed BOTH structural lines this board has been tracking since the 8/6 attempt failed: the 30.20 close it broke and the 30.32 pre-earnings level. Today it has pulled back, low 30.45, and is 30.57 bid at -1.29%, which is above both reclaimed lines. That is the shape the rulebook buys: not the up day, the day after it, with the level holding.

IT ALSO RETIRES THE SPECIFIC REASON THIS NAME WAS REFUSED YESTERDAY. The 8/13 open ranked UPST third and refused it on two counts: no catalyst, and 'still below BOTH structural lines the 8/6 attempt failed at, now closing a fourth session under them'. The second count is no longer true - the tape resolved it that afternoon. The first count still stands and is what makes this entry forced. A refusal whose stated reason has half-expired should be re-read rather than repeated, and this is the re-read.

WHY NOT SMCI, WHICH IS THE ENTRY THIS BOARD MADE YESTERDAY. SMCI is 40.26 bid, +2.81%, and it is refused today on a number rather than on a view. Three things, in order of weight. First: the entry is 27.4% above the 31.60 pre-print close and there has still been no pullback, which is the identical item-2 failure the 8/13 spec was forced on, only larger. Second, and this is the one that decides it: this board refused SMCI five separate times yesterday at 39.65, 39.87, 40.09, 39.87 and 39.41, every one of them BELOW today's bid, each time on that same item-2 reasoning. Buying it higher today would reverse five documented refusals, and reversing a refusal requires new information. Third: there is no new information, and what the tape did add points the other way - 8/13 touched 42.31 and closed 39.16, a 7.4% fade off the high on 122.8M shares. A name that gave back its whole range into the close is not a name that has resolved its extension. Under the 2026-08-10 standing tiebreak the number decides and the narrative is discarded; the number here is that today's entry is strictly worse than five entries this board already declined.

AND WHY THAT REVERSES YESTERDAY'S RANKING LOGIC, SAID OUT LOUD RATHER THAN QUIETLY. The 8/13 spec chose the item-2 failure over the item-1 failure on the reasoning that item 1 'is the more fundamental question'. I am choosing the other way today and the record deserves the reason: yesterday item 1 was ANSWERABLE - SMCI's print was two sessions old and the day-2 continuation is a setup the rulebook lists. Today it is answerable by nobody, so the item-1 failure is no longer a choice between a name with a catalyst and a name without one; it is the floor under every candidate. Once item 1 fails regardless, the tiebreak moves to which entry the rest of the checklist can defend, and a name passing 2, 4 and 6 on a listed setup beats a name failing 2 by a wider margin than it did yesterday. If that reasoning is wrong, it is wrong in a way the record can now check against both entries.

THE REST OF THE FIELD, RANKED, AND ALL OF IT POOR. IONQ 45.93 bid +2.11%, seven sessions past its print, nothing ahead - item 1 fails and it has no setup to put in its place. AMD 496.13 is refused mechanically before any view: one share is 49.0% of the account against the 40% single-name ceiling. RGTI 19.07 +2.42% and QBTS 21.22 +1.53% are both a week past their prints and are moving with the tape. SMR 9.75 and LEU 194.42 sit in the nuclear complex the OKLO position half-fills and are past their prints regardless. MARA 9.14 and SOUN 7.53 have neither a catalyst nor a structure. JOBY 8.07 is the weakest name on the board at -2.30% and the dead 8.85 specification from 8/10 is now -8.85% against it. This is a poor set and UPST is the best of it, not a good entry.

OPTIONS WERE PRICED LIVE AND REFUSED ON THE SPREAD, WHICH IS THE THIRD TIME THIS FINDING HAS BEEN NARROWED. Three UPST 2026-09-18 calls, 35 days out: the 27.5 strike 3.85/4.85 is 23.0% of mark, the 30 strike 2.41/2.71 is 11.7% on 11,609 open interest and 0.590 delta, the 32.5 strike 1.43/1.65 is 14.3% on 0.417 delta. The tightest misses a 10% ceiling by 1.7 points. Worth recording precisely because it is close: UPST quoted 25.5% of mark on 8/5 and quotes 11.7% now, so the standing finding is not that this chain is unusable, it is that this chain is nearly usable and still is not. No balance and no narrowing narrows it the rest of the way. Equity risks 19.60 at its stop and loses only on direction; the contract would risk 40% of a 256.00 premium on a thesis that is already forced.

SIZE, AND THE EXITS, STRUCK BEFORE ENTRY. 8 shares at a 30.59 limit is 244.72, 24.2% of a 1012.81 account - inside the 40% single-name ceiling and above the ~10% floor where a full winner cannot move the day. Target 36.71 is +20%. Stop 28.14 is -8%, and it sits 1.0% below the 28.41 low of 7/22, which is the nearest structure underneath rather than a number chosen to be comfortable. Time stop is the 8/20 close, five sessions counting today. UPST is tagged fintech, a complex this book has never held, so the two-per-complex cap is nowhere near binding beside the nuclear OKLO position and no stop in this book gaps with another.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. The honest case against it is that a breakout pullback with no catalyst is a chart pattern, and this rulebook's own item 1 says 'it has been going up' is not a reason. UPST's reclaim was a single session; one session above a line it spent four sessions below is thin evidence that the line has changed sides, and the -8% stop is only 1.3% below yesterday's 30.13 close-to-low excursion in percentage terms, which means ordinary noise in this name can reach it. If the 30.20/30.32 shelf fails and the stop takes it out inside two sessions, the correct reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup without a catalyst had nothing to hold it up, and the mandate bought a chart because the board had nothing else to buy. That is the specific thing this entry is testing, and it is what the grader should mark it against.

ITEM 5 IS LOGGED 'ne' AND IT IS A REAL GAP RATHER THAN A FORMALITY. The rule guards against crowding into a print, and there is no print ahead, so its stated case does not arise. But the honest version of item 5 here - whether a name that just reclaimed a broken level is being bought alongside everyone else who watched it reclaim - is a question this run has no positioning data to answer, and it did not invent one.

order.forcedReason: Item 1, and it fails on every candidate on the board rather than only on this one. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 2026-08-14 to 2026-08-20 and NOT ONE of the twelve watched names appears in it, so there is no dated catalyst available to buy today at any price. UPST reported 8/4 after the close - ten sessions back - and the 8/5 reaction failed outright, opening 34.595 and closing 30.20. What it has instead is a setup the rulebook lists under 'Setups that fit': 8/13 reclaimed both the 30.20 close it broke and the 30.32 pre-earnings level, closing 30.97 on 4.85M shares against a 4.30M thirty-day average, and today's pullback to a 30.45 low holds above both. That makes item 2 a genuine pass rather than a technicality - this is the day after the up day, which is the entry the rule asks for. Chosen over SMCI, which was ranked second and is the entry this board made yesterday, on a number rather than a view: at a 40.26 bid SMCI is 27.4% above its 31.60 pre-print close with still no pullback, and this board refused that identical entry five times yesterday at 39.65, 39.87, 40.09, 39.87 and 39.41 - every one BELOW today's bid. Reversing five documented refusals requires new information, and the only thing the tape added was an 8/13 bar that touched 42.31 and closed 39.16, a 7.4% fade off the high. Also ranked: IONQ 45.93 and RGTI 19.07 and QBTS 21.22, all a week or more past their prints with no setup to put in place of the missing catalyst; AMD 496.13, refused mechanically at 49.0% of the account against a 40% ceiling; SMR 9.75 and LEU 194.42, in the nuclear complex the OKLO position half-fills and past their prints regardless; MARA, SOUN and JOBY with neither catalyst nor structure. The setup I would rather have had is this same pullback with a dated event inside the five-session window, and no such thing exists on this board today. No limit was placed below the market to manufacture a better entry, because a spec priced where it cannot fill in 46 minutes is standing aside wearing the mandate's clothes.

entries.head: No exit was due on three clear levels, and the time stop that decides OKLO is the close rather than this hour
entries.body: NO EXIT WAS DUE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OUTPUT OF THIS SLOT. Fired 10:21 against the 10:17 slot, four minutes late and inside the 20-minute guard. The scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. THREE OKLO LEVELS CHECKED ON A LIVE 46.57 BID, ALL CLEAR. 2 shares at 45.1499: +3.15%, 2.84 unrealized on a 90.30 cost, 93.14 at the bid and 9.20% of a 1012.73 account. The 54.18 target needs a further 16.34%; the 41.54 stop needs 10.80% down. Option positions queried live and empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything. The position has given back 0.33 of bid since the open read 46.90 at 09:44, which moves the number and not the decision. THE TIME STOP IS THE ONE LIVE LEVEL AND THIS RUN DELIBERATELY DOES NOT FIRE IT. Today is session 5 of 5 and the level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. An hourly that sells at 10:21 has not enforced the time stop; it has substituted a different and earlier exit for the one the position was entered under, and done so on the argument that the day will end - which is true at every hour and therefore justifies selling at any of them. The rule this board keeps is that levels are struck at entry and enforced as written, and 'the close' is as much a written level as 41.54 is. The open handed this to the pre-close in advance rather than in hindsight and the handoff stands. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS HOUR ACT, STATED SO THE NEXT ONE INHERITS IT: 54.18 or 41.54 printing on the bid. Both are more than ten percent away, so the honest reading is that the calendar closes this position rather than the tape, and the pre-close should expect to sell 2 shares at the bid unless one of those two numbers speaks first. THE UPST SPECIFICATION IS STILL LIVE, STILL UNFILLED, AND IS NEITHER RE-STRUCK NOR RE-GRADED. The broker returns zero equity orders in this account today, so the 30.59 limit has not executed; it expires at 10:30, nine minutes from this read, and UPST is 31.08 bid - 1.60% above the limit and now +0.36% on the day against the -1.29% the open bought into. Two things follow and they point the same way. It is not re-struck: the thesis was published forced on item 1, no catalyst has appeared in the intervening thirty-seven minutes, and buying the same name higher because it moved is the definition of the chase both this slot's default and the rulebook's item 2 exist to refuse. And it is not re-graded: the 8/13 board settled, across six hourly readings of one dead SMCI limit spanning twelve dollars and ending three cents from where it started, that an intraday grade of an unexecuted specification measures the tape rather than the decision. Recording that UPST is currently above its limit as though it were a verdict would be the seventh instance of the behaviour that finding closed. Its verdict belongs to the retro. THE CANDIDATE BOARD IS NOT RE-STRUCK AND THE REASON IS STATED RATHER THAN LEFT AS A GAP. The twelve rows in state.json carry the open's 09:44 bids inside a six-second window, which is what makes them comparable to each other. Re-quoting the three names this run had reason to touch would leave a board of two timestamps reading as one, which is the same defect as the 8/13 pre-close publishing a 15:35 bid as a close. The exit board and the two watch rows carry this run's 10:22 quotes and say so; the candidate table remains the open's and says so. Account value 1012.73 pulled live, deployable 919.58 settled, nothing unsettled. Actions 0.
entries.grade: PASS. Three levels checked against a live 46.57 bid and every figure verifies: +3.15% on a 45.1499 average, 2.84 unrealized on a 90.30 cost, 93.14 at the bid and 9.20% of the 1012.73 account it quotes, with the 54.18 target 16.34% away and the 41.54 stop 10.80% down. The graded decision is NOT the hold - it is the refusal to fire the time stop six hours early, and the reason given is the correct one rather than a convenient one: the level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE, and an hourly selling at 10:21 has substituted a nearer exit on the argument that the day will end, which is true at every hour and therefore licenses selling at any of them. It states what would make it act, 54.18 or 41.54 on the bid, before knowing whether either would come. It declines to grade the still-live UPST specification on the finding the 8/13 board reached across six readings of one dead limit, which is this run applying a precedent that constrains it rather than one that flatters it. It refuses to re-strike the candidate table on the ground that a two-timestamp board reads as one - citing the 8/13 pre-close 15:35-bid-as-a-close error against itself. Outcome-blind and stated plainly: this run refusal was followed by six red hours and the position closed lower, which is not what makes it right and is not why it passes.

entries.head: The position crossed below its cost and no exit is due, because zero is not a level this book defends
entries.body: NO EXIT WAS DUE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OUTPUT OF THIS SLOT. Fired 14:21 against the 14:17 slot, four minutes late and inside the 20-minute guard. The scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. THREE OKLO LEVELS CHECKED ON A LIVE 44.93 BID, ALL CLEAR. 2 shares at 45.1499: -0.49%, an unrealized LOSS of 0.44 on a 90.30 cost, 89.86 at the bid and 8.90% of a 1009.46 account. The 54.18 target needs a further 20.59%; the 41.54 stop needs 7.55% down. Option positions queried live and empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything. THE ONE GENUINELY NEW FACT THIS HOUR IS THE SIGN. The position has been green at every reading since the 8/10 fill and is now red: 46.90 at the open, then 46.57, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93 - 1.64 of bid across four hours, +3.15% decaying through +1.79%, +1.37% and +0.31% to -0.49%, and -3.27% against the 46.45 close. It is new as a fact about the account and it is not new as an input to a decision, and keeping those two apart is the entire job. THE BOOK DOES NOT CONTAIN THE SIGN. Every exit this rulebook defines is a number: +20% take-profit, -8% equity stop, ~5 sessions, the option no-fly window. None of them is 'the position went red'. The stop is 41.54, struck at entry off the 45.1499 fill, and the bid is 7.55% clear of it. If crossing cost were an exit, every position would carry an implicit 0% stop, no thesis would ever be given the room the -8% was chosen to give it, and the -8% would be decoration. Selling here would set the stop to the entry price after the fact - the same defect as widening a stop, pointed the other way, and no more defensible for being the conservative direction. There was also no gain to protect: the take-profit was never within 20% of being touched, so nothing this slot was entitled to defend has been given up. THE TIME STOP IS THE LIVE LEVEL AND THIS RUN AGAIN DOES NOT FIRE IT EARLY. Today is session 5 of 5 and the level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. Four earlier runs today refused to contract it and the reasoning is unchanged rather than re-derived: an hourly that sells at 14:21 has not enforced the time stop, it has substituted a nearer exit on the argument that the day will end, which is true at every hour and therefore justifies selling at any of them. What is new is the temptation, not the argument. A red position at session 5 of 5 with roughly 70 minutes left is the most persuasive occasion this week to make an exception, and the smallness of the gap is the tell: if selling now and selling as written are nearly the same trade, then patience costs nearly nothing and the rule is nearly free to keep. Rules are not kept on the days they are cheap and abandoned on the days they are not; that is the mechanism by which a rulebook stops existing. The 2026-08-10 change says the time stop is not extendable by conviction, and the symmetric reading is that it is not contractable by impatience either. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS HOUR ACT, UNCHANGED SINCE 10:21: 54.18 or 41.54 printing on the bid. Neither is reachable from here, so the calendar closes this position rather than the tape, and the pre-close should expect to sell 2 shares at the bid. THE UPST SPECIFICATION IS DEAD AND DRIFTING BACK TOWARD ITS OWN LIMIT, WHICH IS NOT A REVIVAL. Zero equity orders in this account all session, re-checked live. UPST is 30.68 bid against the dead 30.59 limit, 0.29% above it and -0.94% on the day, the closest it has come since expiry. A limit that expired is not restored by the tape crossing it again, and re-striking on price movement alone - with the thesis still forced on item 1 and no catalyst since - is exactly the chase this slot's raised bar exists to refuse. Its grade belongs to the retro. NO NEW ENTRY: the mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44, and the default here is no trade. Actions 0.
entries.grade: PASS, and it is the strongest of the three. Levels verify against a live 44.93 bid: -0.49%, a 0.44 unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost, 89.86 at the bid and 8.90% of the 1009.46 account it quotes, target 20.59% away and stop 7.55% down. The graded decision is the refusal to treat the position crossing its own cost as an exit, and the entry does the hard thing - it names the sign flip as the most loaded print of the day, then separates the fact from the input to the decision and keeps them apart, which it correctly calls the entire job. The reasoning is the rulebook own: every exit this book defines is a number, none of them is the position went red, and if crossing cost were an exit then every position would carry an implicit 0% stop and the -8% would be decoration. It also refuses the symmetric temptation on the time stop, and its tell is exact - if selling now and selling as written are nearly the same trade, patience costs nearly nothing and the rule is nearly free to keep, and rules are not kept on the days they are cheap and abandoned on the days they are not. It adds that there was no gain to protect because the take-profit was never within 20% of being touched, which forecloses the one argument it had not already answered. No checklist is marked, which is correct handling on a position whose item 6 was never satisfiable.

entries.head: The last hourly refuses to contract the time stop by nine minutes, and the dead UPST limit turns marketable without turning live
entries.body:
NO EXIT WAS DUE AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OUTPUT OF THIS SLOT. Fired 15:21 against the 15:17 slot, four minutes late and inside the 20-minute guard, and this is the last hourly of the session. The scope preflight matched the mandate identifier exactly against the connector list and every other account was discarded unread. THREE OKLO LEVELS CHECKED ON A LIVE 44.58 BID, ALL CLEAR. 2 shares at 45.1499: -1.26%, an unrealized LOSS of 1.14 on a 90.30 cost, 89.16 at the bid and 8.84% of a 1008.79 account. The 54.18 target needs a further 21.53%; the 41.54 stop needs 6.82% down. Option positions queried live and empty, so no no-fly window closes on anything.

SIX CONSECUTIVE LOWER HOURS, AND THE RIGHT PLACE TO PUT THAT FACT IS THE TIME STOP RATHER THAN THE PRICE STOP. 46.90 at the open, then 46.57, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93, 44.58 - 1.99 of bid across five hours, +3.15% decaying through +1.79%, +1.37%, +0.31% and -0.49% to -1.26%, and -4.03% against the 46.45 close. The loss has more than doubled in the hour since the sign flipped. That is a real signal and it says something specific: a position that has drifted one direction for six hours on its fifth session is a thesis that did not work. The rulebook already has an instrument for exactly that reading, and it is the ~5 session time stop, which fires today. What the drift is NOT is evidence about the 41.54 stop, which is 6.82% away and was struck at entry off the 45.1499 fill. Reading a slow bleed as a stop hit is how a stop stops being a number.

THE LAST HOUR IS THE EASIEST ONE TO MAKE AN EXCEPTION IN, WHICH IS WHY IT IS REFUSED HERE TOO. The level written at entry is the 8/14 CLOSE. Five earlier runs today refused to contract it and the argument is unchanged rather than re-derived: an hourly that sells at 15:21 has not enforced the time stop, it has substituted a nearer exit on the reasoning that the day will end - true at every hour, and therefore a licence to sell at any of them. What is different this hour is only that the substitution has almost no cost: nine minutes and one slot separate this read from the pre-close. That smallness is an argument for the rule being cheap to keep, not for it being optional to keep. A rule kept only when it is free is not a rule, and the 2026-08-10 change that says the time stop is not extendable by conviction reads symmetrically - it is not contractable by impatience either, least of all in the final hour when the impatience is nearly costless and therefore nearly invisible.

THE HANDOFF, WRITTEN EXPLICITLY BECAUSE NO FURTHER HOURLY WILL RUN. Unless 54.18 or 41.54 prints on the bid first, the pre-close sells 2 shares at the bid on the time stop, session 5 of 5 from the 8/10 fill. Neither of those two numbers is reachable from 44.58 in nine minutes, so the honest expectation is that the calendar closes this position at a small loss rather than the tape closing it at a level. That was already the expectation at 10:21 when the position was +3.15%, and it is worth noting that the expectation did not change while the number moved 4.4 points - which is the test of whether a level was actually written down in advance or merely narrated afterward.

THE DEAD UPST LIMIT BECAME MARKETABLE THIS HOUR AND IS STILL DEAD. UPST is 30.49 bid / 30.52 ask. The ask is now BELOW the 30.59 limit the open published, so the specification that expired unfilled at 10:30 would fill at this moment - the first time all session that has been true. Zero equity orders in this account all session, re-checked live, so it did not execute and no order exists. It is not re-struck, and the fact that it is now fillable is precisely the reason to say so rather than to quietly let it stand: a limit that expired by its own written terms is not revived by the tape finally reaching it, and re-striking a spec because the price came to it - with the thesis still forced on item 1 and no catalyst appearing since - is an entry made on price movement alone. That is the chase this slot raised bar exists to refuse, and it is more tempting when the price is better rather than less. This is also the cleanest illustration this week of why an unexecuted spec is graded by the retro and not by an hourly: the same limit read as 1.60% out of the money at 10:21, 0.29% away at 14:21, and fillable at 15:22, and any of the three could have been written up as a verdict.

NO NEW ENTRY: the mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44, and the default here is no trade. Actions 0.
entries.grade: PASS. Levels verify against a live 44.58 bid: -1.26%, a 1.14 unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost, 89.16 at the bid and 8.84% of the 1008.79 account it quotes, target 21.53% away and stop 6.82% down, and -4.03% against the 46.45 close. The graded decision is the refusal to contract the time stop by NINE MINUTES, which is the hardest version of the refusal because it is the cheapest - and the entry says so itself rather than hiding it, that the substitution has almost no cost and that its smallness is an argument for the rule being cheap to keep rather than optional to keep. It puts six consecutive lower hours in the right place: a slow bleed is evidence about the THESIS and the instrument for a thesis that did not work is the time stop, which was already firing today, not the 41.54 price stop 6.82% away - and reading a slow bleed as a stop hit is how a stop stops being a number. The self-test in it is the best thing on the board this week: the expectation that the calendar rather than the tape would close this position was written at 10:21 when the position was +3.15% and is unchanged at 15:21 at -1.26%, which the entry names as the test of whether a level was written in advance or narrated afterward. It handles the dead UPST limit turning MARKETABLE - ask 30.52 below the 30.59 limit - by reporting it precisely and refusing to revive it, on the ground that a limit expired by its own terms is not restored by the tape reaching it, and it notes that the temptation is greater when the price is better. It hands off explicitly because no further hourly will run. What it could not know, and what the retro records against it rather than for it: the position was sold eleven minutes later at 44.7889, above this bid and above the specification limit.

entries.head: The time stop fires on OKLO: sell 2 at 44.70. The level was written on 8/10 and it is the calendar closing this, not the six red hours
entries.body:
THE DECISION IS THE ONE THING THIS SLOT EXISTS FOR AND IT IS AN EXIT. The 8/10 10:39 fill carried a ~5 session time stop per docs/RULES.md, struck as the 8/14 close. Today is session 5 of 5. The open wrote that level down before the session had an opinion about it, six hourly runs re-read it without contracting it, and the 15:21 hourly handed the action here explicitly: unless 54.18 or 41.54 prints first, the pre-close sells 2 shares at the bid. Neither printed. So the specification below is not a new judgement - it is the discharge of one made four sessions ago, and the only work left to this run was to check that the two price levels had not pre-empted it and to quote the exit live.

NEITHER PRICE LEVEL WAS HIT, AND SAYING SO PRECISELY MATTERS FOR THE RETRO. Against a 44.70 bid struck 19:35:35 UTC, the 54.18 target needs a further 21.21% and the 41.54 stop needs a further 7.03% down. This position is being closed by the CALENDAR, not by the tape, and the distinction is the whole content of the trade: a stop-out is the market taking a position away and a time stop is the book admitting the thesis did not happen. The record should read the second, because the second is what occurred.

WHAT THE SIX RED HOURS ARE AND ARE NOT EVIDENCE OF. 46.57 at 10:22, 45.96, 45.77, 45.29, 44.93, 44.58 at 15:21, 44.70 now - the position ran +3.15% and finished -1.00%, giving back 1.87 of bid across the session and -3.77% against the 46.45 close. Every hourly today refused to sell on that drift, on the correct ground that a trend on a chart is not a level and that 'the day will end' licenses selling at any hour. That refusal is not retroactively vindicated by the time stop arriving on schedule, and this run does not get to bank the drift as its reason now. The drift is evidence about the THESIS - six hours one direction on the final session says the move did not come - and the rulebook's instrument for a thesis that did not happen is precisely the time stop, which was already firing today regardless. The two facts agree, and only one of them is the rule.

THE ONE ARGUMENT FOR HOLDING, TAKEN SERIOUSLY AND REFUSED. It is a Friday, the position is only -1.00%, and a weekend hold costs nothing in theta on common stock. The 2026-08-10 rule answers it in one line: the ~5 session time stop is not extendable by conviction. Holding here would extend a written level because the loss is small - which is the same defect as widening a stop, pointed at the clock instead of the price, and it would convert a decision into an accident that happened to be cheap. A hold on Monday would then need its own reason, and the only one available would be that the position is still open, which is not a reason. Flat into the weekend is the decision.

EARNINGS AND THE NO-FLY WINDOW, BOTH CHECKED LIVE RATHER THAN CARRIED. The option position list was queried and is EMPTY, so no contract exists for a print to land inside and no no-fly window closes today. The earnings calendar was re-pulled across 8/14 to 8/20 and OKLO is not in it, nor is any other watched name - so nothing is dated into the weekend. No straddle was owed: the rule requiring one governs a HOLD through a print, and this run is not holding through anything.

HOW TO READ THE THREE PRICES BELOW, WRITTEN OUT BECAUSE THIS IS THE FIRST SELL SPECIFICATION THIS BOARD HAS PUBLISHED AND THE FIELDS MEAN SOMETHING DIFFERENT ON AN EXIT. The limit 44.70 is the bid, marketable and inside the 44.70/44.77 quote. The target 44.60 is the FLOOR rather than an ambition - if the bid slips in the closing minutes, complete the exit down to there rather than carry the position overnight over pennies. The stop 41.54 is the position's own standing stop from the 8/10 fill, carried unchanged and retired with the position; it is recorded rather than recalculated so the exit cannot be read as having quietly moved it. Nothing is sold above the bid and nothing is left working after 15:58.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. If OKLO gaps up Monday, this exit was still correct and the retro should not grade it as a miss: the position was given its five sessions and did not move, and a rule that is abandoned the first time it costs something was never a rule. The reading that WOULD indict it is the opposite one - if the five-session window is systematically too short for the setups this book buys, that is a finding about the rulebook to be made across the sample and by the operator, not by a run on a Friday afternoon with one position in front of it.

entries.head: Forced on items 1 and 5: buy 7 SMCI at 38.24. UPST is disqualified by the invalidation this board wrote down on Friday, and the options finding stops being about spread
entries.body:
THIS ENTRY IS FORCED AND IT IS FORCED TWICE, WHICH IS WORSE THAN THE LAST FOUR AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH. Items 1 and 5 fail. The mandate requires a specification every trading day and this is the best of a poor set, not a good entry, and the difference is the whole content of this note.

WHAT IS BOUGHT. 7 SMCI at a 38.24 limit, inside a 38.21/38.25 quote struck 13:45:27 UTC. Target 45.89 (+20%), stop 35.18 (-8%), time stop the 8/21 close counting today as session 1. Cost 267.68, which is 26.5% of a 1009.16 account: the natural quarter-weight at a four-position ceiling rather than the 40% single-name maximum, because a thesis this compromised does not earn the top of its range. The stop risks 21.42, or 2.1% of the account; the target pays 53.55, or 5.3%.

ITEM 1 FAILS ON THE WHOLE BOARD, FOR A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 8/17 to 8/23 and not one of the twelve watched names appears in it. SMCI reported 8/11 after the close - four sessions back - so there is no dated event inside a five-session hold on this name or on any other. The catalyst question did not rank the field today, it floored it, and the entry went to the name whose remaining checklist can be defended.

ITEM 5 FAILS, AND MARKING IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS PAGE. The rule is written around positioning into a print, and this print is behind rather than ahead, so calling it 'na' would be defensible on the letter and dishonest on the substance. The positioning the item exists to test is exactly the live question here: SMCI is 20.9% above its 31.60 pre-print close, and the four sessions since the +19.0% reaction of 8/12 are distribution rather than consolidation. 8/13 opened 38.28, touched 42.31 and closed 39.16 on 122.8M shares, giving back the whole range. 8/14 held on 62.0M. Today opened 39.31 and broke the 38.20 low of 8/13 to 37.88, with 8.9M shares done by 09:42 against a 58.0M thirty-day average, which is roughly five times normal pace for the elapsed session. I am buying into an unwind, not after one. Reading item 5 as not-applicable to reduce the forced count from two to one is precisely the move this board should distrust in itself, so it is marked fail.

THE BOARD'S OWN WRITTEN BUY CONDITION FOR THIS NAME IS NOT MET, AND I AM BUYING ANYWAY BECAUSE THE MANDATE COMPELS AN ENTRY. On 8/14 this board wrote the condition a grader can check: 'a pullback that holds - a defence of the 38.20 low or a fade toward 37.61 on lighter volume - bought there rather than here.' Neither branch is satisfied. 38.20 did not hold; it broke to 37.88. The fade toward 37.61 is arriving on price - the 8/12 close of 37.61 is the gap base and today's low sits 0.7% above it - but on HEAVIER volume, not lighter. So the correct description of this entry is early, on a name whose objection is compressing, and not vindicated.

WHY IT IS STILL FIRST, AND WHY UPST IS NOT. Friday's board ranked UPST first and wrote its invalidation in advance: 'If the 30.20/30.32 shelf gives way and the 28.14 stop is taken inside two sessions, the reading is not bad luck - it is that a setup with no catalyst had nothing holding it up.' That condition fired this morning. UPST opened 30.35, broke to a 29.80 low and is 29.92 bid, through the 30.20 close-line, through the 30.32 pre-earnings level, and through Friday's 30.25 low. A pre-registered disqualification that triggers and is then ignored was never a disqualification. So the name that was first is out on its own terms.

That leaves the mirror-image argument for SMCI, and it is the same argument Friday used to promote UPST from third to first: a refusal whose stated reason has expired gets re-read rather than repeated. SMCI was refused six times on a NUMBER - extension above the pre-print close with no pullback - and that number has moved 6.5 points in the buyer's favour, from 27.4% to 20.9%, while the pullback the board said was missing has now run four sessions and 9.7% off the 42.31 high. Under the standing numbers-over-narrative tiebreak, the number that drove the refusal has changed, so the refusal cannot simply be restated a seventh time. What has NOT changed is that there is no catalyst and that the unwind is still in progress, which is why this is forced rather than clean.

The asymmetry that decides between the two: UPST carries a triggered disqualification and SMCI carries an unmet precondition. The first says the thesis is wrong; the second says not yet. Given an entry is compulsory today, buying the not-yet over the already-wrong is the defensible order, and I would rather be early on a compressing objection than long a broken shelf.

THE OPTIONS FINDING CHANGES TODAY AND IT NO LONGER SAYS WHAT THIS BOARD HAS BEEN SAYING. For three sessions the refusal has been on spread, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling. That statement is FALSE of SMCI today. Four live 2026-09-18 calls, 32 days out and inside the 3-6 week rule, quote: the 40 strike 2.80/2.92 at 4.20% of mark on 14,360 open interest and 0.475 delta; the 37 strike 4.05/4.30 at 5.99% on 1,054 and 0.607 delta; the 39 strike 3.15/3.35 at 6.15% on 1,714 and 0.518 delta; the 38 strike 3.55/3.80 at 6.80% on 3,967 and 0.562 delta. Every one clears the ceiling. Every one clears delta 0.40. One contract at the 40 strike costs 286.00 at the mark against 1009.16 deployable. For the first time in this record, every mechanical option rule passes at once.

The contract is still not bought, and the honest reason is not spread. First, the 8/13 precedent, set by this board and reaffirmed on 8/14, is that the first option purchase waits for 'the next time a liquid chain appears beside a thesis that is NOT forced.' This thesis is forced twice. Abandoning a self-imposed precedent the first session it becomes inconvenient - in the direction of MORE risk on a WEAKER thesis - is the exact shape the rule-drift policy watches for, and it would be the agent loosening a rule rather than the operator. Second, arithmetic: a -40% option stop puts 114.00 at risk against the 21.42 the 7-share equity risks for the same directional view, and at 78% implied volatility the 40 strike bleeds about 0.0565 a day, roughly 0.28 or a tenth of the premium across a five-session hold, before the stock does anything. A thesis with no dated catalyst has nothing to pay for that decay. The accurate statement of the finding is now: this account's chains span roughly 4% to 23% of mark, the liquid end clears the ceiling outright and is affordable, and what stands between this board and its first option is the quality of the thesis rather than the quality of the market.

THE REST OF THE BOARD, RANKED. Third are the four green names on a 4-of-12 red tape - SMR +1.9%, MARA +1.5%, OKLO +0.3%, RGTI +0.1% - and buying the green half of a red morning is chasing green candles, which the rulebook lists by name under 'Does not fit'. SMR is additionally the name this account lost 14.0% in on 8/6. Fourth is AMD, refused by an explicit limit before any view is formed: one share at 510.63 is 50.6% of the account against the 40% single-name ceiling. Fifth are SOUN -3.5%, JOBY -0.8%, IONQ -0.2%, QBTS -0.5% and LEU -1.0%, all a week or more past their prints with no structure to put where the catalyst should be; SOUN and JOBY are weak without being at a level, which is a fact about the tape and not a setup. No limit was placed far below the market to manufacture a prettier entry, because a spec priced where it cannot fill inside 43 minutes is standing aside wearing the mandate's clothes.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. The bear case is the one I just marked fail: this is day four of an unwind of print-driven positioning, it broke its reference low on heavy volume this morning, and 37.61 is the last level between the entry and the 33.94 low of 8/12 - which sits below the 35.18 stop, so a full retrace of the gap takes me out. If the 37.61 gap base gives way and the stop is taken inside two or three sessions, the reading is NOT bad luck and not the mandate's fault. It is that I bought a name in the middle of distribution because a compressing valuation number and the best liquidity on the board were the only arguments available, and neither of those is a reason for a stock to go up inside five sessions. The setup I would rather have had is this same fade arriving at 37.61 on lighter volume with a dated event in the window, and no such thing exists on this board today.

entries.head: The SMCI specification expired unfilled and stays dead while the stock trades 1.52% above its limit - the pre-registered refusal held, and what it cost is recorded rather than left for the retro
entries.body: NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS A FINDING THIS RUN VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 11:23 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. This is the exits slot reporting an empty book, not a slot that skipped its levels. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 15:23:17 UTC against a local 11:21 ET call, the -4 EDT offset this run assumed, so the staleness guard was measured against an independently confirmed time and the run fired six minutes past a 11:17 slot. THE 09:47 SPECIFICATION IS NOW CONFIRMED DEAD, NOT PREDICTED DEAD. The 10:21 hourly wrote that unless SMCI traded back through 38.24 in the following eight minutes the spec expired at 10:30 by its own terms. It did not, and the confirmation is not an inference: ZERO equity orders and ZERO option orders exist in this account for the entire session, queried live, so the 7-share 38.24 limit was never placed by anyone and cannot have partially filled. That is the THIRD published specification in eight sessions to expire unexecuted. IT IS NOT REVIVED, AND THE ONLY REASON WORTH RECORDING IS THAT THE RULE RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. SMCI is 38.82 bid / 38.83 ask, a 0.03% spread, -2.56% against the 39.84 close but +1.60% above the 38.21 bid the limit was struck inside at 09:45 - so the dead 38.24 limit now sits 0.58, or 1.52%, BELOW the bid. It has risen a further 0.24 since the 10:22 read. On 8/14 this board refused to revive the dead UPST 30.59 limit when the tape came back UP through it, on the ground that a limit is not restored by the tape. Refusing to raise this one because the tape ran AWAY from it is that same rule applied in the direction that costs something, which is the only test of whether it was a rule. Re-striking a live specification mid-session would also be a NEW mid-session entry, held to a higher bar than the open, on a thesis already forced on items 1 and 5 - a bar it does not clear. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44; it grants this run nothing. WHAT THE REFUSAL COST IS STATED IN NUMBERS, BECAUSE A BOARD THAT ONLY RECORDS ITS CORRECT REFUSALS IS KEEPING A HIGHLIGHT REEL. Had the 7 shares filled at 38.24 for 267.68, the position would be 271.74 at the bid right now: +4.06, or +1.52%, unrealized. So the second half of this entry is that the thesis was directionally right for two hours and the account holds nothing, exactly as the forced JOBY 8.85 specification of 8/10 was right and unexecuted. THE PATTERN IS NO LONGER ABOUT ANY ONE THESIS. Three of eight sessions' specifications have expired unfilled and agentTrades remains 0, so the binding constraint on this record is now EXECUTION rather than selection - a process fact this run records and does not act on, because acting on it would mean either placing an order this run has no authority to place or widening a limit to chase, and both are worse than the bottleneck. THE UPST INVALIDATION STILL HOLDS AND THE MARGINAL BOUNCE IS NOT A RECLAIM. 29.37 bid, -3.48% on the day, 0.16 or +0.55% above the 29.21 the 10:22 run read, and still 0.43 BELOW this morning's 29.80 low - through the 30.20 close-line, the 30.32 pre-earnings level and Friday's 30.25 low. A 0.55% tick off an hourly low in a name whose structure broke this morning is noise, not evidence the shelf came back, and the dead 30.59 limit is 4.15% above the bid. The condition for this name's return was written down and is unchanged: 30.32 reclaimed and HELD on real volume, as a fresh setup with a fresh level, not as a resurrection of this one. Not shorted, not re-entered lower, not graded here. NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, and a flat book is not itself an argument for filling it. Balances pulled live rather than derived: 1009.16 total, all cash, zero equity value and zero options value, 1009.16 SETTLED with ZERO unsettled and no pending deposits. Actions 0 - this run has no order authority and placed nothing.
entries.grade: PASS. The book is flat and the entry proves it rather than asserting it - equity and option position lists both queried live at 11:23 and both empty, so every exit question is answered by arithmetic and none is skipped. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than the machine: venue_bid_time 15:23:17 UTC against a local 11:21 ET, which on this machine is not a formality. Every number verifies against the tape. SMCI 38.82 bid puts the 38.24 limit 0.58 or 1.52% below the bid, -2.56% against the official 39.84 close of 8/14 and +1.60% above the 38.21 bid the limit was struck inside, and 7 shares at 38.24 for 267.68 are 271.74 at that bid, +4.06 and +1.52% - all four confirmed here to the cent. UPST 29.37 bid is -3.48% against the official 30.43 close and puts the dead 30.59 limit 4.15% above the bid; both confirmed. The expiry is CONFIRMED rather than inferred - zero equity and zero option orders exist in this account for the whole session, which this retro re-queried independently and found the same. THE GRADED DECISION IS THE REFUSAL TO RAISE THE DEAD LIMIT WHEN THE TAPE HAD RUN AWAY FROM IT, and the entry gets the reason right: on 8/14 this board refused to revive a dead UPST limit when the tape came back DOWN through it, and refusing to chase this one UP is that same rule applied in the direction where it costs something, which is the only test of whether it was a rule. It also books the cost of its own discipline in numbers on the hour the discipline looks expensive, rather than leaving the unflattering half for this slot to find. And it names the constraint honestly - three of eight sessions' specifications unfilled, execution rather than selection now binding - while declining to act on it, on the ground that the only two available actions are placing an order it has no authority to place or widening a limit to chase. No checklist is marked, which is correct on a slot that opened nothing.

entries.head: The tape came back through the dead 38.24 limit and the limit stayed dead - the same refusal made on 8/14, now tested in the direction where keeping it is free
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 12:22 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. This is the exits slot reporting an empty book, not a slot that skipped its levels. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 16:22:30 UTC against a local 12:21 ET, the -4 EDT offset assumed, so the staleness guard was measured against an independently confirmed time.

THE ONE THING THIS HOUR HAD TO DECIDE. SMCI is 38.19 bid / 38.20 ask, a 0.01 spread on a 38.195 mark - 0.03%, the tightest quote on this board by a wide margin. The 38.20 ask is 0.04 BELOW the 38.24 limit that expired unfilled at 10:30. A buy limit is marketable when the ask reaches it, so the dead specification would fill right now, at 38.20, four cents better than it asked for. An hour ago the same limit sat 1.52% out of reach and this board recorded that as a cost. The tape has handed it back.

IT IS NOT REVIVED, AND THE PRECEDENT IS NOT NEW. On 8/14 a dead UPST 30.59 limit became marketable when the tape came back down through it, and this board refused to revive it: a specification that expired by its own written terms is not restored by the tape finally reaching it, because the expiry was a decision and not an accident. That is the identical situation on a different name three sessions later, and the identical answer. The rule has now been tested in all three directions available to it - refused a revival on 8/14 when the tape came back, refused a RAISE at 11:21 when the tape ran away, refuses a revival again now - and a rule that holds only in the direction where holding it is cheap was never a rule at all. Re-striking would also be a NEW mid-session entry, which this slot holds to a HIGHER bar than the open, on a thesis already forced on items 1 and 5. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44; it grants this run nothing.

THE COST BOOKED AN HOUR AGO HAS FULLY REVERSED, AND BOTH SIGNS ARE KEPT ON THE RECORD. At 11:23 this board wrote that 7 shares filled at 38.24 for 267.68 would be worth 271.74 at the bid: +4.06, or +1.52% unrealized, a thesis directionally right for two hours against an account holding nothing. At this bid the same 7 shares are 267.33 - a loss of 0.35, or -0.13%. SMCI is now 0.05 below the 38.21 bid the limit was struck inside at 09:45, which is to say the stock has travelled up 1.6% and back down 1.6% and gone nowhere in three hours. THIS IS NOT WHY THE LIMIT WAS LEFT DEAD AND IT IS NOT CLAIMED AS VINDICATION. The refusal was made at 11:21 on a precedent, at a moment when it looked expensive, and it would have been the same refusal had the stock kept rising. What the reversal establishes is narrower and worth exactly what it is: the 'cost of discipline' this board recorded an hour ago was a mark-to-market on an unfilled order across a single hour, and hourly marks on positions that do not exist are noise in both directions. A board that logs the cost of its rules only when they look expensive is keeping a scoreboard, not a record, so the reversal is logged with the same weight the cost was.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT LICENCE. It does not make the 09:47 entry good - it was forced on items 1 and 5, it had no catalyst, and its own written buy condition was unmet on both branches. It does not argue for buying SMCI here at a better price than the specification asked for, which would be the same chase wearing a discount. And it does not resolve the execution problem: three of eight sessions' specifications have now expired unfilled and agentTrades is still 0. That constraint is real, it is flagged for the retro, and the only two ways this run could act on it are placing an order it has no authority to place or re-striking a limit to chase - both worse than the bottleneck itself.

UPST HOLDS ITS INVALIDATION AND SIDEWAYS IS NOT A RECLAIM. 29.42 bid, -3.32% on the day, +0.17% above the 11:21 read, and still 0.38 below this morning's 29.80 low. The three hourly reads - 29.21, 29.37, 29.42 - sit inside a 0.21 band entirely beneath that low. A name that has stopped falling under a broken level has produced an absence of evidence, not evidence, and the written condition for its return is unchanged: 30.32 reclaimed and HELD on real volume, as a fresh setup with a fresh level rather than a resurrection of the dead 30.59 limit now 3.98% above the bid.

NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, and a flat book is not an argument for filling it. Balances pulled live rather than derived: 1009.16 total, all cash, zero equity value and zero options value, 1009.16 SETTLED with zero unsettled and no pending deposits. Actions 0 - this run has no order authority and placed nothing.
entries.grade: PASS, and it is the strongest of the three. Positions re-queried live at 12:22 and both lists empty; clock cross-checked at venue_bid_time 16:22:30 UTC against a local 12:21 ET. The numbers verify: SMCI 38.19 bid / 38.20 ask on a 38.195 mark is a 0.03% spread, the 38.20 ask sits 0.04 BELOW the 38.24 limit so the dead specification was genuinely marketable, 7 shares are 267.33 against a 267.68 cost for -0.35 and -0.13%, and 38.19 is 0.05 below the 38.21 bid the limit was struck inside - each confirmed against the 30-minute tape, which has this half hour opening 38.4285 and low 38.115. UPST 29.42 bid is -3.32% against the official 30.43 close, +0.17% above the 11:21 read, and puts the dead 30.59 limit 3.98% above the bid; confirmed. THE GRADED DECISION IS THE REFUSAL TO REVIVE A DEAD SPECIFICATION AT THE MOMENT REVIVAL WAS FREE - four cents better than it asked for - and the entry makes the harder argument rather than the available one: a specification that expired by its own written terms is not restored by the tape reaching it, because the expiry was a decision and not an accident. What raises this above a restatement is that it refuses to bank the reversal. The +4.06 booked an hour earlier had become -0.35, and instead of claiming vindication the entry says in terms that the refusal was made at 11:21 on a precedent when it looked expensive and would have been the same refusal had the stock kept rising, and that hourly marks on a position that does not exist are noise in both directions. A board that logs the cost of its rules only when they look expensive keeps a scoreboard; this one logged both signs with the same weight, on its own initiative, an hour before this slot could ask for it. It also refuses the three arguments this hour offered it - that the entry was good, that a better price is a reason to buy, and that the execution gap licenses acting - and names the second as the same chase wearing a discount. No checklist is marked, which is correct.

entries.head: Flat into the close, by decision - nothing held, so no overnight hold was available to get wrong, and the dead SMCI limit ends the day out of reach after a session spent crossing it
entries.body: THE DECISION THIS SLOT EXISTS TO MAKE IS WHETHER TO HOLD, AND TONIGHT IT IS MADE BY ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN BY JUDGEMENT: equity and option position lists were both queried live at 15:36 and both are EMPTY, so there is no target, no stop, no time stop, and no option no-fly window that could close today. No contract is open and this account has never opened one, so the no-fly question - does an earnings print land before this contract expires - has no subject. The earnings calendar was pulled live across 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-23 and none of the twelve watched names appears in it, so no straddle was owed and none was invented; the rule that no straddle pulled means no earnings hold is satisfied in its honest form, which is that there is no print and no position. NO NEW POSITION IS OPENED IN THE LAST THIRTY MINUTES AND THE MANDATE DOES NOT ASK FOR ONE. The daily entry mandate binds the open slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:44 with the forced 7-share SMCI specification at a 38.24 limit, which expired unfilled at 10:30. This slot's job is to decide holds explicitly, not to acquire one so that a decision exists to be made. WHAT TODAY ACTUALLY TESTED WAS WHETHER AN EXPIRED SPECIFICATION STAYS EXPIRED, AND THE ANSWER SURVIVED THE TAPE MOVING THROUGH IT IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The 38.24 limit was unmarketable at 11:21 when the tape ran away, marketable by 0.04, 0.21 and 0.17 across the next three hours, and unmarketable again by 0.03 at 15:21 and by 0.46 now, with SMCI 38.69 bid / 38.70 ask at 19:35:49 UTC. It was never revived. Five of those were refusals this board made and the sixth was settled by the ask rather than by judgement, which is a weaker form of evidence and is counted as such. THE COST OF THAT DISCIPLINE IS RECORDED ON THE DAY IT LOOKS WORST. Seven shares at 38.24 would be 270.83 at the closing bid, +3.15 or +1.18% unrealized - the best of six prints taken through the session, which read +4.06, -0.35, -1.54, -1.26, +0.14 and now +3.15. The sign changed three times and the refusal ends the day roughly three dollars out of pocket on paper. A board that logs the cost of its rules only when the rules look free is keeping a scoreboard, not a record. WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS, WRITTEN BEFORE TOMORROW RATHER THAN AFTER IT. SMCI is not carried forward as a live level: today's specification is dead, and if the open re-approaches this name it must be struck as a fresh entry with a fresh limit off a fresh quote, marked forced again if the catalyst and positioning items still fail - which on today's evidence they will, since the 8/11 print is five sessions back and the live calendar is empty through 8/23. UPST returns only on 30.32 reclaimed and HELD on real volume; it spent every one of seven hourly reads today beneath the low of its own morning, so the pre-registered invalidation that fired on 8/17 is carried into Tuesday intact rather than quietly relaxed at a lower price. The board goes into tomorrow with 1009.16 settled, nothing unsettled, no working orders, and no overnight risk of any kind - which is not a triumph, it is simply what the record says, and going into an empty calendar it is the position this rulebook prefers.
entries.grade: PASS ON THE DECISION, WITH A FLAG ON A PUBLISHED NUMBER, and the flag is the seventh naming of a defect this board has now carried since 8/5. The decision is right and rests on live reads: equity and option position lists both queried at 15:36 and both empty, so the hold question is answered by arithmetic rather than judgement; the earnings calendar re-pulled LIVE across 8/17 to 8/23 with none of the twelve watched names in it, so no straddle was owed and none was invented; no position opened in the last thirty minutes, which the rulebook forbids and which the entry declines without leaning on the mandate to justify acquiring a decision to make. The clock was cross-checked at venue_bid_time 19:35:49 UTC. It also carries its invalidations forward intact rather than relaxing them at a better price - SMCI is explicitly NOT carried as a live level and must be struck fresh, UPST returns only on 30.32 reclaimed and held. THE FLAG. The entry describes SMCI 38.69 bid / 38.70 ask struck at 19:35:49 UTC - twenty-four minutes before the bell - as 'the closing bid', and prices the day's headline figure off it: 7 shares at 38.24 worth 270.83, +3.15 or +1.18%. The true regular-session last trade is 38.275 at 19:59:59.93 UTC, which makes the same seven shares 267.93 and the figure +0.25 or +0.09%. The claim survives in direction and not as a closing figure, and it is off by better than an order of magnitude. The same read produced 'the dead 38.24 limit ends the day 0.46 out of reach', which reached the commit message and so git history: at the bell the final half-hour's low is 38.25 and the last trade 38.275, so the limit did stay unmarketable through the close but by about a cent rather than by forty-six. This is the identical shape the 8/13 retro flagged on the 8/13 pre-close and the 8/14 retro named a sixth time - a pre-bell read published as a settled one - and it is now a recurring defect of this slot rather than an incident. It did not change a decision and it cost nothing today: the broker returns zero orders of any kind dated 8/17, and the write-then-push window measured 2 minutes 28 seconds from quote to commit, the tightest this board has recorded against 3:09 on 8/13 and 3:53 on 8/14. The mechanical fix has been the same in all seven namings and is one line: re-read before pushing, or drop the closing claim.

entries.head: Buying 10 shares of AS at 33.86 on this morning's 100% earnings beat - the first not-forced entry in this board's recent record, and the day the option chain cleared every gate and then lost it in four minutes
entries.body: THIS IS A CLEAN ENTRY AND THE FIRST THING TO SAY ABOUT IT IS WHAT MADE IT POSSIBLE, WHICH WAS LOOKING SOMEWHERE ELSE. For five consecutive sessions item 1 has floored this board's entire field: the twelve names it re-reads every morning are all eight to ten sessions past their prints and NONE of them appears in the live 8/18-to-8/26 earnings calendar. Yesterday's entry was forced on items 1 and 5 and expired unfilled; the three before it were forced too. The drought was never going to break inside that list, so this run pulled the calendar for names that reported THIS MORNING and found AS (Amer Sports) at 0.22 EPS actual against a 0.11 estimate - a 100% beat, verified=true, reported 8/18 before the open. Item 1 passes on a dated event hours old rather than on a valuation number standing in for one. THE SPECIFICATION: BUY 10 SHARES OF AS AT A 33.86 LIMIT, 338.60 against 1009.16 settled, 33.6% of the account. Target 40.63 (+20%), stop 31.15 (-8%), time stop the 8/24 close counting today as session 1. Expires 10:30. The limit is set AT the quoted 33.86 ask rather than under it, deliberately: three of this board's last specifications expired unfilled because the limit waited for a tape that never came back, and on a five-cent spread crossing it costs 0.06 against a thesis whose entire premise is a catalyst that landed this morning. A limit at the ask is still a limit order and the rulebook's equity requirement is limit orders only. THE OPTION WAS THE REAL TEST OF THE DAY AND IT FAILED ON ITS SECOND QUOTE, WHICH IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS RUN LEARNED. Yesterday's board recorded that the three-session spread refusal was 'factually spent' after four SMCI contracts quoted inside the ceiling, and set a precedent that the first option waits for a liquid chain beside an UNFORCED thesis. Today supplies exactly that: the thesis is unforced and the AS 2026-09-18 32.5 call quoted 2.25/2.40 at 13:43:58Z - a 6.45% spread against a 10% ceiling, 0.638 delta against a 0.40 floor, 7,770 open interest, 31 days to expiry inside the 3-6 week band, and no earnings inside that window, confirmed by searching all 799 events on the live 8/19-to-9/18 calendar and finding no AS. That is the first contract in this project's history to clear every mechanical gate simultaneously with the precedent's own condition met. Four minutes later, at 13:47:29Z, the IDENTICAL contract quoted 2.25/2.75 - a 20.0% spread, exactly double the ceiling. THE CONTRACT WAS REFUSED, AND SO WAS THE ONE THAT STILL CLEARED. The 9/18 35 call reads 1.25/1.35, a 7.69% spread on 0.431 delta with 29,022 open interest, and it passes every stated gate. It is refused anyway, on three numbers: its neighbour just demonstrated that this book can double its own spread inside four minutes, and a book that is 20% wide is a book that will not be there at the -40% stop, which is the exact moment it is needed; the 36.30 break-even requires +7.0% on the underlying by 9/18; and theta of -0.029 against a 1.30 premium is 2.2% of the position per day, roughly 11% across a five-session hold. Equity on the same name quotes 0.148%. The instrument decision was made by the second quote and not the first, which is the whole reason the rulebook says pull the chain and quote the bid rather than assume. WHAT I AM CONCEDING ON THE EQUITY, BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST HALF: a +20% take-profit on a 19.4B consumer-durables name inside five sessions is not realistically reachable, so this position will almost certainly be closed by the time stop or the stop rather than by the target, and the target is close to decorative. That asymmetry was the strongest argument FOR the option - a 0.64-delta call reaches +20% on about +2.2% of underlying, a level this stock already traded at 34.6974 this morning - and it lost to the spread evidence above. A grader should know the trade-off was priced rather than missed. THE CHECKLIST, IN ORDER. (1) CATALYST - PASS. Reported 8/18 am, 0.22 against 0.11, a 100% beat, verified on the live calendar, hours old. (2) NOT THE +8% DAY - PASS. +3.81% at the bid against the 32.57 official close, on a session that opened 33.84, ran to 34.6974, fell to 33.41 and came back to 33.81. Not a spike. The deviation I am NOT hiding: the rulebook's 'setups that fit' names post-earnings day-TWO continuation and this is day one, so the preferred entry is tomorrow's or Thursday's pullback rather than this. It is bought today because the daily entry mandate binds this slot and because the alternative field is eleven red names with no catalyst among them. No checklist item fails on it, and a grader should still mark the timing against this entry. (3) IMPLIED MOVE - 'na', and the reasoning is logged rather than the item skipped. The rule triggers before an earnings HOLD; this print is BEHIND rather than ahead, and searching all 799 events on the live 8/19-to-9/18 calendar returns no AS, so no print lands inside a five-session hold. No straddle was owed and none was invented. (4) LIQUIDITY - PASS. 19.44B market cap, 4.85M thirty-day average volume, 2.33M shares already traded by 09:44, and a 33.81/33.86 quote which is a 0.148% spread. (5) EXPECTATIONS VS POSITIONING - PASS, AND THIS GRADE MOVED DURING THE RUN, WHICH IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY SETTLED. At 09:42 AS was 33.68 bid having faded from 34.6974, and this run provisionally marked item 5 FAIL on the sell-the-news signature of a 100% beat round-tripping its gap. At 09:46 it printed 33.93, the dip bought, and the grade was revised to PASS. What decides it is the thing item 5 actually asks about, which is positioning INTO the print: AS fell from 36.17 on 8/10 to 32.57 on 8/17, five red sessions and -10.0%, bottoming at 32.08 yesterday. That is a de-risked name, not crowded bulls with raised targets, so the precondition the item warns about is absent - and the realised reaction is a name holding +3.8% on a morning when eleven of twelve names on this board are red. I am aware that revising a fail to a pass is the direction that flatters the entry, which is why both prints and both timestamps are written here. (6) EXITS - PASS. Target 40.63, stop 31.15, time stop the 8/24 close, all struck off the 33.86 limit before entry and all written above. WHY AS AND NOT THE ALTERNATIVES, RANKED. KLAR beat this morning too, at 0.01 against -0.06, and is -19.27%: not bought, because the first print of a 19% gap is not a support level and no rulebook setup covers it - it is kept on the board precisely as the counterexample that stops item 1 decaying into 'a number came out'. BIDU missed at 1.06 against 1.35 and is -8.66%, a dated catalyst that resolved against the name. SMCI, at 37.35, is 0.89 below yesterday's expired limit and is NOT revived cheaper - a lower price does not supply the catalyst item 1 wanted, and the 8/11 print is now five sessions back; had it filled, seven shares would be -6.23 today, the first print in seven where the refusal saved money and it is recorded with the same weight as the six that went the other way. UPST, IONQ, RGTI, SOUN, OKLO, SMR and JOBY are all eight to ten sessions past their prints with nothing dated ahead, and all are red today. AMD is refused mechanically at 48.2% of the account against the 40% ceiling. THE TAPE THIS IS BEING BOUGHT INTO, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS THE MAIN RISK. Eleven of twelve names on this board are red at 13:48:32 UTC, with AMD -3.98%, OKLO -4.72% and BIDU -8.66%. Buying anything on a morning like this carries the risk that a market-wide down day drags a good name with it regardless of its news. The argument for doing it anyway is that AS is green on a company-specific event rather than on the tape, which is the one kind of relative strength that is not the chase the rulebook names under 'does not fit' - but if the broad tape keeps selling, the 31.15 stop is what settles the question rather than this paragraph. WHAT WOULD TELL ME THIS IS WRONG, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME. A close back below 32.57, the pre-print close, means the entire beat has been given back and the thesis is void regardless of where the stop sits. Failure to hold above the 33.41 session low on any pullback today is the earlier warning. And if five sessions pass with AS between 33 and 35, the time stop closes it on 8/24 at whatever it is - the thesis was that a 100% beat on a de-risked name moves it, and a name that does not move has answered.
