entries.head: A limit struck AT the ask to stop it expiring unfilled is six cents under the market ninety minutes later - and it is still not raised
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 10:22 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 14:22:37.700 UTC against a local 10:22 ET, the -4 EDT offset assumed.

THE ONE THING THIS HOUR HAD TO LOOK AT. The open published 10 shares of AS at a 33.86 limit and set that limit AT the quoted ask on purpose, naming the three prior specifications that expired unfilled because their limits sat under the market waiting for a tape that never came back. AS is now 33.90 bid / 33.92 ask. The ask is 0.06 ABOVE the limit, so the order does not fill at this quote, and it has 8 minutes left before it expires at 10:30.

THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE MODE ARRIVING FROM THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, WHICH IS WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY. The three earlier specifications died because the price fell away from them. This one is failing because the price ROSE away from it - the thesis was right for ninety minutes and the entry still may not get filled. A limit at the ask is not a guarantee of a fill; it is a guarantee of a fill only against the quote it was struck on. Nothing about that was hidden at 09:49 and nothing about it is a surprise now, but four consecutive specifications going unfilled for two opposite reasons says the problem is the human execution gap this board runs on, not the width of the limit.

IT IS NOT RAISED, AND THE PRECEDENT IS EXACT RATHER THAN ANALOGOUS. On 8/17 at 11:21 the SMCI tape ran away from a 38.24 limit and this board refused to raise it; the reasoning was that re-striking is a NEW mid-session entry, held to a HIGHER bar than the open, and that a specification expires on its own written terms. Chasing AS six cents higher because it went up is the definition of the chase the rulebook names under 'does not fit', and the fact that the underlying thesis is this board's best in weeks is exactly what makes the temptation worth refusing on the record. The daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:49.

THE DEAD SMCI LIMIT IS TESTED A SEVENTH TIME AND THE GENEROSITY OF THE TEST IS THE POINT. The 37.19 ask sits 1.05 BELOW the expired 38.24 limit, against the 0.04, 0.21 and 0.17 of yesterday's three tests - that order would now fill a full dollar better than it asked. A rule that holds when it is refused by four cents and breaks when it is refused by a dollar is a rule about the size of the temptation rather than about the reasoning, so the answer is unchanged: expired by its own terms, thesis forced on items 1 and 5, print six sessions back, absent from the live calendar. Had it filled, seven shares would read 260.19 against 267.68, -7.49 or -2.80%: the worst of eight recorded prints, and the second running in which the refusal is what saved money. That is recorded with the same weight as the six prints where it cost money.

NOTHING ELSE WAS DONE. No new entry is proposed and none is owed - the standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, and a flat book is not an argument for filling it. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist for the session, so nothing was executed by anyone and agentTrades is unchanged at 0. Balances were pulled live rather than derived: 1009.16, all settled, nothing unsettled.
entries.grade: PASS. Both position lists queried live at 10:22 rather than inherited, the clock cross-checked against venue_bid_time, and the day's one live specification re-quoted at 33.90/33.92 - the ask six cents ABOVE its own limit with eight minutes to live - and correctly NOT raised, on a precedent cited exactly rather than by analogy. The entry also names the failure mode arriving from the opposite direction to the three prior expiries, which is a genuine finding rather than a restatement. The dead SMCI 38.24 was refused on a test that had grown to a full dollar of generosity, on the stated ground that a rule which holds at four cents and breaks at a dollar is a rule about the size of the temptation, and the money the refusal SAVED was logged at the same weight as the six prints where refusing cost money. WHAT A GRADER CAN HOLD AGAINST IT IS NOT A RULE BREACH AND IS NOT MARKED AS ONE: with the specification eight minutes from death and six cents from filling, nobody outside a git commit knew it existed, and this run did not say so. The notification duty did not exist at 10:21 - it arrives in today's rule change, which the runs first cite at 13:21 - so it is not graded a failure here. It is the gap that change was written to close, observed one hour before the change closed it.

entries.head: The specification expired unfilled at 10:30, and an hour later the name it would not chase is 1.8% below the limit that would not chase it
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 11:22 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 15:22:47.829 UTC against a local 11:22 ET, the -4 EDT offset assumed.

THE SPECIFICATION IS DEAD, AND THE BROKER IS THE ONE SAYING SO. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist in this account for the whole session, queried live with a created_at floor of 2026-08-18. The 10 shares of AS at a 33.86 limit published at 09:49 were never executed by anyone, nothing partially filled, and the order expired at 10:30 on its own written terms. That is the FOURTH consecutive specification this board has published and watched expire - JOBY at 8.85, SMCI at 38.24 twice, now AS at 33.86 - and the count is the finding rather than any single one of them. Four published theses, four unexecuted, agentTrades still 0. A process whose output nobody executes is not being tested, whatever its reasoning looks like.

THE ONE DECISION THIS SLOT MADE LAST HOUR HAS ALREADY BEEN PRICED. At 10:22 AS was 33.90 bid / 33.92 ask, six cents through the limit with eight minutes to live, and this run refused to raise it - on the ground that chasing six cents is a NEW mid-session entry held to a higher bar, and that the identical raise was refused on 8/17. AS is now 33.29 bid / 33.31 ask on a 0.06% spread, last trade 33.300. It is DOWN 0.61 or 1.80% from that ask inside one hour, and +2.21% against the 32.57 close where it had been +4.08%. Raised and filled at 33.92, the position would be 1.86% underwater right now. Filled at the original 33.86, the ten shares that cost 338.60 would read 332.90 - minus 5.70, or 1.68%.

WHAT THAT IS AND WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not proof the rule is right. One session's tape paying a refusal is not evidence about refusals in general, and this board has six recorded prints in the other direction where not filling cost it money - the JOBY entry that expired and would have been green is the cleanest of them. It is recorded here at exactly the weight those six were given, which is the only reason it is worth writing down at all. The honest version: the reasoning at 10:21 did not predict this, it declined to chase, and declining to chase is a policy whose payoff is only visible across a sample this board does not yet have.

AS IS NOT RE-STRUCK CHEAPER, AND THE ARGUMENT AGAINST IT IS ONE THIS BOARD HAS ALREADY MADE SEVEN TIMES ABOUT ANOTHER NAME. The name now sits 0.57 BELOW the limit that expired, the most marketable a dead AS level has been. The SMCI 38.24 has been refused on every one of its eight tests on the principle that a specification which expired by its own terms is not restored by the tape reaching it, and that generosity is not a catalyst. Applying that to SMCI and not to AS would make the principle a preference. Beyond consistency, the substance is worse here than it looks: this would be a NEW mid-session entry, which the rulebook holds to a HIGHER bar than the open, into a day-1 post-earnings name that is actively fading its own gap. Buying the giveback on print day is not a setup in this book. The day-2 or day-3 pullback it does prefer cannot exist before tomorrow, and if AS is still worth owning it will be ownable then on a level struck after the fade rather than during it.

THE REST OF THE BOARD, FOR COMPLETENESS. SMCI 36.42 bid / 36.43 ask, a 0.027% spread and the tightest quote here, -4.86% against the 38.28 close; the ask is 1.81 below the dead 38.24, against 1.05 an hour ago and 0.04 on its first test. Seven shares filled there for 267.68 would read 254.94, minus 12.74 or 4.76% - the worst of the nine prints in that series. Its thesis is still forced on items 1 and 5, the 8/11 print is six sessions back, and SMCI is absent from the live 8/18-to-8/26 calendar. KLAR 15.45 bid / 15.46 ask, -20.81% against the 19.51 close and below the 15.69 read an hour ago: still making session lows, still no base, still not a setup and still the live counterexample sitting beside today's AS thesis - two EPS beats printed this morning, one is +2.2% and one is -20.8%.

NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text - discharged at 09:49 with a specification that was not forced. Balances are 1009.16 total, all cash, fully settled with nothing unsettled and no pending deposits, unchanged from the 09:43 and 10:22 reads because nothing has traded. Actions 0; this run has no order authority and placed nothing.
entries.grade: PASS, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST OF THE SIX. The specification's death is established from the broker's own order record on a created_at floor - zero equity orders, zero option orders, nothing partially filled - rather than from the log or from the previous run's account of itself, which is the reconciliation direction this board is supposed to work in. The count is named as the finding rather than the single order: four published theses, four unexecuted, agentTrades still 0. Levels verify against live quotes and both position lists were queried at 11:22. The decisive paragraph is the one grading its own refusal: it states plainly that one session's tape paying a refusal is NOT evidence about refusals in general, that six recorded prints run the other way, and that the JOBY entry which expired and would have been green is the cleanest of them - then declines to re-strike AS cheaper on the same principle that has refused SMCI eight times, with the explicit reason that applying it to one name and not the other would make the principle a preference. That is the outcome-blind discipline this slot exists to impose, written by the run against itself before any grader arrived.

entries.head: No exit is due against a flat book, and the specification that expired at 10:30 stays expired - today's wider window is for specifications written under it, not a way to reopen one that already died
entries.body: NOTHING IS HELD, SO NO LEVEL COULD BE HIT THIS HOUR. Equity positions and option positions were both queried live against the mandate account and both lists are empty. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window reachable. This is the exits slot reporting an empty book, not a slot that skipped its levels. THE RE-VALIDATION DUTY FOUND NOTHING TO RE-VALIDATE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Today's rule change gives a specification life until 15:30 ET and obliges every hourly to re-quote each open one and either confirm or kill it. This run looked: the only 'will' entry dated today is the 09:49 AS specification, and it carried expiresAt 10:30 because it was written before the window widened. It expired on its own terms and the 11:21 run confirmed it dead against zero equity orders and zero option orders in the account for the entire session. IT IS NOT REVIVED, AND THE REASON IS WORTH WRITING DOWN BECAUSE THE TEMPTATION IS NEW TODAY. A rule that extends the life of specifications arrives on the same day as a specification that just died forty minutes into its life, six cents from filling, the fourth consecutive entry to expire unexecuted. The obvious move is to notice that under this morning's new rule it would still be alive, and to treat it as alive. That is not what the rule says and it is not what it is for. The window was widened for specifications written under it, on quotes reasoned inside it. Reaching back to re-open an expired one is re-striking a dead level in the time dimension rather than the price dimension, and this board has refused the price version of that move more often than any other. Widening the time is not permission to widen the time retroactively either. AS WAS RE-QUOTED REGARDLESS. 33.24 bid / 33.26 ask at 17:23:10 UTC, a 0.06% spread, +2.06% on the day against the 32.57 close. The dead limit was 33.86, so the name trades 0.62 - 1.83% - BELOW the level this board would not chase at 10:21 and would not chase at 11:21. Three hours later the refusal still costs nothing, which is not proof it was right but is the only evidence available. The limit stays where it was struck and is not raised. NO NEW ENTRY. The daily entry mandate applies to the open slot, which discharged it cleanly at 09:49 with the first not-forced entry in this board's recent record. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design, and a flat book at 13:21 with one name already published and already expired is not a reason to publish a second. ONE RUN-HEALTH FACT, RECORDED NOW RATHER THAN DISCOVERED IN THE RETRO: the 12:17 slot has no row. It was scheduled and it did not fire. That is the known desktop-scheduler failure mode - the task runs only while the operator's app is open - and it means the specification window between 11:21 and 13:21 went two hours without the hourly re-check the new rule depends on. Today that cost nothing, because the specification in question was already dead before the gap opened. On a day when one is live it would matter, and the rule that a specification nobody re-checked is dead by neglect is only as good as the scheduler underneath it.
entries.grade: PASS, AND ON THE HARDEST TEST THE DAY OFFERED. The re-validation duty was discharged by looking rather than by asserting, and the temptation it refused was the sharpest available: a rule widening specification life to 15:30 arrived on the same day as a specification that died at 10:30, forty minutes into its life, six cents from filling. Treating it as alive under the new rule would have been the obvious move and this run named it as such and refused, on the ground that widening the time is not permission to widen it retroactively, and that reaching back to reopen an expired level is the time-dimension version of the price-dimension chase this board has refused more often than anything else. It then RE-QUOTED the dead level anyway at 33.24/33.26 rather than treating deadness as a reason to stop looking. AND IT REPORTED THE MISSED 12:17 SLOT IN ITS OWN BODY rather than leaving the retro to discover it - correctly, including the part that does not flatter it: the two-hour gap in the hourly re-check cost nothing today only because the specification was already dead before the gap opened, and on a day when one is live it would matter. A run that logs the scheduler hole it did not cause, and states the condition under which it would have been serious, is doing the job this file exists for.

No notification is sent because nothing was published, nothing was killed, no spec is in its last hour, the guard was cleared, and no level was hit and left unacted.
entries.grade: PASS. Both position lists queried live at 14:22, the staleness guard measured against a broker-confirmed offset, and the re-validation duty discharged with the correct finding that nothing was open to discharge it on. The substantive work is the third geometry of the same refusal inside one session: the tape ran six cents THROUGH the limit at 10:22, sat 0.57 and 0.62 BENEATH it at 11:22 and 13:21, and is now closing on it FROM BELOW - and it is still not revived, on the principle that an expired specification is not restored by the tape approaching from any side. WHAT EARNS THE GRADE IS THE SELF-AUDIT ATTACHED TO IT: the cost of the 10:21 refusal was logged on the specific hour it moved AGAINST the refusal, narrowing from -1.68% to -1.09%, with the stated reason that a board recording the cost of its discipline only while that cost is shrinking is keeping a scoreboard rather than a record. Applying the board's own standard in the unflattering direction, unprompted, is exactly what an outcome-blind record requires and is rarer than the reasoning that surrounds it.

entries.head: No exit is due against a flat book, and on the last hourly of the day AS has given back the whole afternoon recovery to trade below the session low its own entry named this morning as the early warning
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 15:22 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. Fired 15:21 against the 15:17 slot, four minutes late, inside the 20-minute guard; venue_bid_time reads 19:22:50.310 UTC against a local 15:21 ET, confirming the -4 EDT offset the guard was measured with.

THE RE-VALIDATION DUTY IS DISCHARGED FOR THE LAST TIME TODAY AND FINDS NOTHING OPEN TO DISCHARGE IT ON. The only 'will' entry dated today carried expiresAt 10:30 and died there against a broker showing zero orders for the session. The 13:21 run settled that today's wider 15:30 window does not reach backwards, and nothing has been published since. So no specification was confirmed, none was killed, and none is in its last hour because none is open. This matters more than it reads: the whole point of widening the window to 15:30 was to create a standing proposal the operator could act on through the afternoon, and that window now closes in eight minutes with nothing in it. The first session under the new rule produced a specification that died at 10:30 under the old one.

THE FINDING OF THE HOUR IS THAT THE AS INVALIDATION, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME, HAS TRIGGERED ON ITS EARLIER CONDITION. AS is 33.01 bid / 33.03 ask at 19:22:50.310Z on a 0.06% spread, last trade 33.020, +1.35% on the bid against the 32.57 close. This morning's entry wrote down two things that would tell it the thesis was wrong: a close back below the 32.57 pre-print close voids it entirely, and 'failure to hold above the 33.41 session low on any pullback today is the earlier warning'. AS is trading 33.02. The earlier warning has triggered. The later condition has not, and the name is still green on the day. That distinction is the whole value of having written both down in advance instead of deciding after the fact which one counted.

THE AFTERNOON RECOVERY IS FULLY REVERSED, AND THE SIX-READ SERIES IS THE CLEAREST WAY TO SAY IT. Bids at 33.81 (09:48), 33.90 (10:22), 33.29 (11:22), 33.24 (13:21), 33.49 (14:22) and 33.01 now - down 0.48 or 1.43% in the hour and the lowest of the six. The 33.03 ask is 0.83 BELOW the dead 33.86 limit, the widest that gap has been all day against 0.35 an hour ago. So the fourth geometry the level has been tested in today is just the second one reopening, wider. It is not revived, at any distance, from any direction, and the reason has not changed since 10:21: a specification that expired on its own written terms is not restored by the tape.

THE COST OF THE 10:21 REFUSAL MOVED BACK IN ITS FAVOUR THIS HOUR, AND IT IS LOGGED AT EXACTLY THE WEIGHT THE HOUR IT MOVED AGAINST IT WAS LOGGED. Ten shares filled at 33.86 for 338.60 would read 330.10 now - minus 8.50, or 2.51% - against the 1.09% recorded at 14:22 and the 1.68% at 11:22. That is the worst print of the series and the most the refusal has been paid today; a limit raised to 33.92 as the tape invited at 10:22 would be 2.68% underwater. An hour ago this board wrote that number down while it was narrowing against its own discipline, on the stated ground that a record which only reports the cost of discipline while that cost is shrinking is a scoreboard rather than a record. The same standard applies in the flattering direction: this is one session's tape paying a refusal, it is not evidence about refusals in general, and the six recorded prints where not filling COST money still stand beside it unchanged.

NO NEW ENTRY, AND THIS HOUR THE TAPE MAKES THE DEFAULT EASIER RATHER THAN HARDER. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, the mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text - discharged at 09:49 with the first not-forced entry in this board's recent record. Beyond all of that: the single name here carrying a live catalyst is making session lows thirty-eight minutes from the bell, and buying the giveback of a day-1 gap into the close is not a setup this rulebook contains. The day-2 pullback it does prefer is tomorrow's decision, made on tomorrow's quotes, by tomorrow's open.

SMCI TESTED A TENTH TIME, STILL DEAD: 37.47 bid / 37.48 ask at 19:22:51.411Z, a 0.03% spread and again the tightest quote on the board, -2.12% against the 38.28 close. The ask is 0.76 below the expired 38.24 limit. Its thesis is still forced on items 1 and 5, the 8/11 print is six sessions back, and SMCI is absent from the live 8/18-to-8/26 calendar. Seven shares at 38.24 for 267.68 would read 262.29, minus 5.39 or 2.01%.

KLAR IS STILL MAKING SESSION LOWS AND IS STILL NOT BOUGHT: 15.12 bid / 15.13 ask at 19:22:46.864Z, -22.50% against the 19.51 close, below both the 15.21 read at 14:22 and the 15.75 the open read. Six hours after the print the gap has not begun to base, which is the precondition any setup here would need. The counterexample it is kept on the board for has sharpened once more - two EPS beats printed this morning, one is +1.4% and one is -22.5%.

BALANCES LIVE, NOT DERIVED: 1009.16 total, all cash, zero equity and zero options value, zero pending deposits, ZERO unsettled. Unchanged from the 09:43, 10:22, 11:22 and 14:22 reads because nothing has traded. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist for the entire session, queried with a created_at floor of 2026-08-18, so nothing was executed or partially filled by anyone and agentTrades stays 0. Actions 0; this run has no order authority and placed nothing. No notification is sent because nothing was published, nothing was killed, no specification is open let alone in its last hour, the guard was cleared, and no level was hit and left unacted.
entries.grade: PASS. The finding of the hour is the one that only exists because two levels were written down BEFORE the outcome: the earlier invalidation - failure to hold above the 33.41 session low - triggered at 33.02, and the later one - a close back below the 32.57 pre-print close - did not. The run keeps that distinction rather than collapsing it into a verdict, which is the entire value of having written both in advance instead of deciding afterwards which one counted. Positions queried live at 15:22, the six-read bid series published in full so the reversal is legible rather than asserted, and the dead limit refused at the widest gap it had all day. SYMMETRY HONOURED WITHOUT BEING ASKED: one hour after logging the cost of its refusal while that cost was narrowing against it, this run logged the worst print of the series - -8.50 or -2.51% - and restated that this is one session's tape and not evidence about refusals, with the six contrary prints left standing beside it unchanged. It also names the thing that most undercuts today's rule change: the window widened to 15:30 closed in eight minutes with nothing standing in it.

entries.head: Flat into the bell, and that is the decision rather than the leftover - nothing to exit, nothing to hold, and the 15:30 window closed with nothing standing in it
entries.body:
THE OVERNIGHT HOLD DECISION IS ANSWERED BY AN EMPTY BOOK, AND THE BOOK WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 15:36 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. The portfolio reads 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits and zero unsettled. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 19:37:21.420 UTC against a local 15:35 ET, the -4 EDT offset the staleness guard was measured with. Fired two minutes after the 15:33 slot, twenty minutes clear of the 15:55 cutoff.

EVERY STEP-2 QUESTION WAS ASKED AND EACH IS RECORDED, BECAUSE A HOLD WITH NO ENTRY IN THE LOG IS AN ACCIDENT THAT HAPPENED TO WORK. Is an option no-fly window closing today - no, because no option is held, and none can be reached. Is anything printing tonight that this board is exposed to - no, because nothing is held into any print, so no straddle is owed and none is claimed. Has a target, stop or time stop been hit - none exists to hit. And the fourth: what is being held overnight, and why. NOTHING IS. That is not the absence of a decision, it is the decision, and it is the one the tape argued for all afternoon.

NOTHING SURVIVED THE BELL BECAUSE NOTHING WAS STILL ALIVE TO SURVIVE IT. Today's only 'will' entry - 10 shares of AS at a 33.86 limit, published 09:49 - carried expiresAt 2026-08-18 10:30 and expired there unexecuted. The 11:21 run appended its 'did' against a broker showing zero orders for the session, and the 13:21 run settled that today's wider 15:30 window does not reach backwards to revive an order that had already died. So this slot found no unexpired specification: none to expire, none to kill, none to carry. Re-verified now - ZERO equity orders and ZERO option orders exist in this account for the entire session, agentTrades unchanged at 0. The closing number is put beside the dead limit so the record shows how it finished rather than only how close it came at 10:30: AS is 33.26 bid against a 33.86 limit, 0.58 or 1.71% beneath it.

IT IS NOT RE-STRUCK FOR TOMORROW, AND THIS IS THE FIFTH DIRECTION THE SAME REFUSAL HAS BEEN TESTED IN TODAY. Raised when the tape ran six cents through it at 10:22; refused. Cut when the tape sat 0.57 and 0.62 beneath it at 11:22 and 13:21; refused. Revived when the tape closed back toward it from below at 14:22; refused. Refused again at 15:22 at the widest gap of the day. And refused now as a carry into tomorrow, which is the one that matters most, because a specification carried overnight is a standing instruction resting on a tape that no longer exists. Tomorrow's open writes tomorrow's entry on tomorrow's quotes.

THE INVALIDATION THIS BOARD WROTE BEFORE THE OUTCOME IS STILL TRIGGERED AT THE CLOSE, AND THAT IS WHAT TOMORROW INHERITS. The 09:49 entry named two levels in advance. The earlier - failure to hold above the 33.41 session low - triggered at 15:22 and has NOT been repaired: AS is 33.26, still beneath it, despite recovering 0.25 off the 33.01 low read. The later - a close back below the 32.57 pre-print close, which voids the thesis outright - did NOT trigger, and AS finishes green at +2.12%. So the honest summary of the day's one thesis is that it half-broke: the beat was real, the gap faded most of the way, and the level that would have said abandon it entirely was never reached. A day-2 entry tomorrow is therefore reachable but not owed, and it will be struck on tomorrow's quotes against a written invalidation of its own or not at all.

SMCI AND KLAR CLOSE THE DAY WHERE THEY HAVE SPENT IT. SMCI is 37.50 bid / 37.52 ask, -2.03% against the 38.28 close, an eleventh test of the dead 38.24 limit and 0.72 beneath it. Marketable, as on most tests, and no more meaningful for it: the thesis is forced on items 1 and 5, the 8/11 print is six sessions back, and SMCI is absent from the live 8/18-to-8/26 calendar. Had seven shares filled at 38.24 for 267.68 they would read 262.50, -5.18 or -1.94%. KLAR is 15.12 bid / 15.13 ask, -22.50%, closing on its lows six hours after an EPS beat. No base has formed, which is the precondition any entry here would need, and the counterexample it is kept on the board for closes as sharply as it opened: two beats this morning, one +2.1% and one -22.5%.

NO POSITION IS OPENED, AND THAT IS MECHANICAL RATHER THAN A VIEW. The pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text, which discharged it at 09:49 with the first not-forced entry in this board's recent record. The mandate is not a quota this slot inherits when the open's order fails to fill.

THE CATALYST LIST WAS PRUNED AGAINST A LIVE CALENDAR AND IS NO LONGER EMPTY. Nothing was removed - there were no rows to remove - but the pull found that AS, KLAR and BIDU printed this morning and are behind rather than ahead, and that not one of the twelve watched names has a dated event in the 8/18-to-8/26 window. It also found NVDA on 2026-08-26 after the close, verified, six sessions out. That row was ADDED with spot pulled live in the same call as every other quote here, because AMD sits on this board's candidate list and the 2026-08-10 rule change was written specifically about a correlated AI complex that gaps together; a file titled what is ahead cannot be empty when the largest dated event in that complex is six sessions out. impliedMove is null deliberately - no straddle was pulled, nothing is held into that print, and a straddle quoted six sessions early is not the number that will govern on 8/25. Both branches carry their reasoning and are decided now rather than on the day.

NO NOTIFICATION IS SENT, AND THE RULE SAYS SO RATHER THAN THIS RUN DECIDING SO. No exit is due, no option no-fly window closes today, nothing is held overnight, this run did not decline, and the staleness guard was cleared with twenty minutes in hand. The notification rule exists because four consecutive specifications expired unseen - it is a gate for things that need acting on, and it is degraded, not honoured, by a ping that says nothing happened.
entries.grade: PASS ON THE DECISION, WITH A FLAG ON A PUBLISHED NUMBER, AND THE FLAG IS NOW EIGHT SESSIONS OLD. On the decision: all four step-2 questions were asked and each is answered in the log rather than assumed, both position lists were queried live at 15:36, the flat book is recorded as a DECISION rather than a leftover, and the refusal to carry the dead 33.86 into tomorrow is named as the fifth geometry of the same refusal with the reason that a specification carried overnight is a standing instruction resting on a tape that no longer exists. The written-in-advance invalidation is re-checked at the bell and reported half-broken rather than resolved in either direction, which is the honest reading. THE FLAG: this entry publishes a 19:37:21Z BID of 33.26 as the day's closing number and prices the miss at 0.58 or 1.71% beneath the limit, and the state.json this slot also wrote carries the cost of the 10:21 refusal at -5.90 or -1.74%. The regular-session last trade at 15:59:59 ET is 33.64, which makes those figures 0.22, 0.65%, -2.20 and -0.65% - the miss SAVED 2.20 rather than costing 5.90. The number was pulled live and labelled a bid at a stated timestamp, so this is not an invented figure and the grade is unchanged; but a bid taken twenty-five minutes before the bell is not a close, and this is the eighth consecutive session on which that substitution has been named here. The error runs in the direction that flatters the board's own discipline, which is the direction a record should be slowest to accept.

entries.head: Day-2 continuation in AS at 33.87 for 11 shares, six of six and not forced - and the option that finally cleared every gate in the rulebook is refused anyway, because its spread went 1.94% to 9.71% in 82 seconds
entries.body:
THE ENTRY. Buy 11 shares of AS at a 33.87 limit, 372.57 or 36.9% of a 1009.16 account, target 40.64, stop 31.16, time stop the 8/25 close counting today as session 1. Not forced: items 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 pass and item 3 is not applicable. The quotes behind this limit were pulled at 09:46 ET - 33.82 bid / 33.87 ask, a 0.148% spread - and specStruckAt records that, because under the 15:30 window a fill at 14:00 is not the entry this reasoning describes and the grader needs the gap.

THE SETUP IS THE ONE THIS RULEBOOK NAMES FIRST AND HAS NEVER ACTUALLY BOUGHT. Post-earnings day-2 continuation heads the setups-that-fit list. AS reported 8/18 before the open at 0.22 EPS against a 0.11 estimate - a 100% beat, verified on the live calendar, one session old. Yesterday it gapped to 33.84, ran to 34.6974, gave the whole gap back to 33.41, and closed 33.62, up 3.22% on the day. Today it opened 33.85, made 34.47, and has pulled back to 33.88 last. That is the shape the rulebook prefers: the spike happened, the fade happened, the close held, and the day-2 entry is struck on the pullback rather than on the high. Yesterday's open flagged its own day-1 timing as the weakest part of that entry. Today that objection is spent.

A CORRECTION THAT HAD TO COME BEFORE THE ENTRY, BECAUSE IT IS THE REASON THE ENTRY IS ALLOWED AT ALL. Yesterday's pre-close recorded that the AS invalidation - failure to hold above the 33.41 session low - had triggered and was NOT repaired into the bell, and state.json carries that sentence. It was measured on a 33.26 bid timestamped 19:37:21Z, twenty-three minutes before the close. THE OFFICIAL SETTLED CLOSE IS 33.62, ABOVE 33.41. The written invalidation did not trigger. The 8/18 retro flagged this bid-for-close substitution as eight sessions old and running in the direction that flatters the board's own discipline; this is the first time it has been caught BEFORE being acted on rather than after. Had it been inherited unexamined, today's run would have refused a name whose thesis was intact on the record it wrote in advance. Both of yesterday's levels are therefore intact: the 33.41 earlier warning held at the close, and the 32.57 outright-void level was never approached.

THE OPTION CLEARED EVERY GATE AND IS STILL REFUSED, ON A GROUND THIS BOARD HAS NOT USED BEFORE. The AS 2026-09-18 32.50 call, contract 3f45eefe-f68a-4d5c-8c67-44d10bb026e1, quoted 2.55 bid / 2.60 ask at 13:45:01.722Z: a 1.94% spread against a 10% ceiling, delta 0.6716 against a 0.40 floor, 7,857 open interest, 30 days to expiry inside the 3-6 week window, no print between here and expiration, and 260.00 a contract against 1009.16 deployable. That is every option requirement in docs/RULES.md met outright, by margin, for the first time in this board's record - the affordability half of the 2026-08-05 size finding and the spread half answered in the same quote. IT IS REFUSED ANYWAY. At 13:46:23.355Z, 82 seconds later, the same contract quoted 2.45 / 2.70 - a 9.71% spread, five times wider, still technically inside the ceiling and plainly not the same market. Yesterday the same strike went 6.45% to 20.0% in four minutes. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES IS THE SECOND ONE, NOT THE FIRST: a spread that quintuples inside 82 seconds is not a 1.94% spread that moved, it is an unstable quote that happened to be tight when it was looked at, and the 10% ceiling exists to make a fill land near the mark. Under the old 30-60 minute fuse a tight read was worth something because execution was minutes away. Under the 15:30 window execution may be five hours away, so quote instability is a materially worse defect today than it was on 8/17 - the cost of the window widening turning up in a place the rule change did not anticipate. Equity on the same name at the same instant quoted 0.05 on 33.845, 0.148%. Numbers over narrative cuts against the exciting finding here, not for it.

WHAT IS GIVEN UP BY REFUSING IT, STATED SO THE RETRO CAN PRICE IT. At delta 0.66 the contract reaches a +20% premium target on roughly a 2.3% move in AS, about 34.65, which is inside yesterday's range. The equity's +20% target of 40.64 requires a 20% move in five sessions, which this rulebook's own section 5 says the setups it buys do not typically deliver - so the honest expectation for the equity leg is that the TIME STOP fires before the target does. That asymmetry is real and it favours the option. It loses to the spread instability, and it loses on risk as well: a -40% option stop puts 104.00 at risk against the equity stop's 29.85, and that option stop corresponds to roughly a 4.5% move in AS, inside a name that ranged 3.8% yesterday. The option would very likely have stopped out on noise.

ITEM 5 PASSES ON EVIDENCE STANDING ON TODAY'S OWN TAPE RATHER THAN ON ASSERTION. AS went into the print de-risked, not crowded: five red sessions and -10.0% from 36.17 on 8/10 to the 32.08 low on 8/17. The live control group is this morning. TJX beat at 1.22 against 1.19 and is 148.73 bid, -1.4%. ADI beat at 3.45 against 3.34 and is 373.44 bid, -0.85%. KEYS beat at 3.07 against 2.42, a 27% beat, and is 332.36 bid, -2.5%. Three beats sold off on the same tape on which AS, two sessions off a 100% beat, is green. That is exactly the mechanism item 5 describes - a merely-good report selling off into raised expectations - firing on three names and not on this one.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME AND CHECKABLE BY A RUN THAT WAS NOT HERE AT 09:49. Two levels, in order. THE EARLIER WARNING: a trade below 33.70, today's session low. That low is the higher-low the day-2 structure rests on, and losing it means the continuation failed on the day it was bought. THE OUTRIGHT VOID: a close below 33.41, yesterday's session low - the level that survived yesterday and whose survival is the entire reason this entry exists. If 33.41 goes on a closing basis the day-2 thesis is not weakened, it is wrong, and the position comes off without waiting for the 31.16 stop. NOTE THE STRUCTURE DELIBERATELY: both invalidations sit ABOVE the mechanical stop, so on this entry the thesis is built to break before the stop does and the exit should come from the written level rather than from the stop. An hourly run re-reading this at 13:00 needs only the tape and these three numbers.

THE AWKWARD COINCIDENCE, NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT FOR A GRADER TO FIND. Today's 33.87 limit is one cent above the 33.86 limit this board published yesterday and refused to revive from four directions across the session. It is not a revival. Yesterday's specification expired on its own written terms at 10:30 and stays expired; this is a new entry, on a new day, with a new thesis - day-2 rather than day-1 - new exits, new invalidation levels and a new expiry, struck on quotes pulled at 09:46 today. The prohibition this board takes most seriously is that a limit may never be RAISED to chase a name that got away, and the tape says plainly that AS did not get away: it closed at 33.62, BELOW the dead limit, and is 33.87 offered now. The price being nearly identical is a coincidence of the tape and is neither a reason to publish nor a reason to refuse.

RANKED AGAINST THE ALTERNATIVES, ON A MUCH RICHER FIELD THAN YESTERDAY'S. SECOND, TGT: a 2.46 against 2.25 beat this morning, 160.45 bid, +5.2%, on a genuinely striking structure - it opened 148.285, BELOW the 152.48 close, and reversed to 159.94, a new 52-week high, on 2.16M shares in thirteen minutes against a 4.28M two-week average. Better catalyst, better liquidity, bigger name. Refused on item 2, which exists precisely for this: buying at 160.45 is buying 9.7% off a session low set fourteen minutes earlier, at a fresh 52-week high, on day 1. If TGT holds this into tomorrow it is a better day-2 candidate than AS is today, and that is written down now so tomorrow's run is not free to discover it conveniently. THIRD, JKHY, +4.9% on an 8/18 after-hours beat, effectively day-1 and carrying the same objection. REFUSED ON ITEM 2 OUTRIGHT: EL at +15.8% on a 0.39 against 0.32 beat, and KC at +11.5% - both are the +8% day the rule names. REFUSED AS BEATS THE TAPE SOLD: TJX -1.4%, ADI -0.85%, KEYS -2.5%, VIK +0.5% after fading from 100.39 to 97.19, OPRA -8.8%. LOW beat by two cents against a 4.38 estimate, which is not a catalyst. ZIM missed at 0.64 against 1.08 and BIDU missed yesterday - buying the down half of a print is not a setup here. ADI is also 37.0% of the account for a single share, and AMD at 475.58 is 47.1%, over the 40% ceiling before any view is formed. THE OLD BOARD IS REFUSED ON ITEM 1 AS IT HAS BEEN ALL WEEK: UPST, IONQ, RGTI, SOUN, JOBY, OKLO and SMR carry nothing dated ahead, and SMCI - 36.75 bid, -1.76%, a twelfth test of a dead 38.24 limit and still 1.49 below it - keeps a thesis forced on items 1 and 5 that a lower price does not repair. KLAR at 14.62, -2.9% and making new lows a day after its own beat, still has no base and stays the counterexample that keeps item 1 from decaying into a number came out.

SIZE AND MECHANICS. 11 shares is the largest quantity that fits under the 40% single-name ceiling: 11 x 33.87 = 372.57 = 36.9%, where 12 shares would be 406.44 = 40.3% and fail the gate. Cash account, T+1, 1009.16 settled with zero unsettled, so there is no good-faith exposure. The limit is struck AT the 33.87 ask, deliberately and for the same reason as yesterday: four consecutive specifications have expired unexecuted, the 8/18 one missed by six cents, and a limit at the bid is how that keeps happening. This is the second consecutive not-forced entry, and the delivery leg - notifying the operator on the same pass - is the part of this run the 8/18 retro graded as failed.

entries.head: The 33.87 AS specification is re-quoted and CONFIRMED with five hours to run - the name is 0.26 through it to the upside, both written invalidations are untouched, and the limit is not raised to follow it
entries.body:
THE ONE LIVE SPECIFICATION IS RE-QUOTED AND CONFIRMED, NOT KILLED AND NOT RAISED. The 09:49 entry - buy 11 shares of AS at a 33.87 limit, target 40.64, stop 31.16, time stop the 8/25 close, expiring 15:30 ET today - was re-checked against live quotes at 14:23:16.100Z. AS is 34.13 bid / 34.16 ask on a 0.088% spread, last trade 34.15, +1.58% against the official 33.62 settled close. The limit is UNFILLED and now sits 0.26 BELOW the bid, so it is no longer marketable: it fills on a pullback to 33.87 and not otherwise. That is the entry it always was - a day-2 continuation struck on a pullback - and the name simply has not come back to it yet.

BOTH INVALIDATIONS WRITTEN BEFORE THE OUTCOME ARE UNTRIGGERED, AND THE TAPE HAS MOVED AWAY FROM THEM RATHER THAN TOWARD THEM. The earlier warning was a trade below 33.70, this morning's session low and the higher-low the day-2 structure rests on; AS is 34.13 bid, 0.43 above it. The outright void was a close below 33.41, yesterday's session low; that is 0.72 below the current bid and cannot be tested before the bell. Against the 09:46 strike the name is up 0.31 on the bid, 0.91%. Nothing in the thesis has been contradicted and the structure it described is the structure on the tape.

THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED, AND THIS IS THE FIFTH DIRECTION THAT REFUSAL HAS BEEN TESTED IN ACROSS TWO SESSIONS. AS is offered 0.29 above the limit. Re-striking at 34.16 to capture a name that has run 0.9% away is precisely the behaviour the 2026-08-18 rule change forbids in terms - widening the time is not permission to widen the price - and it is the same refusal this board applied to the 33.86 limit on 8/18 from four separate directions and to SMCI on twelve tests. Confirming a specification is not improving it. The 33.87 limit stands exactly as written.

THE KILL TEST IS APPLIED IN FULL AND ONE OF ITS THREE LIMBS IS ARGUABLY MET ON A LITERAL READING, SO THE READING IS DECIDED HERE IN WRITING RATHER THAN ASSUMED. A specification is killed when its stated invalidation has triggered, when its limit is no longer inside the spread, or when the setup it described is no longer the setup on the tape. Limbs one and three are plainly not met. Limb two is met word-for-word: a 33.87 limit is not inside a 34.13/34.16 market. But a buy limit leaves the spread in two opposite ways, and they are not the same event. It leaves downward when the tape falls THROUGH it, at which point the order would buy above the offer, into a decline, and the level it was reasoned on is gone - that is the case worth killing, and it usually arrives with the invalidation anyway. It leaves upward when the tape rises above it, at which point it is an ordinary resting bid waiting for the pullback it was always waiting for. Reading limb two to cover the upward case would kill every published entry the moment its name ticked one cent through the ask, and the same rulebook forbids re-striking it, which would make the 15:30 window that the 2026-08-18 change created inoperative for exactly the case it was written for. A rule may not be read so that it destroys the rule beside it. The narrow reading is taken: the limit left the spread upward, the specification is CONFIRMED, and this paragraph exists so the retro can overrule it on the record rather than discover the question.

THE DELIVERY LEG COULD NOT BE VERIFIED FROM THIS SIDE, AND THAT IS WHY AN OPERATOR NOTIFICATION WAS SENT OUTSIDE THE FIVE LITERAL TRIGGERS. The 8/18 retro graded the delivery leg for the first time and failed it: the 09:49 specification that day was published to a git commit and a static page and announced to nobody. Today's 09:49 entry names that duty in its own text but records no notification as having been sent, and nothing in data/ logs one either way - notifications leave no trace in this repo. So this run cannot establish whether the live specification has ever reached a human. The step-5 list would have this slot stay silent: nothing was published, nothing was killed, no level was hit, the guard was cleared, and the specification is five hours from expiry rather than in its last hour. The list is nonetheless a list of ways the delivery duty can bind, and the duty itself is that a specification nobody sees does not exist. Weighed against four consecutive entries that died unseen - the 8/18 one six cents from filling - a duplicate ping is the cheap error and a fifth silent expiry is the expensive one. One line was sent, no account identifier, and it is recorded here as a judgement call made slightly early rather than as a trigger that fired.

NO EXIT IS DUE AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 10:23 and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With nothing held there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour - not one level went unchecked, because none exists. ZERO equity orders and ZERO option orders exist in this account with a created_at floor of 2026-08-19, so the 33.87 limit has not been executed or partially executed by anyone and agentTrades stays 0. Portfolio pulled live: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits, ZERO unsettled - unchanged from the 09:43 read because nothing has traded. The specification's 372.57 cost is 36.9% of that, inside the 40% single-name ceiling, and it is the only claim on the cash, so one of four concurrent slots is used.

NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. This slot is exits-only, the standing default is no trade, the bar for a mid-session entry is higher than the open's by design, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text - it was discharged at 09:49 with a not-forced six-of-six entry that is still live. The three other names carried on the watch list were re-quoted in the SAME call as AS so they share one timestamp, and none of them changes. TGT is 158.86 bid / 159.12 ask at 14:23:17.239Z, +4.19% against the 152.48 close - it has FADED 1.59 or 0.99% from the 160.45 bid this morning's run refused it at, which is the item-2 refusal being paid rather than regretted, and it remains the named day-2 candidate for tomorrow on the written test of holding today's close on lighter volume. SMCI is 36.46 bid / 36.48 ask at 14:23:18.295Z, a 0.055% spread and again the tightest quote on the board, -2.54% against the 37.41 close; the 36.48 ask is 1.76 BELOW the 38.24 limit that expired on 8/17, a THIRTEENTH test, still marketable and still not revived, because a lower price does not supply the catalyst item 1 wanted. KLAR is 14.70 bid / 14.72 ask at 14:23:09.629Z, -2.39% against 15.06, off its lows but with no base yet formed, which is the precondition any entry there would need.

MECHANICS. Fired 10:21 ET against the 10:17 slot, four minutes late and sixteen minutes inside the 20-minute guard. The clock was cross-checked against the broker rather than trusted: venue_bid_time reads 14:23:16.100Z against a local 10:21 ET, confirming the -4 EDT offset the guard was measured with, on a machine this project has already caught reporting a clock nearly eight hours slow. Connector attached and the scope preflight matched the mandate identifier EXACTLY against the connector list - one account, unique, cash, agentic-allowed - and every other account was discarded unread; no identifier appears in this file, the commit, or the notification. The twenty-row candidate table is deliberately NOT re-struck: its rows carry the open's 13:42-13:46Z bids, and re-quoting only the four names this run touched would publish a two-timestamp board reading as one. Actions 0 - this run has no order authority, placed nothing, and allowOrderPlacement remains false.
entries.grade: PASS, AND THIS IS THE BEST RUN OF THE DAY. It re-quoted the live specification within its hour, found the name 0.26 through the limit to the UPSIDE, checked both written invalidations and found both untouched, and REFUSED TO RAISE THE LIMIT to follow a name that was moving away - the prohibition this board takes most seriously and the one a five-hour window makes hardest to keep. Both position lists were queried live rather than inferred from a flat log. THE PART THAT EARNS THE GRADE IS THE NOTIFICATION. This run noticed that the 09:49 entry names the delivery duty without recording that a notification was sent, reasoned that notifications leave no trace in data/ so it could not establish the specification had ever reached a human, and sent one DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE the five literal triggers - logging it as a judgement call rather than dressing it as a rule. That is one run repairing another run's omission from first principles, on a duty that was twenty-four hours old, and it is the reason today's expiry carries information that 8/18's did not. The tape says the repair was not academic: FIVE of the SEVEN five-minute bars that printed at or through 33.87 came after 10:21, twenty-five minutes of fillable tape still ahead of the ping. IT ALSO PUT ITS ONE HARD QUESTION ON THE RECORD FOR THIS SLOT TO OVERRULE rather than settling it in its own favour - whether a buy limit the tape has risen above is a dead level or a resting bid. THE RETRO UPHOLDS THE NARROW READING: it stands. The spec's written tests were a trade below 33.70 or a close below 33.41 and neither fired, killing a level struck in advance because the thesis worked without owning it is the exact mirror of raising it for the same reason, and the tape settled it empirically when the name came back through 33.87 on seven separate bars. Asking a question you could have answered yourself in the flattering direction is the behaviour this separation exists to produce.

entries.head: The AS specification is re-quoted and CONFIRMED for a second hour - and the limit it would not raise was touched and traded through for forty minutes with nothing resting to fill, which is the cost of the human gate arriving on the record rather than in a retro
entries.body:
THE SPECIFICATION IS CONFIRMED, NOT KILLED, AND THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED. The 09:49 entry - buy 11 shares of AS at a 33.87 limit, target 40.64, stop 31.16, time stop the 8/25 close, expiring 15:30 ET today - was re-checked against live quotes at 15:23:36.493Z. AS is 34.15 bid / 34.17 ask, a 0.02 spread on a 34.16 mark or 0.059%, last trade 34.16, +1.6% on the bid against the official 33.62 settled close. The limit is unfilled and sits 0.28 below the bid. Both invalidations written before the outcome are untriggered: the earlier warning is a trade below 33.70 and the session low is 33.70 EXACTLY, set between 09:30 and 09:35 and never breached in the four hours since; the outright void is a close below 33.41, which is 0.74 below the bid and cannot be tested before the bell.

THE FINDING OF THIS HOUR, AND IT IS NOT A COMFORTABLE ONE: THE ENTRY LEVEL PRINTED, REPEATEDLY, AND THERE WAS NO ORDER THERE. The 10:21 run wrote that the limit fills on a pullback to 33.87 and not otherwise, while AS was 34.13 bid. The five-minute bars say the pullback began within two minutes of that sentence. AS traded to a 33.82 low in the 10:15 bar, 33.83 in the 10:25 and 10:30 bars, 33.80 in the 10:35 bar, and 33.82 again in the 10:45 and 10:50 bars - and 33.85 as early as the 09:50 bar, one minute after the specification was published. Every one of those is at or through a 33.87 buy limit. A resting order would have filled, comfortably, on any of seven separate bars across roughly forty minutes.

WHAT THAT COSTS, PRICED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Filled at 33.87 the position would read 34.15 bid now: 372.57 becomes 375.65, up 3.08 or 0.83%. That is a small number and it is quoted small on purpose - the point is not the 3.08. The point is that this is the fifth consecutive specification this board has published that nobody executed, after 8/13, 8/14, 8/17 and 8/18, and it is the FIRST of them whose level actually printed while the specification was live and re-validated. The four earlier misses died of expiry or were never marketable. This one was marketable for forty minutes under the new 15:30 window, with a confirmation written an hour ago, and it still did not happen. The 2026-08-18 rule change widened the window precisely so that a good entry would not need the operator to be at a desk at 10:30, and this hour is the first clean measurement of whether that worked. It did not, and the reason is delivery rather than duration.

THE REASONING WAS RIGHT AND THE BOARD STILL HAS NOTHING, WHICH IS THE DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING. The 09:46 strike put the limit 0.05 under the then-bid on the theory that a day-2 continuation is bought on the pullback and not at the high. The tape confirmed that theory within the hour: AS ran to 34.47, came back to 33.80, and has since made 34.18. The limit was well struck. A specification is not an order, and a correctly struck level that nobody sat on is indistinguishable in the P/L from a badly struck one. That is the whole argument for the notification step, and this run notifies on it.

THE KILL TEST IS APPLIED IN FULL AND THE ANSWER IS THE SAME AS THE 10:21 RUN'S, WITH ONE NEW OBJECTION ANSWERED. Limb one, the invalidation, is untriggered and further away than at the open. Limb two, the limit no longer inside the spread, is met on the same literal reading as an hour ago and rejected on the same narrow one: a buy limit that the tape has risen ABOVE is an ordinary resting bid, not a dead level, and this hour supplies the proof - it rose above the limit, came back through it, and rose above it again. Reading limb two to kill on the upward case would have killed this specification at 10:21, forty minutes before its own entry printed. Limb three is the new objection: it can be argued that the pullback the entry described has now HAPPENED and been spent, so the setup on the tape is no longer the setup the entry named. That is the strongest case for killing and it is rejected, because the thesis was never one pullback - it was a day-2 continuation holding its higher low, and the higher low at 33.70 is intact on a name that is +1.6% today after +3.2% yesterday. The structure is the structure it described.

AND THE LIMIT IS STILL NOT RAISED, WHICH IS NOW THE SIXTH DIRECTION THAT REFUSAL HAS BEEN TESTED IN. This hour supplies the most tempting version of it yet: not merely a name that ran away, but a name that came back, offered the fill, and left again. Re-striking at 34.16 to capture what a resting order would already have had is exactly the behaviour the 2026-08-18 change forbids in terms - widening the time is not permission to widen the price - and it would be worse here than in the ordinary case, because it would convert a documented delivery failure into a higher entry price and call it a repair. The 33.87 limit stands exactly as written, with four hours left on it and a tape that has now demonstrated twice that it can reach it.

NO EXIT IS DUE AND NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED. Equity and option position lists were both queried live and both are empty: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits and zero unsettled, so the whole balance is settled and no good-faith violation is reachable. There is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window in existence to be hit this hour. The mid-session bar for a new entry is higher than the open's by design and the daily entry mandate belongs to the open slot, which has already discharged it; standing aside here is the rulebook working rather than a slot with nothing to say.

THE REST OF THE BOARD, RE-QUOTED, INCLUDING THE ROW THAT HAS TURNED AGAINST THIS BOARD'S OWN NOTE. TGT is 160.74 bid / 160.97 ask, +5.42% against its 152.48 close and 160.875 last - ABOVE the 159.94 fifty-two-week high and 0.29 ABOVE the 160.45 bid the open refused it at on item 2. The 10:23 note called that refusal being paid rather than regretted, on a 158.86 bid; within the hour it reversed, and the honest reading now is that the item-2 refusal is costing rather than paying. It is recorded that way and the rule is not changed for it - item 2 refuses buying 9.7% off a session low at a fresh high on day 1, and being wrong for one session is the cost the rule was written knowing about. The day-2 test for tomorrow is unchanged and still needs a close that does not exist yet. SMCI is 37.15 bid / 37.16 ask, -0.70%, up 0.69 from the 10:23 read and now 1.09 below the 38.24 limit that expired unfilled on 8/17 - a fourteenth test, still not revived, because a moving price does not supply the catalyst item 1 wanted. KLAR is 14.71 bid / 14.72 ask, -2.32%, one cent from the 10:23 read and still without the base any entry there would need.
entries.grade: PASS. Re-quoted within the hour, confirmed on the written tests rather than on a view, limit not raised for a second time. WHAT LIFTS IT ABOVE ROUTINE IS THAT IT RECORDED THE COST OF THE HUMAN GATE AT THE MOMENT IT WAS BEING PAID rather than leaving it for a retro to discover: the limit was touched and traded through with nothing resting to fill, and the run wrote that down while it was happening instead of reporting a clean confirm. The retro's own bar count agrees with it and sharpens it - seven five-minute bars printed at or through 33.87 after publication, thirty-five minutes of fillable tape, the last of it in the 10:50-to-10:55 bar, so by the time this run fired the window had already closed. A run that reports the uncomfortable fact about its own board's architecture in the hour it occurs is doing the job the log exists for.

entries.head: No exit is due against a flat book, and the AS specification is re-quoted and CONFIRMED for a third hour - but the limit that traded on seven bars this morning was 0.21 out of reach at the lowest tick of this entire hour
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD, AND THAT IS VERIFIED RATHER THAN INHERITED. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live against the mandate account at 12:23 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. With no position open there is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that can be reached this hour. Not one level went unchecked, because there are none to check. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist with a created_at floor of today. Fired 12:22 against the 12:17 slot, five minutes late, inside the 20-minute guard; venue_bid_time reads 16:23:26.523Z against a local 12:23 ET, confirming the -4 EDT offset.

THE ONE LIVE SPECIFICATION IS RE-QUOTED AND CONFIRMED. AS is 34.23 bid / 34.26 ask at 16:23:26.523Z on a 0.088% spread, last trade 34.23, +1.81% on the bid against the 33.62 settled close. The 33.87 limit for 11 shares is unfilled, its 372.57 cost is 36.9% of the 1009.16 account and inside the 40% single-name ceiling, and it is the only claim on the cash. Three hours and seven minutes remained on its 15:30 expiry when this was written.

THIS HOUR REVERSES LAST HOUR'S FINDING AND THE REVERSAL IS THE POINT. At 11:22 this board recorded that the level printed on seven five-minute bars across roughly forty minutes with no order resting - the first published level ever reached while live. Between 11:20 and 12:15 ET the lows are 34.08, 34.09, 34.14, 34.23, 34.22, 34.19, 34.23, 34.22, 34.14, 34.26, 34.21 and 34.15. The lowest tick of the hour is 34.08, which is 0.21 ABOVE the limit. The entry was available this morning and was not available at any moment of this hour, and both halves belong in the record because only one of them is comfortable.

THE KILL TEST, ARGUED AGAINST ITS STRONGEST FORM. Limb one, invalidation: untriggered and further away than at the open. The early warning is a trade below 33.70, which is the session low EXACTLY, set in the opening five minutes and not revisited in six and a half hours; the outright void is a close below 33.41, now 0.82 under the bid. Limb two, the limit no longer inside the spread: met literally, rejected on the same narrow reading the 10:21 and 11:22 runs wrote down - a buy limit the tape has risen above is a resting bid, not a dead level - and this morning is the evidence for that reading rather than against it, because the name rose above the limit, came back through it for forty minutes, and rose above it again.

LIMB THREE IS WHERE THIS HOUR IS WEAKER THAN THE LAST TWO, AND IT IS NOT DRESSED UP. The gap from limit to bid has widened every single hour: 0.26 through at 10:23, 0.28 at 11:23, 0.36 now. A limit the tape leaves further behind each hour is a limit converging on irrelevance, and that is a real objection rather than a rhetorical one. It does not become a kill because irrelevance is not invalidation. The specification's own written test is 33.70 or 33.41, neither is close, and a 1.1% pullback into the limit is an ordinary move in a name whose session range is already 2.3% wide and which sits 0.24 UNDER its own 34.47 session high rather than running away from it.

SO THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED AND THE SPEC IS NOT KILLED, AND THOSE ARE THE SAME REFUSAL SEEN FROM TWO SIDES. Raising 33.87 to 34.26 would convert a delivery failure into a worse entry price and call it a repair; killing it because the price went up would let the tape retire a level struck in advance just as surely. The forbidden move is the level moving to meet the tape, in either direction. This is the seventh direction that refusal has been tested in today and it is the most tempting one yet, because a name drifting away supplies a better excuse than a name sitting still.

WHAT THIS RUN DID NOT DO AND WHY. It sent no notification. No exit specification was published, nothing was killed, the connector attached, and no level was hit on a position that does not exist. The specification is not in its last hour - the rule's trigger is the 14:17 run, not this one - and the rulebook's own reasoning is that a routine hour which pings anyway is what teaches an operator to ignore the ping that matters. It also proposed no new entry: the mid-session bar is higher than the open's, the daily mandate belongs to the open slot, and the account is already 36.9% claimed by a specification whose thesis this run has just spent an hour confirming. Chasing AS at 34.26 while refusing to raise its own 33.87 limit would be the identical trade with the rule filed off.

THE STANDING COST IS REPEATED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED. This is the fifth consecutive published specification nobody executed, after 8/13, 8/14, 8/17 and 8/18, and the first whose level printed while it was live and re-validated. Filled at 33.87 it would read 34.23 bid now - 372.57 becoming 376.53, up 3.96 or 1.06%. The 3.96 is not the point. The point is that the board has now correctly identified a setup, correctly struck a level, watched that level trade, re-validated it three times, and still holds nothing.
entries.grade: PASS. Both position lists queried live against a flat book, no exit due and the run says why rather than saying nothing, the specification re-quoted and confirmed inside its hour, and the limit not raised for a third time. The hour's own arithmetic is quoted rather than asserted - 0.21 out of reach at the lowest tick of the entire hour - and the retro's bar data confirms it to the cent. KILLING WAS ARGUED AND REFUSED ON THE RIGHT GROUND: that killing a level because the price went UP rewrites a level struck in advance exactly as raising it would. The decision not to notify is correct and is reasoned rather than defaulted - nothing published, nothing killed, no level hit, three hours and seven minutes still to run, and the run names the 14:17 slot in advance as the one that will owe the last-hour ping. Naming which future slot inherits a duty is how this board stops a duty from evaporating between runs, and both the 13:21 and 14:21 rows show it worked.

entries.head: No exit is due against a flat book, and the AS specification is re-quoted and CONFIRMED for a fourth hour - but the limit drifted 0.35 further out of reach in this single hour, more than in the previous three combined, and the kill test now turns on limb three
entries.body:
THE BOOK IS FLAT, SO THE EXITS HALF OF THIS SLOT IS ANSWERED BY EVIDENCE RATHER THAN BY SILENCE. Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live at 13:22 ET and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. There is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window that could have been reached this hour, so not one level went unchecked - there are none to check. Balance re-read live rather than carried forward: 1009.16 total, all of it cash, zero unsettled, zero pending deposits. Zero equity orders and zero option orders exist with a created_at floor of 2026-08-19, so agentTrades stays 0 and the 33.87 level is still unowned.

THE RE-VALIDATION DUTY IS THE WHOLE JOB THIS HOUR AND THE ANSWER IS CONFIRM. AS is 34.58 bid / 34.61 ask at 17:22:55.618Z on a 0.087% spread, last trade 34.59, +2.86% on the bid against the 33.62 settled close, with a fresh 34.65 session high printed in the last twelve minutes. Both written invalidations are untouched and both moved further away: the 33.70 early warning is the session low EXACTLY, set in the opening five minutes and unrevisited in seven and a half hours of tape, and the 33.41 outright void is 1.17 below the bid and untestable before the bell.

THE HONEST HALF, AND IT IS MATERIALLY WORSE THAN LAST HOUR'S RATHER THAN THE SAME SENTENCE REPEATED. The gap from limit to bid across four hourly reads is 0.26, 0.28, 0.36 and now 0.71. This one hour widened it by 0.35 - more than the previous three hours put together - and 33.87 now sits 2.05% below the bid. The lowest five-minute tick between 12:15 and 13:20 ET is 34.15, a full 0.28 above the limit, so this is the second consecutive hour in which a resting order could not have filled at any price, and the forty-minute morning window in which it would have filled closed two and a half hours ago. Filling before 15:30 requires a 2.05% reversal inside two hours and eight minutes, in a name making session highs. That is not the ordinary 1.1% pullback the 12:22 run could reasonably describe.

THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED, FOR AN EIGHTH TIME AND AGAINST THE HARDEST VERSION OF THE TEMPTATION THIS BOARD HAS FACED. The 2026-08-18 rule change says it in terms: widening the time is not permission to widen the price, and re-striking a dead level higher is the behaviour this board has refused most often. The name is no longer sitting near the level and drifting; it is running. That makes the argument for chasing louder and does not make it better.

THE KILL TEST, AND THIS HOUR IT TURNS ON LIMB THREE RATHER THAN LIMB TWO. A specification dies when its invalidation triggers, when its limit is no longer inside the spread, or when the setup it described is no longer the setup on the tape.

Limb one plainly fails: 1.17 from the void.

Limb two is met word-for-word and is rejected on the narrow reading the 10:21 run wrote down and the 11:22 and 12:22 runs upheld. A buy limit leaves the spread two opposite ways. Downward, when the tape falls THROUGH it and the order would buy above the offer into a decline - that is the case worth killing, and it usually arrives with the invalidation anyway. Upward, when the tape rises above it and the order is an ordinary resting bid awaiting the pullback it always awaited. Reading limb two to cover the upward case would kill every entry the moment its name ticked a cent through the ask, while the same rulebook forbids re-striking it - which would make the 15:30 window inoperative for exactly the case it was written for.

LIMB THREE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS NOW AND IT ARGUES FOR CONFIRM, WHICH IS NOT WHAT THE DRIFT SUGGESTS. The test asks whether the setup the entry described is still the setup on the tape. The setup was a day-2 post-earnings continuation off a 100% EPS beat, entered on a pullback, with a higher low at 33.70 as its written support. Every element is MORE true than when it was struck: 33.70 has held all session as the exact low, and the name has just made a new session high. What has left the tape is the ENTRY PRICE, not the SETUP. Conflating those two is the only way a kill gets written here, and killing a specification because its thesis worked without the board owning it is the exact mirror image of raising the limit because its thesis worked without the board owning it. Both rewrite a level struck in advance. One of them this board has refused eight times; the other should be refused for the same reason.

SO THE TWO HONEST OUTCOMES REMAIN HOLD AT 33.87 OR NOTHING, AND THIS RUN WILL NOT DRESS UP WHICH ONE IT PICKED. The specification is confirmed, valid, and in practice probably unfillable. The operator reading this should take away that the level is live and hard to reach, not merely that it is live.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE HALF IS UNCHANGED AND HAS GROWN. This is the fifth consecutive published specification nobody executed, and the first whose level printed while it was live and re-validated. Filled at 33.87 the 372.57 would read 380.38 now: up 7.81, or 2.10%, against 1.06% an hour ago. The 7.81 is not the point. The point is that the board has now spent four hours re-validating an entry it identified correctly, struck correctly, and does not own - which measures the delivery leg, not the reasoning leg, and measures it to the cent.

NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, the bar for a mid-session entry is higher than the open's by design, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text - it was discharged at 09:49 with a not-forced six-of-six entry that is still live. TGT running 0.75 above the level it was refused at this morning is exactly the kind of thing that would tempt a mid-session chase, and item 2 refuses it on day 1 at 161.20 for the same reason it refused it at 160.45.

NO NOTIFICATION WAS SENT, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. No exit spec was published, nothing was killed, the connector attached, no level was hit-and-missed on a book that holds nothing, and the specification is not in its last hour - 15:30 is two hours and eight minutes away. The last-hour ping falls to the 14:17 slot, exactly as the 12:22 run predicted. A routine hour that pings anyway is what teaches an operator to ignore the ping that matters.
entries.grade: PASS, AND THE MOST HONEST OF THE SIX CONFIRMS. Re-quoted within the hour, limit not raised for a fourth time, and the run reported the WORST fact available about its own specification without softening it: the gap drifted 0.35 in this single hour, more than in the previous three combined. It then wrote the sentence that a run reluctant to admit a dead position would not write - that the specification is confirmed, valid, and probably unfillable - and left the two honest outcomes as hold at 33.87 or nothing, with no third option constructed to make the hold look better. The refusal to kill rests on the same limb as the previous two hours and is consistent rather than convenient. The notification decision is again reasoned rather than defaulted, with the 14:17 slot named in advance for the second consecutive hour.

entries.head: No exit is due against a flat book, the AS specification is re-quoted and CONFIRMED for a fifth hour, and the last-hour notification is sent - the drift that accelerated 0.35 last hour added 0.03 this one, which corrects the emphasis without moving the level any closer
entries.body:
NO EXIT IS DUE AND THAT IS A FINDING RATHER THAN A SKIP. Equity and option position lists were both queried live at 14:22 and both are empty; zero equity orders and zero option orders exist on a created_at floor of 2026-08-19. There is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window on this book, so not one level went unchecked. Balances live and not derived: 1009.16 total, all cash, zero unsettled, zero pending deposits.

THE RE-VALIDATION DUTY IS THE WHOLE JOB AND THE ANSWER IS CONFIRM FOR A FIFTH HOUR. AS is 34.61 bid / 34.62 ask at 18:22:53.232Z, a one-cent spread at 0.029% of mark and the tightest quote this name has printed today, last trade 34.615, +2.94% on the bid against the 33.62 settled close, with a fresh 34.83 session high set in the 14:00 ET bar.

THE CORRECTION COMES FIRST, BECAUSE IT CUTS AGAINST THIS BOARD'S OWN HEADLINE FROM AN HOUR AGO. The 13:21 entry led with the drift ACCELERATING - the gap from limit to bid went 0.26, 0.28, 0.36, then 0.71, one hour adding more than the previous three combined - and a reader would fairly take from that an expectation of a level running away at an increasing rate. It did not. This hour added 0.03. The series is 0.26, 0.28, 0.36, 0.71, 0.74. One hour was never a trend, and the deceleration is reported as plainly as the acceleration was rather than dropped because it is the less dramatic half.

WHAT THE CORRECTION DOES NOT DO IS IMPROVE THE POSITION. 0.74 is the widest the gap has been at any read today and the 33.87 limit is 2.14% under the bid. The lowest five-minute low between 13:20 and 14:20 ET is 34.49, a full 0.62 above the limit, so a resting order was unfillable for a THIRD consecutive hour; the forty-minute morning window in which it would have filled closed three and a half hours ago. Filling before the 15:30 expiry requires a 2.14% reversal in sixty-seven minutes in a name still making session highs.

BOTH WRITTEN INVALIDATIONS ARE UNTOUCHED. The early warning is a trade below 33.70: that is the session low EXACTLY, set in the opening five minutes and unrevisited in eight and a half hours of tape. The outright void is a close below 33.41, now 1.20 below the bid and untestable before the bell.

THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED, FOR A NINTH TIME. Re-striking at 34.62 to capture a name that ran 2.9% away is what the 2026-08-18 rule change forbids in terms: widening the time is not permission to widen the price. Had 11 shares filled at 33.87 for 372.57 they would read 380.71 now, up 8.14 or 2.19%.

THE KILL TEST, APPLIED IN FULL FOR A THIRD CONSECUTIVE HOUR. Limb one, the invalidation, is untriggered and 1.20 from the void. Limb two, the limit no longer inside the spread, is met word-for-word and rejected on the narrow reading the 10:21 run wrote down and every hourly since has defended: a buy limit the tape has risen ABOVE is a resting bid awaiting the pullback it always awaited, not a dead level, and the wide reading would kill every entry the moment its name ticked through the ask while the same rulebook forbids re-striking it. Limb three asks whether the setup the entry described is still the setup on the tape, and it argues FOR confirm - a day-2 post-earnings continuation off a 100% EPS beat, entered on a pullback, with a higher low at 33.70 as written support; 33.70 has held all session as the exact low and the name has made another new high. What has left the tape is the ENTRY PRICE, not the SETUP. Killing a specification because the thesis worked without the board owning it is the exact mirror of raising the limit because the thesis worked without the board owning it, and both are the tape rewriting a level struck in advance.

SO THE SPECIFICATION IS CONFIRMED, VALID, AND LESS LIKELY TO FILL THAN AT ANY PRIOR READ, AND THIS RUN SAYS THE SECOND PART OUT LOUD. Sixty-seven minutes and a required 2.14% reversal is a worse proposition than the two hours and 2.05% the last run described. The operator relying on this row should know the level is live and probably out of reach, not merely that it is live.

THE LAST-HOUR NOTIFICATION IS SENT, AND IT IS THE LITERAL STEP-5 TRIGGER RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT CALL. A live specification is unexecuted with sixty-seven minutes to run and the next hourly fires at 15:17, thirteen minutes before expiry - a warning delivered then is not a warning. The 12:22 and 13:21 entries both named this slot in advance as the one that owed it, and it is discharged: one line, under 200 characters, no account identifier.

THE UNCOMFORTABLE HALF IS UNCHANGED AND GREW AGAIN. This is the fifth consecutive published specification nobody executed, the first whose level printed while it was live and re-validated, and the board has now spent five hours re-validating an entry it correctly identified, correctly struck, and does not own. The 8.14 is not the point. The point is that the process worked and the delivery did not, and the one thing this run could do about that - deliver the warning - it did rather than adding a sixth hour of silent re-validation.

NO NEW ENTRY IS PROPOSED AND NONE IS OWED. The standing default is no trade, this slot is exits-only, the mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:49 with a not-forced six-of-six entry that is still live. Actions 0; this run has no order authority, placed nothing, and allowOrderPlacement remains false.
entries.grade: PASS. Re-quoted inside the hour, limit not raised for a fifth time, and THE STEP-5 LAST-HOUR NOTIFICATION WAS SENT FROM THIS SLOT WITH SIXTY-SEVEN MINUTES TO RUN, which is the correct reading of a trigger whose literal wording would have put it at 15:17 with thirteen minutes left.
