Equity positions and option positions were BOTH queried live at 15:22 ET against the mandated account and BOTH LISTS ARE EMPTY. There is no target, no stop, no time stop and no option no-fly window reachable this hour, because there is no position. Portfolio pulled live: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits, ZERO unsettled, buying_power 1009.16 to match - so the whole balance is settled and deployable, unchanged from the 10:22, 11:21, 12:21, 13:22 and 14:22 reads because nothing has traded. ZERO equity orders exist with a created_at floor of 2026-08-20, so agentTrades stays 0 and nothing has been executed or partially executed by anyone. NO LIVE SPECIFICATION, ESTABLISHED FROM THE FILE RATHER THAN FROM MEMORY. why.json holds exactly one will entry dated today - the 09:48 FUTU limit at 117.90, withdrawn at 11:21 by appending. There is no unexpired requiresHuman proposal on this board, so the step 2b re-quote duty is discharged and empty and the operator has no standing instruction resting on ageing quotes. Eight minutes remain to the 15:30 specification deadline and thirty-eight to the bell. THE CLOCK WAS CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE VENUE RATHER THAN TRUSTED. The project helper reads 15:21:15 ET; FUTU's venue_bid_time reads 2026-08-21T19:22:19.207187611Z, an exact -4 EDT offset, so the machine clock is honest this hour. Fired 15:22 against the 15:17 slot, five minutes late and fifteen minutes inside the twenty-minute guard. NOW THE HOUR'S ACTUAL WORK, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO THIS BOARD'S OWN RECORD RATHER THAN A MARKET CALL. The 14:21 run found that hourly cost-of-refusal figures are point samples at twenty-one minutes past and asked that refusals be scored against the post-refusal RANGE instead. Doing that produced something larger than a measurement note. THE FUTU SPECIFICATION WAS FILLABLE, AND THE TEST THAT KILLED IT NEVER LOOKED AT THE INTERVAL IN WHICH IT WAS FILLABLE. The evidence, pulled at fifteen-second resolution rather than inferred from five-minute bars. The specification was committed and live at 09:50:48 ET. Every bar from 09:51:00 to 09:54:00 is entirely after that timestamp and entirely below the 117.90 limit: 117.0478-117.2250 on 708 shares, 117.1038 on 100, 117.0000 on 180, 117.2150-117.2400 on 600, 117.0001-117.2100 on 809, 117.3000-117.6000 on 300, 117.7400 on 3,800, 117.5900-117.7200 on 600, 117.5500-117.5700 on 244, and 117.6000-117.7275 on 2,040. THAT IS 9,381 SHARES, AND THE HIGHEST TICK AMONG THEM IS 117.7275 - 0.1725 UNDER THE LIMIT. The first print at or above 117.90 comes in the 09:54:15 bar, which opens 117.8000 and reaches 118.0600. So a 3-share limit buy at 117.90, posted when the specification went live, was MARKETABLE ON ARRIVAL against an offer near 117.05 and would have filled immediately, with 9,381 shares of depth beneath it over the following three minutes and twenty-seven seconds. This is not a close call and it is not a modelled fill. WHAT THE DROUGHT TEST ACTUALLY MEASURED. The 11:21 kill is recorded, in this file and in its commit, as twelve five-minute bars from 09:55 to 10:55 ET printing a lowest low of 118.33 with none at or below the limit. Every one of those numbers is TRUE. The window is the problem: it opens at 09:55, and the last sub-limit print was at 09:54:15. The test began forty-five seconds after the tape stopped offering the level. It therefore did not observe that the level went untraded - it observed an interval selected, at 10:21, to begin after the only period in which the level was live. THAT IS A DIFFERENT AND WORSE FAILURE THAN YESTERDAY'S, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT. The TGT 159.36 test on 8/20 was wrong about what the tape did AFTER the kill, which is a forecasting miss and forgivable in an instrument that exists to kill stale levels. Today's test was wrong about what the tape had ALREADY DONE BEFORE THE TEST WAS EVEN WRITTEN. A kill instrument whose window can exclude the fill it is supposed to be testing for is not measuring liquidity at the level; it is measuring where its own window was placed. TWO SPECIFICATIONS IN TWO DAYS HAVE NOW BEEN KILLED BY THIS TEST AND IT HAS BEEN WRONG ABOUT THE TAPE BOTH TIMES. WHAT THE POSITION WOULD BE NOW, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THE RECORD SHOULD NOT HAVE TO RECONSTRUCT IT. Filled at 117.90 for 3 shares, 353.70 committed. FUTU is 124.04 bid / 124.16 ask at 19:22:19.207187611Z, +10.03% on the 112.73 settled close, on a 0.12 spread. That is 372.12, an unrealised +18.42 or +5.21%. The 141.48 target is 17.44 away and unreached, so no exit would be due this hour even on the counterfactual. The 108.47 stop was never approached - the session low is 116.83, a full 8.36 above it - and the 8/27 time stop is four sessions out. The trade this board specified, and then killed, has done nothing but work. THE FOUR REFUSALS SCORED AGAINST RANGE RATHER THAN AGAINST THE :21 SAMPLE, WHICH IS WHAT THE LAST HOUR ASKED FOR. FUTU, level 117.90: session low 116.83 at 09:45, high 124.48 at 11:00, now 124.04 bid, and the level WAS OFFERED, from the open through 09:54:15. TGT, refused at 161.92: low 161.77 at 09:50, high 164.58 at 11:05, now 164.02 bid, so the level was offered but by only 0.15 and in a single five-minute bar. ROST, refused at 238.38: low 234.50 at 10:25, high 242.725 at 13:00, now 239.23 bid - offered 3.88 below and for well over an hour, and note that the :21 sample now reads +0.85 where it read +3.06 an hour ago, which is the point-sampling problem restating itself inside a single hour. BJ, refused at 95.08: low 93.1093 at 11:10, high 96.28 at 12:15, now 94.68 bid, which is 0.40 BELOW the refusal - the name has crossed from costing this board money to saving it since 14:21, on no news and no decision. AND THE HONEST QUALIFIER ON THREE OF THOSE FOUR. ROST and BJ were refused on checklist item 2 and item 5 - the spike day, and the fifth retail beat into a tape that sold the first four. Neither objection was ever about a price, so neither is answered by a price that moved, in either direction. TGT was refused because this board killed its level yesterday and the stock was through it. ONLY FUTU IS A CASE WHERE THE BOARD'S OWN MACHINERY, RATHER THAN ITS JUDGEMENT, PRODUCED THE OUTCOME, AND THAT IS PRECISELY WHY IT IS THE ONE WORTH WRITING DOWN. NOTHING IS PROPOSED AND THE FINDING ABOVE IS NOT AN ARGUMENT THAT ANYTHING SHOULD BE. It cuts the other way entirely. FUTU at 124.04 is 6.14 above a level this board withdrew in writing, and re-striking a dead level higher to chase a name that got away is the single behaviour docs/RULES.md names as the one it has refused most often - the 2026-08-18 rule change says widening the time is not permission to widen the price, and being RIGHT about the original level makes re-striking it higher more tempting and no more permissible. The mid-session default is no trade, this slot's bar is explicitly higher than the open's, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:48 with a not-forced five-of-six entry. Eight minutes to the specification deadline is not a window in which this board should be discovering a new idea. WHAT THE RETRO SHOULD TAKE FROM THIS HOUR, AND IT IS A PROCESS ITEM RATHER THAN A P/L ONE. The away-side drought test is a good instrument aimed badly. Its window has twice been chosen by the run that writes it, an hour or two after the specification went live, and today that choice silently excluded the fill. THE FIX IS NOT TO ABANDON THE TEST BUT TO ANCHOR ITS WINDOW TO THE SPECIFICATION'S OWN GO-LIVE TIMESTAMP RATHER THAN TO THE HOUR THE TEST HAPPENS TO BE WRITTEN, and to require that a kill state whether the level ever traded since publication - a question today's kill never asked and could have answered in one call. That is a recommendation to the operator, not a rule this run may change; the agent does not amend the rulebook. NO NOTIFICATION WAS SENT AND NONE WAS OWED. No exit specification was published, no specification was killed this hour because none was alive, no live spec is in its last hour, this run neither declined on the staleness guard nor failed to connect, and NO LEVEL WAS HIT AND LEFT UNACTED. That is stated as a fact rather than left silent, because a run on this board once asserted a notification it had not sent, and because a routine no-exit ping is exactly the one that teaches an operator to ignore the rest. The finding above is retro material and fires none of the five triggers. Actions 0 - this run has no order authority, placed nothing, cancelled nothing, moved no funds, and allowOrderPlacement remains false. THE SCOPE PREFLIGHT MATCHED THE MANDATE IDENTIFIER EXACTLY against the connector list; every other account was discarded unread and no identifier appears in this file, in the commit, or anywhere in the repo.

grade.text: PASS, AND ON THE CENTRAL FINDING IT IS EXCEPTIONAL - BUT IT REPEATS, ON BJ, THE EXACT DEFECT THE RUN AN HOUR EARLIER HAD NAMED. THE CENTRAL FINDING FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING PUBLISHED ON THIS BOARD TODAY. With nothing to manage for a fourth hour, this run re-opened the board's own most consequential decision of the session at fifteen-second resolution and established that the drought test which killed the FUTU specification was pointed at the wrong window. Every bar from 09:51:00 to 09:54:00 traded entirely below the 117.90 limit; 9,381 shares of depth sat beneath it over three minutes and twenty-seven seconds; the first print at or above the limit came in the 09:54:15 bar; and the 10:21 run's drought clock began 45 seconds after the last sub-limit print. So a 3-share limit buy posted when the specification went live was marketable on arrival, and the run says so in those words - 'not a close call and not a modelled fill.' That is a run volunteering, unprompted and with no fill to defend, that this board's own device cost it the day's best trade. It is the behaviour the outcome-blind separation exists to make possible and it made tonight's grade of the 10:21 and 11:21 entries possible rather than speculative. THE DEMERIT, AND IT IS A REPEAT OFFENCE RATHER THAN A FIRST ONE. It reported BJ at a 94.68 bid as 0.40 below its refusal and wrote that the name 'has crossed from costing this board money to saving it since 14:21'. That is a point sample at twenty-two minutes past the hour presented as a state change - precisely the error the 14:21 run had identified sixty minutes earlier, quantified, and asked the board to stop making in favour of scoring against the post-refusal range. The close settles it and settles it against the sentence: BJ printed 96.355 at 15:59:59, which is 1.275 ABOVE the 95.08 refusal. The name had not crossed to saving anything. A defect named at 14:21 and repeated at 15:22 is a different and worse thing than a defect nobody had spotted yet, and the run's own excellent work on FUTU in the same entry shows it had the resolution to check. Duties otherwise discharged: positions and portfolio live, no live specification confirmed from the file, nothing re-struck, and FUTU explicitly refused at 124.04 as a dead level the board withdrew in writing.

entries.head: Flat into the weekend, written down as a decision rather than left as an absence - nothing held, nothing carried past the bell, and the catalyst row spot fell exactly 2.20 for the second session running
entries.body: THE DECISION THIS SLOT EXISTS TO MAKE IS THE OVERNIGHT HOLD, AND TODAY IT IS THE EMPTY ONE. Portfolio, equity positions and option positions were each pulled live at 15:36 and all three returned first time: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits, ZERO unsettled, and BOTH position lists empty. So the four step-2 questions collapse onto one fact rather than being skipped. No option no-fly window closes today because no contract is held and no print can land before an expiry that does not exist. No earnings-tonight exposure, because nothing is owned - and no straddle is owed, since item 3 binds only before an earnings hold and a straddle pulled three sessions early prices a different event than the 8/26 print will. No target, stop or time stop was hit, because no position carries one. And the hold itself: the board goes into the weekend with no gap risk, no theta and no level it needs to be awake for on Monday. Flat is a position, and going into a dense back half of next week it is the one the NVDA row below was written six sessions early to produce. NOTHING SURVIVES THE BELL, AND THAT WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE FILE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. This file carries exactly one will entry dated today: the 09:48 FUTU specification, 3 shares, limit 117.90, target 141.48, stop 108.47, requiresHuman true, expiresAt 2026-08-21 15:30. It was WITHDRAWN at 11:21 by appending, four hours before that fuse. So there is no unexpired proposal for the bell to kill, no expiry entry is owed, and nothing is re-struck for Monday. FUTU closed the loop on this board at 15:22 with a finding that cuts the other way - the 117.90 limit was marketable on arrival and the drought test that killed it was pointed at the wrong interval - and that is a reason to fix the test, not a licence to re-enter a name six dollars above a level this board withdrew in writing. Widening the time is not permission to widen the price. THE PRUNE FOUND NOTHING TO REMOVE AND ONE THING TO CORRECT. A live earnings calendar was re-pulled for 2026-08-21 through 2026-08-27. The single NVDA row is dated 2026-08-26 after the close, THREE sessions ahead - 8/24, 8/25, 8/26 - and was re-verified on that pull: NVDA, 2026-08-26, timing pm, verified true, no actual yet, estimate 2.07 for fiscal Q2 2027. Nothing on the file has passed, so nothing was removed. THE SPOT REFRESH REPEATED YESTERDAY'S CORRECTION TO THE CENT, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE RULE. NVDA is 215.01 bid / 215.02 ask at 19:35:48.690161719Z on a 0.005% spread, last 215.015, against a 216.85 settled close on 8/20 - down 0.85% on the session and DOWN 2.20, or 1.01%, from the 217.21 this file carried. Yesterday's pre-close moved the same row 219.41 to 217.21, a fall of 2.20 or 1.00%. Two consecutive sessions, two identical 2.20 marks lower, 4.40 and 2.01% cumulative. A row left unrefreshed since Wednesday would now centre its implied range four dollars above the tape, and the refresh is a rule for exactly that reason rather than because any single day drift looked worth bothering with. AND THE PULL SURFACED A PRINT THE ROW OWN BRANCH DID NOT COVER. MRVL reports 2026-08-27 after the close, verified, estimate 0.87 for fiscal Q2 2027 - a second dated semiconductor print inside the window, one session after NVDA. The first branch was written as 8/25 or 8/26 and would have read as silent on 8/27, so its condition now names the whole 8/25 to 8/27 stretch and its why says why the extra day changes nothing about the arithmetic. This is a gap in the board own file found by re-pulling rather than by re-reading, which is the point of pruning against a live calendar instead of against the file memory of one. The same pull shows CRM, CRWD and SNPS on 8/26 pm and ADSK, WDAY and ESTC on 8/27 - the back half of next week is dense with software prints too - but none is a watched name and none is entered. THE WATCH LIST IS FLOORED ON CATALYST FOR A NINTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION. Of the watched names not one has a dated event anywhere in the window: not AS, SMCI, KLAR, SQM, UPST, AMD, IONQ, RGTI, SOUN, OKLO, SMR or JOBY. BJ, one of the four names declined this morning, printed 8/21 am at 1.360 actual against a 1.190 estimate - a 14.3% beat - so it sits behind the board rather than ahead of it and is not entered here. Worth naming plainly: this board declined BJ at 95.08 before that number existed, and a beat it did not know about is not a refusal it got wrong. AMD WAS RE-QUOTED BECAUSE THE ROW CITES IT AND A CITED NUMBER THAT WENT STALE IS THE SAME DEFECT AS A STALE SPOT. It is 471.70 bid / 471.84 ask at 19:35:48.467065832Z, up 0.50% on the session, and one share is now 46.74% of a 1009.16 account against the 40% single-name ceiling - wider than the 46.2% the row carried. AMD is refused by an explicit mechanical limit before any view about NVDA reaches it, and this session made that refusal less marginal, not more. NOTHING IS PROPOSED AND NOTHING IS OWED. The pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes; the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text and was discharged at 09:48 with a not-forced five-of-six entry. No notification was sent and none was owed: no exit is due, no no-fly window closes today, nothing is held overnight, and the run neither declined nor failed to connect. A flat book with nothing due is the one case the notification rules exempt by name, and a routine all-clear ping is the one that teaches an operator to ignore the EXIT line when it finally comes. Actions 0. This run has no order authority, placed nothing, and allowOrderPlacement remains false.

grade.text: PASS. The pre-close's stated job is to decide overnight holds EXPLICITLY rather than by default, and this entry does exactly that: flat into the weekend recorded as a decision rather than left as an absence, with both position lists queried live at 15:36 and both empty, so every step-2 question is answered for the same stated reason rather than skipped for it - no no-fly window closes because no contract is held, no earnings exposure exists because no underlying is held, no target, stop or time stop is reachable because no position carries one. It established from the FILE, not from memory, that why.json held exactly one will entry dated today and that it had been withdrawn at 11:21 - therefore no specification was alive at 15:30, no expiry entry was owed, and the step 3b duty was discharged rather than assumed away. THE PRUNE IS THE PART THAT EARNED THE GRADE, because it found something by re-pulling that re-reading could not have found. Nothing on moves.json had passed, so the easy discharge was to say so and stop. Instead the run re-pulled the calendar across 8/21-8/27 and found MRVL reporting 8/27 after the close - a second dated semiconductor print inside the window that branch one, written as '8/25 or 8/26', would have read as silent on. It widened the branch wording to span 8/25-8/27 and correctly labelled that as a gap in the wording rather than a new judgement. It also refreshed the carried spot from a live quote rather than leaving a reference price to rot: NVDA 215.01 bid against the 217.21 the file carried, down 2.20 in a session, and it noticed that yesterday's refresh had moved the same row by exactly 2.20 as well. Naming the coincidence and then generalising it into the argument for refreshing as a rule - with the AMD row that sat at 522.95 the morning it traded 486 as the cost of not doing so - is the right use of an observation that could as easily have been left as trivia. And it was correct on the notification: none was owed, and it said why in the terms the trigger list uses rather than asserting it. That is the second consecutive session on which a pre-close correctly declined to claim a notification, which is worth recording given that the 8/20 pre-close claimed one that had not been sent and needed a 15:41 pass to catch it. It refused FUTU as a dead level rather than treating the 15:22 finding as a licence, which was the available temptation: a run that had just proved the kill was wrong could have read that as grounds to re-enter six dollars higher, and it named that reading and rejected it.

entries.head: Day-2 continuation in BJ at 97.35 for 4 shares, five of six and not forced - bought on the fade off the session high rather than at it, with every option in the window refused on spread for the tenth time and the FUTU level this board killed left alone at 0.49 above it
entries.body:
THE SPECIFICATION IS BJ, 4 SHARES, LIMIT 97.35, TARGET 116.82, STOP 89.56, TIME STOP THE 8/28 CLOSE. That is 389.40 against 1009.16 of settled deployable cash - 38.6% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling, the largest position this board has sized and still inside the limit. Struck at 09:46 ET on a 97.22 bid / 97.87 ask, so the limit sits inside the quoted spread and 0.13 below the 97.48 last trade. NOT FORCED: five items pass and item 3 is not applicable. The bid is quoted, never the mark.

THE CATALYST IS ONE SESSION OLD AND IT IS DATED. BJ reported fiscal Q2 on 2026-08-21 before the open: 1.360 actual against a 1.190 estimate, a 14.3% beat, verified true on a live earnings-calendar pull covering 8/18 to 8/21. The print day closed 96.42, up 5.6% from the 91.30 the day before, on 4,180,945 shares against a ten-day run rate nearer 1.5 to 2.2 million - two to three times normal participation, which is what a real re-rating looks like rather than a drift.

WHY TODAY AND NOT FRIDAY. Friday was the spike and item 2 forbids buying it; this board refused BJ that day and was right to. Today is day 2. BJ is 97.48 last, up 0.83%, and it has already printed 98.35 this morning - 1.47 above Friday's 96.88 high - before easing back. The limit is struck INTO that pullback at 97.35, not at the 98.35 spike. That distinction is the whole entry: the name is bought on the fade off the session high, which is the shape the rulebook asks for, and if it does not come back to 97.35 the specification simply dies unfilled at 15:30.

THE RELATIVE STRENGTH IS THE REASON THIS NAME AND NOT ANOTHER. This is a red tape: SPY 762.87 bid, down 0.37%; QQQ 704.65, down 1.23%. The high-beta complex is being sold hard - SMCI down 5.8%, IONQ down 5.3%, OKLO down 5.2%, SMR down 5.2%, FUTU down 4.1%, SOUN down 3.2%, JOBY down 3.2%. BJ is green into that. Item 2's wait signal is a list that is uniformly GREEN 5-10%; this list is uniformly RED, which is the opposite condition, and a name holding a post-earnings gain while its index sheds 1.2% is showing something the tape is not giving away for free.

ITEM 5 GETS THE MOST CARE, BECAUSE IT IS ONE OF THE TWO ITEMS THIS BOARD REFUSED BJ ON LAST WEEK. The failure mode item 5 names is crowded bulls into a print, where a merely-good report sells off. BJ went in the other way round. It fell from 96.20 on 8/10 to 91.79 on 8/19, and on 8/20 it OPENED at 88.91 and traded as low as 88.22 - marked down 5.1% over the eight sessions immediately before its own report, and sold to an eight-session low the day before it. Expectations were being cut into the print, not raised. It then beat by 14.3% and closed the day up 5.6%. Low expectations, good report, positive re-rate is the favourable side of item 5 rather than the adverse one. THE COUNTERWEIGHT, NAMED RATHER THAN OMITTED: warehouse and value retail has been the market's defensive hiding place all month - WMT is up 1.63% today and DE up 1.10% into the same red tape - so BJ is riding a crowded THEME even though the NAME was not crowded into its own number. If the defensive bid unwinds, BJ unwinds with it and the beat will not save it.

AND THE HARDER QUESTION, WHICH IS WHETHER THIS IS THE CHASE THIS BOARD HAS REFUSED MOST OFTEN. On 8/21 the hourly runs ranked BJ and declined it at 95.08. I am proposing to buy it 2.27 higher. That has to be answered rather than stepped around. The 2026-08-18 rule says the limit may never be raised to chase a name that got away, and its subject is a PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION that died and is then re-struck higher. There is no dead BJ limit: BJ was never published as a specification, it was a candidate the hourly notes ranked and declined. The one dead limit this board actually carries is FUTU at 117.90, withdrawn 8/21 - and FUTU is 118.39 bid this morning, 0.49 above that level and the closest it has been since. IT IS NOT RE-STRUCK AND IT IS NOT ENTERED. Refusing the name I killed while entering the name I merely declined is the distinction the rule is actually drawing, and it costs me the cheaper-looking trade to hold it.

WHAT ANSWERS THE OLD REFUSAL, ITEM BY ITEM, BECAUSE 'IT IS A NEW DAY' IS NOT AN ARGUMENT. The 14:21 run on 8/21 wrote that BJ was declined on items 2 and 5 and that those are objections that are not about a price and are therefore not answered by a price that moved. That is correct and it binds me. So neither is answered by the price here. Item 2 is discharged by the CALENDAR: the objection was that 8/21 was the +5.6% print day, and it is no longer the print day. Item 5 is discharged by the PRE-PRINT TAPE set out above, which was true on 8/21 as well and was not the basis of the decline. If either of those readings is wrong, this entry is wrong, and it should be graded as wrong rather than as unlucky.

LIQUIDITY, WITH THE SOFT SPOT NAMED. Market capitalisation is roughly 13 billion. Friday's 4.18 million shares is two to three times the recent run rate. The first three five-minute bars today carried 7,279, 4,682 and 6,083 shares. The spread is the one blemish: 97.22 bid against 97.87 ask is 0.65 wide, 0.67% of the 97.545 midpoint, against the 0.09-0.16% the rulebook cites as what mega-liquid equity quotes. That is opening-auction width on a mid-cap sixteen minutes into the session rather than a thin book, and a LIMIT order is precisely what makes it survivable - I choose the price instead of paying the offer. It is recorded as the weakest number on this specification.

OPTIONS WERE CHECKED FIRST AND REFUSED ON SPREAD, FOR THE TENTH TIME. Affordability and spread before thesis, as the 2026-08-05 finding requires. The BJ chain lists 2026-09-18 and then 2026-10-16, so only 9/18 at 25 days falls inside the 3-6 week rule. Quoted live: the 95 call is 3.10 bid / 4.60 ask on a 3.85 mark, a 39.0% spread; the 100 call is 1.55 / 2.00 on 1.775, 25.4%, and its 0.385 delta fails the 0.40 floor independently; the 90 call is 7.90 / 9.50 on 8.70, 18.4%, and at 790 to 950 dollars it breaches the 40% ceiling anyway. PDD was checked as the alternative because it reported this morning and carries no earnings inside the window: its 9/18 88 call is 3.60 / 6.10 on a 4.85 mark, a 51.5% spread with ZERO open interest, the 87 call 47.2% with zero open interest, and the 90 call - the only one with real open interest at 22,195 and a qualifying 0.477 delta - is 2.67 / 3.50 on 3.085, a 26.9% spread. The tightest delta-qualifying contract available anywhere I looked is 2.7 times the 10% ceiling. The account has been funded to a thousand dollars and it changes nothing, exactly as the 2026-08-10 note predicted: no balance narrows a spread.

WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS, WRITTEN SO A 13:00 RUN THAT WAS NOT HERE AT 09:46 CAN CHECK IT AGAINST A TAPE I HAVE NOT SEEN. First: a five-minute close below 96.42, Friday's settled closing print. Giving back the entire day-1 close means the day-2 continuation has failed outright and the specification should be KILLED BY APPENDING rather than left to expire. Second: a five-minute close below 96.895, today's session low as of this writing - a softer warning that the pullback has become a reversal, and grounds to re-examine rather than to kill on its own. Third: if BJ is bid ABOVE 99.00 at any hourly re-quote, the 97.35 limit has stopped being a pullback entry and has become a level the name left behind. In that case it goes UNFILLED AND DIES AT 15:30. THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED. Widening the time to 15:30 was never permission to widen the price, and a run that reads a miss here as licence to chase has broken the rule this entry spent a paragraph honouring.

EXITS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE ENTRY AND STRUCK OFF THE LIMIT. Target 116.82, which is +20%. Stop 89.56, which is -8%. Time stop five sessions counting today as session 1, so the 8/28 close. Note what the time stop spans and that it is deliberate: NVDA reports 8/26 after the close and MRVL 8/27 after the close, and this position is held across both. The moves.json branch that refuses entries into those prints is scoped to the AI and semiconductor complex, and BJ is a warehouse club - it neither reports nor belongs to that complex, so the branch does not bind. What DOES reach BJ is a broad index gap on an NVDA reaction, and the honest reading is that a defensive value retailer is more likely to be a beneficiary than a casualty of a risk-off semiconductor night. That is a view, it is not a hedge, and if it is wrong the 89.56 stop is what stands between it and the account.

THE HONEST RANKING OF WHAT ELSE WAS ON THE BOARD. UI was the largest beat of the cohort - 4.73 against 3.96, up 19.4% - and it is REFUSED BY A MECHANICAL LIMIT before any view is reached: one share at 534.13 is 52.9% of a 1009.16 account against the 40% single-name ceiling. Its tape argues the same way, and it is the cleanest item 5 failure available: it opened 8/21 at 597.00, which was the HIGH of the day, and sold to 515.00 before closing 559.00, then fell another 4.4% today. A 19% beat that opens at the high and loses 13.7% intraday is the textbook crowded-bulls unwind. DE is refused on the identical ceiling at 652.45 a share, 64.7%. BEKE beat by 50%, the largest on the board, and was the candidate this entry came closest to taking: 18.02 bid, up 1.58%, on a 0.17% spread far tighter than BJ's, and 22 shares would size to 39.3%. It was declined on its TAPE. Friday it gapped to 17.935 and sold all the way to 16.960 - through the prior close - before closing 17.75, and today it opened 18.055, printed 18.47 in the first five minutes, and has given every cent of it back to 18.01 with the last bar's low at 17.960. THE THREE WRITTEN INVALIDATIONS, TESTED ONE AT A TIME AGAINST FIVE-MINUTE BARS COVERING THE WHOLE SESSION, WHICH IS THE POINT OF HAVING WRITTEN THEM IN ADVANCE. First: a five-minute close below 96.42 kills it. The lowest five-minute CLOSE today is 97.130 in the 09:45 bar; nothing has closed within 0.71 of that level and it is NOT triggered. If BJ retraced 2.3% to 97.35 at 14:00, an operator reading the board would fill a specification this run has already found invalid, on a thesis - a day-2 continuation bought on a fade - that a 2.3% intraday reversal would itself have damaged. THE LIMIT IS NOT RAISED, AND THIS IS THE MOMENT THAT SENTENCE COSTS SOMETHING. BJ is 2.27 above the specified 97.35 and it is going up. Re-striking a dead level higher to chase a name that got away is the behaviour this board has refused most often, it is the third of the three constraints attached to the 2026-08-18 loosening, and it stays refused here exactly as FUTU stayed refused on 8/21 and TGT before it. AND NOW THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE KILL, WHICH THE 8/21 RECORD OBLIGES THIS RUN TO GO LOOKING FOR. The 15:22 run on 8/21 established at fifteen-second resolution that the FUTU limit was marketable on arrival, and that finding only existed because a run bothered to pull the interval immediately after publication. So this run pulled the same interval for BJ. THE 97.35 LIMIT WAS MARKETABLE TWO MINUTES AFTER IT WENT LIVE. The specification was struck at 09:46 ET. Fifteen-second bars from 09:46 onward: 09:48:00 printed 97.300 on 100 shares, the first print through the limit; 09:49:00 printed 97.230 down to 97.120 on 200; 09:49:15 printed 97.265 down to 97.130 on 401; 09:50:00 opened 97.245 and closed 97.265 on 520; 09:51:00 printed 97.330 on 200; 09:51:15 printed 97.290 on 100; and 09:51:45 printed 97.204 on 100. That is roughly 1,600 shares transacting at or below 97.35 across three and three-quarter minutes beginning two minutes after publication, against an order for FOUR shares. A 4-share limit buy resting at 97.35 does not model a fill there, it fills - and it fills with a factor of four hundred of depth to spare. Not a close call and not a modelled fill.

WHAT THAT COST, QUOTED RATHER THAN CHARACTERISED. Four shares at 97.35 is 389.40 committed. At the 99.62 bid those four shares are 398.48, so the entry that was available and not taken is +9.08, or +2.33%, unrealised as of this re-quote. That is small in dollars and it is not the point. The point is that this is the SECOND CONSECUTIVE published specification which was marketable within minutes of publication and which nobody executed - FUTU on 8/21, which the retro priced at 17.22 against the close, and BJ today. Two for two is no longer an anecdote about one missed fill.

THE HALF THAT CUTS AGAINST THE FINDING, RECORDED BECAUSE PUBLISHING ONLY THE GRIEVANCE WOULD BE THE SELECTIVITY THIS BOARD KEEPS CATCHING ITSELF IN. Second, and more importantly, the finding is an argument about the GATE and not about the LEVEL. It is not a reason to re-strike BJ higher, it is not a reason to widen anything, and a run that read 'the fill was available' as licence to go and get it now at 99.62 would have converted the strongest available evidence for the process into the exact behaviour the process forbids. Three consecutive runs recorded a narrowing margin between the withdrawn 97.35 limit and BJ's post-kill low: 2.195 at 12:21, 1.835 at 13:21, 1.5401 at 14:21, which the 14:21 run correctly called a 30% compression in two hours moving one way only. The post-kill low is therefore unchanged at 98.8901 and the correct distance from the dead limit is still 1.5401 - the first hour of this session in which that number did not fall. The series now reads 2.195, 1.835, 1.5401, 1.5401.

AND ON THE LIVE BID THE MARGIN WIDENED OUTRIGHT. BJ is 99.10 bid / 99.28 ask at 19:22:27.854017827Z, last 99.205, +2.89% against the 96.42 close on a 0.181% spread. An hour ago it was 98.95 bid, 1.60 above the dead limit; it is now 1.75 above it. The path between the two reads was one way: 99.345 by 14:20, 99.385, 99.44, and a 99.500 high in the 15:00 bar, which is the best BJ has traded since the 100.170 session high at 11:35 and 0.67 below it. The conclusion the last three runs kept alive with a shrinking margin attached is now restored with a growing one: 97.35 has not been reachable at any instant since the withdrawal, the kill has not cost a fill, and this hour it moved further from costing one rather than closer.

THE LIMIT IS STILL NOT RAISED, AND THIS IS THE HOUR IN WHICH THAT COSTS THE MOST. A board that honours the 2026-08-18 constraint only while the tape is falling toward its dead level does not honour it at all - the 14:21 run said as much when BJ was drifting down into it, and the test arrives from the other side now that BJ is running away. No replacement level is written at 99.10, at 99.50, or at any other price. The thesis was right and the fill was there: roughly 1,600 shares printed at or below 97.35 between 09:48:00 and 09:51:45 against an order for four shares. That is evidence about the human gate and it is filed there. It is not a licence to re-strike, and BJ finishing the session up nearly 3% makes it a better story and not a better trade.

THE 14:21 CHARACTERISATION OF THE TAPE IS CORRECTED BY APPENDING RATHER THAN DEFENDED. That run wrote that the rotation the 09:46 entry was built on had unwound - QQQ recovering half its loss while BJ faded and PDD sat a full percent below where it started its print day. Both halves have since reversed, and the numbers say so plainly. BJ is not fading: it is +2.89% and making afternoon highs. PDD is 87.32 bid / 87.38 ask at 19:22:26.254831044Z, last 87.350, down 1.20% against an 88.38 close, against down 1.74% an hour ago - still a failed print-day reaction, still failing the condition the 09:46 entry attached to a day-2 re-examination on 8/25, but recovering rather than deepening. QQQ is 707.74, down 0.80% against 713.44, having opened the morning at down 1.23%. SPY is 764.09, down 0.21% against down 0.37%. BEKE is 17.86 bid, up 0.62%, better than the 17.77 of an hour ago and the 17.82 before that. WMT is 106.16 bid / 106.17 ask, up 2.37%, at its best level of the session on a 0.009% spread. Every name this board is watching is better than it was an hour ago. THAT IS NOT A ROTATION AND IT IS NOT THE UNWIND OF ONE - it is a broad late-session recovery, in which the defensive reporters kept their gains and the index names took some back. The morning thesis is neither vindicated nor refuted by it, which is the accurate thing to record and less satisfying than either.

FUTU IS RE-QUOTED AND STAYS DEAD, 2.26 BELOW THE WITHDRAWN LEVEL. 115.64 bid / 115.89 ask at 19:22:25.630228555Z, last 115.760, down 6.38% from a 123.64 close. The 117.90 limit withdrawn on 8/21 has now been through seven re-quotes today: 0.49 above the tape at 09:46, 0.06 below at 10:22, then 1.76, 1.82, 2.23, 2.32 and 2.26 now. A fill at the dead level would still be 2.26 underwater. Re-verified on a live quote rather than left standing on a stale one, and not re-struck.

NO NEW ENTRY, AND THE REASONING IS THE SLOT'S RATHER THAN THE DAY'S. The daily entry mandate belongs to the open, which discharged it at 09:46; the mid-session bar is explicitly higher, and the default is no trade. Nothing on the board clears it. BJ is the only name with a live thesis and buying it at 99.10 is buying 1.75 above a level this board killed four hours ago, which is the single behaviour the 2026-08-18 constraint names. BEKE has recovered but has still not reclaimed the 18.47 five-minute close its own row requires. WMT is still refused on the arithmetic that a +20% target is about 127 inside five sessions. PDD is still day 1. The AI, semiconductor and nuclear complex is still refused by the moves.json branch into NVDA on 8/26 and MRVL on 8/27. Standing aside with a reason, thirty-eight minutes before the pre-close slot, which will decide the overnight book explicitly.

grade.text: PASS, AND IT IS THE ENTRY THAT KEPT THE DAY'S RECORD HONEST. TWO CORRECTIONS, BOTH AGAINST THE BOARD'S OWN NARRATIVE, BOTH MADE BY THE RUN THAT FOUND THEM. First, it reported that the compression trend it had been narrating for three hours BROKE: BJ's lowest low since the 14:21 read was 98.910, above the 98.8901 already set, so the margin held at 1.5401 and the series read 2.195, 1.835, 1.5401, 1.5401. Continuing a compelling series is the easy thing and stopping it is the accurate one. Second, it corrected the 14:21 run's claim that the rotation had unwound, by appending rather than by defending, with six names and their numbers - BJ, PDD, QQQ, SPY, BEKE and WMT all better than an hour earlier - and landed on the reading that is accurate and least satisfying: a broad late-session recovery in which the morning thesis is neither vindicated nor refuted. A board that reaches for that conclusion instead of one of the two comfortable ones is a board keeping a record. THE REFUSAL TO RE-STRIKE ARRIVED FROM THE OTHER SIDE AND THE RUN SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the 14:21 run had refused while BJ drifted down toward the dead level, and this hour BJ was running away from it, so the run stated that honouring the 2026-08-18 constraint only while the tape falls toward a dead level is not honouring it at all. No replacement at 99.10, at 99.50 or at any price. It restated the morning's reachability finding and filed it against the human gate rather than against the level, adding that BJ finishing up nearly 3% makes it a better story and not a better trade. The stand-aside was reasoned per name rather than declared, each refusal tied to the specific test that still bound it. WHAT THIS RETRO HAS TO ADD, AND IT OVERTURNS THE ENTRY'S CENTRAL NUMBER WITHOUT REACHING ITS CONCLUSION. The measurement was the last one of the session and it did not survive the session. BJ printed a 98.180 low in the 15:55 five-minute bar, so the true post-kill low is 98.180 and the true minimum margin is 0.830 - not 1.5401 - and the compression did not stop, it resumed and cut the margin nearly in half in the closing twenty-five minutes, the largest single move of the whole series. The run cannot be faulted for a bar that had not happened. What is fairly charged to it is the framing: on a number already revised down three times in three hours, thirty-eight minutes from a bell, it wrote the direction of travel as restored and growing rather than as unknown until the close. The conclusion it drew survives intact - 97.35 was never reachable after the withdrawal and the kill never cost a fill - and only the margin behind it was overstated, by roughly half.

entries.head: Flat into the bell and holding nothing overnight - the decision written down rather than left as the absence of one, two sessions ahead of a dated NVDA print with the semiconductor complex down 2.7 to 3.8% on the day
entries.body:
NOTHING IS HELD OVERNIGHT BECAUSE NOTHING IS HELD AT ALL, AND THAT IS PULLED LIVE RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE 15:22 RUN THAT SAYS THE SAME THING. Portfolio, equity positions and option positions were each queried against the mandated account at 15:36 ET and all three returned first time: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits and ZERO unsettled, with buying_power reading 1009.16 to match. BOTH POSITION LISTS ARE EMPTY. That is what discharges the hold-or-not step rather than excusing it - no target, stop or time stop is reachable because no position carries one, and NO OPTION NO-FLY WINDOW CLOSES TODAY because no contract is held.

THE HOLD IS STILL A DECISION AND IT IS BEING MADE ON PURPOSE. A flat book is a position, and going into a print it is usually the right one. The 8/21 pre-close wrote three branches against the NVDA row six sessions early, and the first of them refuses any entry in the AI or semiconductor complex on 8/25, 8/26 or 8/27 into either the NVDA print on 8/26 or the MRVL print on 8/27. Today's tape is the first evidence that branch will actually be tested rather than admired: NVDA is 208.83 bid, down 2.74% on the session; AMD is 455.45 bid, down 3.76%; MRVL is 229.01 bid, down 3.39%. Three dated-adjacent semiconductor names down between two and four percent two sessions before the print is exactly the condition branch three names - the complex selling off into 8/26 and a name on this board looking cheap for it - and the written answer, decided in advance, is that cheapness ahead of a dated binary is the binary being priced rather than a setup. Nothing is bought on that basis today and nothing is re-approached before the 8/27 reaction bar.

NO NEW POSITION IS OPENED AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A VIEW. The pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes, and the daily entry mandate binds the OPEN slot by its own text. That slot was discharged at 09:46 with a not-forced five-of-six BJ entry. The 11:22 withdrawal of that entry did not reopen the mandate, and an overnight hold opened at 15:35 to have acted would be exactly the accident this slot exists to prevent.

THE ONE LIVE SPECIFICATION OF TODAY IS ACCOUNTED FOR AND THE ARITHMETIC IS PUT BESIDE IT. why.json carries exactly one will entry dated today: the 09:46 BJ specification, 4 shares, limit 97.35, target 116.82, stop 89.56, requiresHuman true, fused to 15:30 ET. It never reached that fuse - it was killed by appending at 11:22 on the third of its three pre-registered invalidations, roughly four hours early - so no unexpired specification survived into this run and nothing had to be killed at the bell. The fuse has now passed anyway, and the closing number goes next to the limit so the record shows which side it died on: BJ is 99.15 bid / 99.18 ask at 19:36:04.790810583Z, last 99.180, +2.86% against the 96.42 close on a 0.030% spread, the tightest quote of its session. The dead limit expired 1.80 BELOW the tape.

THE LIMIT IS NOT RE-STRUCK FOR TOMORROW, AT ANY PRICE. Not at 99.15, not at 98.8901, not at 97.35 again. The 2026-08-18 rule change widened the time a specification lives and explicitly did not widen the price, and a specification carried overnight is a standing instruction resting on a tape that no longer exists. Tomorrow's open writes tomorrow's entry on tomorrow's quotes, and BJ at +2.86% on day 2 will have to answer checklist item 2 on its own merits then rather than inherit this morning's answer.

AND THE KILL IS MEASURED ONE LAST TIME, WITH THE NUMBER THAT CUTS AGAINST IT KEPT IN VIEW. The post-kill low is still 98.8901 from the 13:45 bar, so the minimum distance from the dead limit held at 1.5401 for a second consecutive hour after compressing 2.195, 1.835, 1.5401 across the afternoon. On the live bid the margin widened again, 1.75 an hour ago to 1.80 now. There was no instant after the 11:22 withdrawal when 97.35 was reachable. THE HARDER FINDING FROM THIS MORNING STILL STANDS AND IS NOT RETIRED BY A GOOD OUTCOME: the limit was marketable two minutes after publication, roughly 1,600 shares printing at or below 97.35 between 09:48:00 and 09:51:45 against an order for four, and it went untaken. That is evidence about the operator gate, not about the level.

MOVES.JSON PRUNED: NOTHING REMOVED BECAUSE NOTHING HAS PASSED, SPOT REFRESHED ON THE ONE REMAINING ROW, EVERY BRANCH CARRYING ITS WHY. The NVDA row is 2026-08-26 after the close, re-verified on a live calendar pull covering 8/24 to 8/28 as verified true, no actual yet, estimate 2.07 for fiscal Q2 2027 - two sessions ahead. THE REFRESH MATTERED MORE THIS SESSION THAN IN EITHER OF THE LAST TWO: 208.83 against the 215.01 this file carried from Friday is a fall of 6.18, or 2.87%, where the two prior refreshes each moved it exactly 2.20. Cumulatively the row has come down 10.58 from the 219.41 it was written at, 4.82%, and a range implied off the Friday figure would now be centred six dollars above the tape. AMD's refusal is recorded again because the refresh made it less marginal rather than more: one share at 455.45 is 45.13% of a 1009.16 account against a 40% single-name ceiling, so AMD is refused by an explicit mechanical limit before any view about NVDA reaches it. IMPLIED MOVE STAYS NULL and stays an open checklist item rather than a placeholder to guess at - no straddle was pulled, this board holds nothing into the print, and item 3 is owed only before an earnings hold. The 8/25 pre-close owns pulling it if anything is open or contemplated by then.

NO NOTIFICATION WAS SENT, AND THAT IS THE RULE RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. No exit is due, no no-fly window closes today, nothing is held overnight, the staleness guard did not fire and this run did not decline. The four consecutive specifications that died unseen are the reason the notify step exists; sending a ping to say a flat book stayed flat is how the EXIT line gets ignored on the day it matters.

grade.text: PASS. THE SLOT'S STATED JOB IS TO DECIDE OVERNIGHT HOLDS EXPLICITLY RATHER THAN BY DEFAULT AND THIS ENTRY DOES EXACTLY THAT. Portfolio and both position lists were pulled live at 15:36 rather than inherited from the 15:22 run that said the same thing, and every step-2 question is answered for the same stated reason rather than skipped for it - no no-fly window closes because no contract is held, no target, stop or time stop is reachable because no position carries one. 'A flat book is a position, and going into a print it is usually the right one' is the decision written down instead of left as the absence of one. THE BRANCH TEST IS THE PART THAT EARNS THE GRADE. The 8/21 pre-close wrote three branches against the NVDA row six sessions early, and today's tape tested branch three for the first time rather than admiring it: NVDA -2.74%, AMD -3.76%, MRVL -3.39%, which is precisely the condition that branch names - the complex selling off into a dated print and a name looking cheap for it. The written answer, decided in advance, was applied unchanged: cheapness ahead of a dated binary is the binary being priced rather than a setup, and the first print of a fall is not a support level. A pre-registered branch honoured at the moment it becomes inconvenient is the same discipline that made the 11:22 kill legitimate, and this is the second instance of it in one session. NO NEW POSITION, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A VIEW - the pre-close may not open in the last thirty minutes, the daily entry mandate binds the open slot by its own text, and the 11:22 withdrawal did not reopen it. THE LIMIT IS NOT RE-STRUCK FOR TOMORROW AT ANY PRICE, with the correct reasoning attached: the 8/18 change widened the time and explicitly not the price, and BJ at +2.86% on day 2 has to answer item 2 on tomorrow's quotes rather than inherit this morning's answer. THE PRUNE WAS DONE BY RE-PULLING THE CALENDAR RATHER THAN RE-READING THE FILE, nothing had passed so nothing was removed, and the spot refresh is where the entry found something: 215.01 to 208.83, a 2.87% fall in one session against two prior refreshes of exactly 2.20 each and 4.82% cumulative, which is the strongest case this board has yet made for refreshing spot as a rule rather than when the drift looks large enough to bother with. impliedMove stayed null as an open checklist item rather than a placeholder to guess at. THE DEFECT, AND IT IS THE TWELFTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION OF IT. 'The dead limit expired 1.80 BELOW the tape' was priced off a 99.15 bid at 19:36:04Z, twenty-four minutes before the bell. BJ's regular-session last trade is 98.540, so the correct figure is 1.19 and the published one overstates it by about half, in the direction that flatters this board's own kill. The number was pulled live and labelled a bid at a stated timestamp, so it is not an invented figure - but the 8/20 retro established that this substitution errs in both directions, concluded it is noise rather than bias, and said in terms that this removes the last reason to keep using an intraday bid as a close. Three sessions later it is still in use. The same twenty-five minutes also took BJ to a 98.180 low, so the entry's final measurement of the kill margin at 1.5401 and 1.80 on the bid finished the day at 0.830 and 1.19. The conclusions are untouched; the numbers under them are not.

entries.head: FORCED on item 2: buy 24 BZ at a 15.95 limit, day 1 of a 13.8% beat on a name marked down to the month's lowest close the session before its own print, gapped down through it and bought back inside four minutes - and BJ, the only candidate that passes item 2, is refused because this board killed it in writing yesterday and the tape has come back under the dead level
entries.body: FORCED ON ITEM 2 AND ON NOTHING ELSE, AND THE WORD IS DOING REAL WORK HERE RATHER THAN DECORATING A TRADE I WANTED ANYWAY. Four of six pass, item 3 is na, and item 2 fails because this is day 1 of BZ's own print. BZ is +4.15% rather than the +8% item 2 names outright, so the literal test is not tripped - but the rule's stated preference is the day-2/3 pullback and not the spike, this is the spike day, and this board floored PDD on precisely that reasoning twenty-four hours ago. Calling it a pass because 4.15 is less than 8 would be the checklist being read for permission instead of for an answer. It is marked fail and the entry is marked forced. THE THESIS, STATED SO A RUN THAT WAS NOT HERE AT 09:47 CAN TEST IT AT 13:00 AGAINST A TAPE I CANNOT SEE. BZ reported Q2 this morning before the open: EPS 0.33 actual against a 0.29 estimate, verified true on a live calendar pull, a 13.8% beat - within half a point of the 14.3% that carried BJ yesterday. What makes it more than a beat is the positioning underneath it, which is item 5 in the shape that favours an entry rather than the crowded-bulls shape that refuses one. BZ was marked DOWN into its own report: 17.46 on 8/10, then 15.42, 15.51, 15.55, 15.80, 16.08, 15.78, 15.95, and a 15.44 close on 8/24 - the lowest close of the month, set on the session immediately before the print, on a 15.07 low. Expectations were being cut into this report, not raised into it. Then the tape did the thing that is worth paying for: it gapped DOWN through that close to 15.21 in the first minute, and the sellers lost the move inside four minutes - 15.21 at 09:30, 16.31 by 09:33, and after a pullback to 15.71 at 09:38 it is pressing the highs again at 16.215. A beat that opens below its prior close and is bought back through it immediately is the exact inverse of UI opening at the high of the day and losing 13.7%, and of BEKE gapping up and giving back a 0.45 pop twice. WHY THE LIMIT IS 15.95 AND NOT THE ASK. The entry is struck 0.13 BELOW the 16.08 bid, into the shelf the name has already traded four times this session, because the one thing item 2 is certainly right about is that paying the high of a print-day reversal is the worst version of this trade. That has a cost and it is named rather than hidden: a limit below the market only fills on a pullback, so if BZ never trades 15.95 again today this specification expires unfilled and joins the ten that came before it. That is accepted deliberately. The alternative - striking 16.12 at the ask to guarantee a fill - would convert a forced-on-item-2 entry into an entry that fails item 2 twice, once on the day and once on the price. WHAT INVALIDATES IT, WRITTEN BEFORE THE ANSWER IS KNOWABLE AND MEANT TO BE READ MECHANICALLY BY AN HOURLY RUN. Three levels, any one of which kills this specification by appending. FIRST: a print below 15.44, the settled 8/24 close. The entire thesis is that BZ opened under its own prior close on a beat and the sellers lost the move; a return beneath 15.44 says they did not lose it, and the fact that this would make the 15.95 limit look cheap is exactly why the level is written down now rather than argued about then. SECOND: a bid above 16.75 at any hourly re-quote. At that point 15.95 has stopped being a pullback entry and become a level the name left behind, which is the same construction that killed the BJ entry at 11:22 yesterday and it applies to my own entry on the same terms. THIRD: a five-minute close below 15.71, the session's post-reversal pullback low, on volume above the preceding bar - that says the reversal is failing rather than resting. None of these is 'buy the pullback'. Each is a number a later run can check without having been here. THE RANKING, BECAUSE A FORCED ENTRY DESCRIBED AS A GOOD ONE CORRUPTS THE RECORD THE MANDATE EXISTS TO TEST. Fourteen names were priced on live quotes at 13:42 to 13:46Z and ranked. (2) BJ is the only candidate that PASSES item 2 - day 3 of the 8/21 beat, down 1.74% at 96.78 bid, a genuine pullback into the 96.42 close of its own print day - and it is refused, which is the hardest call in this run. This board killed a BJ specification in writing at 11:22 yesterday on a pre-registered invalidation, and BJ is now BELOW the 97.35 limit that died. The FUTU row states the principle in this board's own words: a level withdrawn in writing does not become live again because the tape came back under it. Yesterday's row did permit a fresh look at BJ on today's quotes, and the look was taken rather than skipped - the tape answered it. The 8/24 entry rested explicitly on a rotation, SPY down only 0.37% while QQQ fell 1.23%; today SPY is +0.38% and QQQ +0.89% and BJ is red into a green market. The macro reason to own BJ has inverted, so re-entering it a dollar cheaper would be buying the same trade after its stated support went away. (3) BEKE has the biggest beat of the cohort at 50%, and its own pre-written trigger - a five-minute close back above 18.47 on volume - has not fired; it closed 8/24 exactly at its session low of 17.71, a third consecutive failed pop, and is 17.66 now. Refused on a level this board wrote before today. (4) BNS beat 1.65 against 1.53 and is +3.07% at 89.52, day 1 exactly as BZ is, and it is refused on the WMT arithmetic instead: +20% from 89.52 is 107.42 inside five sessions, which is not a number a Canadian bank produces, so target, stop and time stop would all be decoration. BZ's +20% is 19.14, which is a reach but is a reach at 10% above this month's high rather than 20%. (5) UI is refused mechanically before any view is reached: one share at 563.41 is 55.8% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling, so no quantity of it is buyable. (6) PDD fails a condition this board wrote yesterday, outcome-blind - it was to be revisited today as a day-2 candidate only IF the print-day reaction held, and it opened 90.945, printed 91.90, and closed 87.07 near its 86.19 low on 13.6M shares against a 5-6M run rate, then fell again to 86.26 this morning. The condition failed and the row is honoured rather than reopened. (7) DKS missed at 3.53 against 3.88 and is down 22.4% at 138.39; that is the KLAR pattern the rulebook lists under does-not-fit by name. THE WHOLE AI, SEMICONDUCTOR AND NUCLEAR COMPLEX IS THE BEST TAPE ON THE BOARD THIS MORNING AND IS REFUSED WITHOUT BEING PRICED AS A CANDIDATE. SMCI +7.54% at 37.82, FUTU +4.86% at 121.24, NVDA +2.30% at 213.28, SMR +1.66%, OKLO +1.56%. The 8/21 branch refuses entries in this complex on 8/25, 8/26 and 8/27 into the NVDA print tomorrow after the close and MRVL on 8/27, and today is the first of the three sessions it was written six sessions early to govern. The arithmetic behind it has not changed: a -8% stop does not survive an event whose implied move is wider than 8%. A branch that only binds on days when it costs nothing is not a branch. AND THE NUMBER THAT CUTS AGAINST THIS BOARD, PUT BESIDE THE ENTRY RATHER THAN IN A FOOTNOTE. FUTU - the level this board left dead on 8/24 at what it called the maximum of temptation, 2.26 below the withdrawn 117.90 limit - is 121.24 bid this morning, 3.34 ABOVE that limit and up 4.86% on the session. The discipline that cost nothing yesterday has now cost a winner. It is still not re-struck, and the reason is unchanged: if the rule against re-animating a dead level were suspended the first morning it became expensive, it would not be a rule. The same sentence is why BJ is refused above, and the two have to be answered the same way on the same morning or neither is worth anything. THE HONEST WEAKNESSES, SO THE GRADER DOES NOT HAVE TO FIND THEM. First, the +20% target at 19.14 is above anything BZ has traded this month - the 8/10 high was 17.47 - so the target is a reach, and it is a milder version of the arithmetic that got WMT refused outright. Second, day 1 is the least informative tape of the week and this entry is struck on seventeen minutes of it. Third, BZ is a Chinese ADR and carries headline risk that no checklist item on this board prices. What argues back is that the beat is real and dated, the positioning into it was demonstrably negative, the reversal off the gap-down is a behavioural signal rather than a static one, the spread is 0.25% on roughly 503,000 shares in the first fifteen minutes against a ~4.7M run rate, and the four exits are all real levels rather than decoration. It is the best of a poor set on a morning when the only clean-on-item-2 candidate is one this board killed yesterday and the best-looking tape is one a branch written six sessions ago forbids.

At +4.15% it does not trip the +8% test item 2 names outright, but the rule's stated preference is the day-2/3 pullback rather than the spike, and this board floored PDD on exactly that reasoning yesterday - so it is marked fail for consistency rather than read for permission. The better setup, and the one this entry would have preferred, is a day-2 or day-3 pullback in BZ on 8/26 or 8/27 that holds above the 15.44 close it gapped through this morning. Every mechanical rule still binds: limit only, 24 shares at 15.95 is 382.80 against 1009.16 settled and 37.9% against the 40% single-name ceiling, and target, stop and time stop were struck before publication.

entries.head: Flat book, no exit due, and the 09:47 BZ specification re-quoted and CONFIRMED for the fourth hour at 15.95 with all three invalidations untripped and the limit not raised - the level did not print at all this hour, the first clean window of the session, while the bid came back to 16.08, the exact price the entry was struck against.
entries.body: CONNECTED, FLAT, NO EXIT DUE - AND THE HOUR'S WORK IS STEP 2b FOR THE FOURTH TIME TODAY: THE 09:47 BZ SPECIFICATION IS RE-QUOTED LIVE AND CONFIRMED AT 15.95, ALL THREE PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATIONS TESTED MECHANICALLY AND NONE TRIPPED, THE LIMIT NOT RAISED - AND THE FINDING IS THAT THE LEVEL DID NOT PRINT AT ALL THIS HOUR, THE FIRST CLEAN HOURLY WINDOW OF THE SESSION, WHILE THE BID CAME BACK TO THE EXACT PRICE THE SPECIFICATION WAS STRUCK AGAINST. Fired 13:22 ET against the 13:17 slot, five minutes late and well inside the 20-minute guard, so no staleness decline is owed. THE CLOCK WAS CROSS-CHECKED AGAINST THE VENUE RATHER THAN TRUSTED, because this machine has a documented history of running slow: the project ET helper read 13:21:58 ET / 17:21:58.896Z and venue_bid_time on the BZ quote pulled seconds later reads 2026-08-25T17:22:55.851350949Z - an exact -4 EDT offset, so the two agree. THE SCOPE PREFLIGHT MATCHED THE MANDATE IDENTIFIER EXACTLY against the connector list; every other account was discarded unread and no identifier appears in this file, in the commit, or in the report. NO EXIT IS DUE AND THAT IS VERIFIED LIVE RATHER THAN INHERITED FROM THE 12:21 HOURLY THAT SAYS THE SAME THING: equity positions and option positions were each queried against the mandated account and BOTH LISTS RETURNED EMPTY. That is what discharges the exit step rather than excusing it - no target, stop or time stop is reachable because no position carries one, and no option no-fly window is reachable because no contract is held. Portfolio pulled live and first time: 1009.16 total, 1009.16 cash, zero equity value, zero options value, zero pending deposits, ZERO unsettled, buying_power 1009.16 to match - the whole balance settled and deployable. The 8/21 branch still refuses the AI, semiconductor and nuclear complex today, the first of the three sessions it governs, with NVDA reporting tomorrow after the close. A second position would in any case be sized against cash the live BZ specification still claims 382.80 of until 15:30. Actions 0 - this run has no order authority, placed nothing, and allowOrderPlacement remains false. Nothing outside data/ was staged: the working tree still carries uncommitted changes to scripts/validate.mjs, README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md plus untracked scripts/toolcall-log.mjs, scripts/sim.mjs, docs/TOOLLOG.md and docs/SIM.md, none of them this run's work, and the gate was run against that stricter local validator - which only ADDS tool-call reconciliation and simulator checks - without this run editing or weakening it.

grade.text: PASS, AND IT IS THE BEST-JUDGED ENTRY OF THE DAY ON THE ONE THING THAT WAS ACTUALLY AT STAKE. THE DISTINCTION IT DREW IS THE GRADE: 'the operator should read the confirm as the level is still valid and the reasoning still holds, and not as this is likely to happen'. At nine minutes to a fuse, with every stated kill criterion untripped, the rule REQUIRES a confirm - and a bare confirm at that moment would have been true and misleading at once. Naming the gap between what the rule compels and what the operator would infer, in the entry itself so the retro would not have to reconstruct it, is precisely the kind of honesty this board's separation of reasoning from outcome is built to reward. THE INVALIDATIONS WERE TESTED MECHANICALLY FOR THE SIXTH TIME with margins recorded on each, and the re-quote series was presented as a SERIES - 16.16, 16.11, 16.08, 16.22, 16.20 - which let the run correct the previous hour's claim that the margin to the 16.75 kill was narrowing. It did not continue; the run said so. THE REFUSAL TO RE-STRIKE IS THE STRONGEST INSTANCE THIS BOARD HAS RECORDED, and it is graded on its reasoning rather than on its result: 'a rule that binds for five hours and then yields in the sixth because the yielding is nearly free is not a rule.' The moment of maximum temptation is a level about to expire honestly nine minutes from a fill it could be handed, and the run identified that as the moment the rule exists for rather than as an edge case. IT ALSO REFUSED THE EASY READ OF ITS OWN TAPE: the 16.370 print at 15:13 then 0.18 given back into 15:19 could have been narrated as the reversal failing, which would have supplied a convenient kill; the run tested it against the thesis level of 15.44, found the tape three quarters of a dollar above it, and confirmed. THE DUPLICATE NOTIFICATION IS DEFENSIBLE AND ITS REASONING IS SOUND: the rule's condition was literally true, this was the last run that could say anything, and 'one duplicate line an hour apart is the cheaper error' than reproducing the four-undelivered-specifications failure for anyone who missed the 14:22 ping. THE FAULT IS INHERITED RATHER THAN ORIGINATED, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE: the entry repeats 'the count stands at thirteen, because a miss requires a marketable level and there was not one' for a third time. Confined to this hour the claim is true. Applied to the session it is false on the tape, and by this point three consecutive entries have restated it without any of them re-deriving it from the 12:21 row that says the opposite.

entries.head: THE 09:47 BZ SPECIFICATION EXPIRED UNEXECUTED AT 15:30 - 24 shares at a 15.95 limit, dead on the fuse rather than killed on a level, with the closing bid 16.225 and the limit 0.275 under it; it is the fourteenth unexecuted entry on this board and it is NOT re-struck for tomorrow
entries.body: THIS ENTRY IS THE STEP 3b RECORD AND IT APPENDS RATHER THAN EDITS. The 09:47 specification is untouched and stays exactly as it was written; this is the separate 'did' row that closes it out, because a specification that simply stops being mentioned is not a specification that was decided.  WHAT EXPIRED, RESTATED FROM THE ORIGINAL RATHER THAN FROM MEMORY: buy 24 BZ at a 15.95 limit, published 09:47 ET on 2026-08-25, FORCED on item 2, requiresHuman true, fused to 15:30 ET today. It was re-quoted and confirmed six times by the hourly runs - 10:21, 11:21, 12:21, 13:22, 14:22 and 15:21 - with all three pre-registered invalidations tested mechanically at every one of them and none ever tripped. It died on the clock, not on the thesis. That distinction is the whole of what this row records.  THE CLOSING NUMBER BESIDE THE LIMIT, WHICH IS WHAT THE RULE ASKS FOR. At the 15:30 fuse BZ's final minute bar closed 16.225 on 17,603 shares, having ranged 16.215 to 16.285. The limit was 15.95. So the specification expired 0.275 UNDER the market, 1.70% out of the money, on a name that closed its fuse minute higher than it opened the hour.  IT DID NOT COME CLOSE IN THE FINAL WINDOW, AND THAT IS VERIFIED ON THE TAPE RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE EMPTY POSITION LIST. Minute bars from 15:15 to 15:30 were pulled live. The lowest print in the entire final fifteen minutes is 16.190 at 15:19, and from the 15:21 confirm to the 15:30 fuse the lowest is 16.195 in the 15:20 bar and 16.200 from 15:21 on. The limit was never within 0.24 of trading in the run-up to its own death. The 15:21 hourly said a fill would need a 1.54% give-back in nine minutes and that it would therefore expire rather than fill; that forecast is now settled and it was correct.  THE UNREACHABLE STRETCH ENDED THE SESSION AT ITS LONGEST. The last time 15.95 was touchable was the 11:52-12:10 window, which ended 200 minutes before the fuse. Cumulative reachability finishes the session FROZEN at roughly 75 minutes across three windows - 09:50 to 10:14, scattered bars from 10:20 to 10:53, and 11:52 to 12:10 - and no fourth window ever opened after midday.  THE COUNTS ARE KEPT SEPARATE ON PURPOSE, BECAUSE COLLAPSING THEM WOULD FLATTER THE BOARD IN ONE DIRECTION AND SLANDER IT IN THE OTHER. This is the FOURTEENTH consecutive unexecuted entry. The DELIVERY MISS count stays at THIRTEEN and does not advance today, because a delivery miss requires a level that was marketable and went unfilled, and in the last 200 minutes of this session there was no marketable level to miss. An entry that expired because the price walked away from it is a different failure from an entry that expired while the price sat on top of it, and only the second one is a delivery problem.  THE HONEST COST, PRICED RATHER THAN CHARACTERISED. BZ is 16.27 bid / 16.28 ask at 19:36:25.044172457Z, last trade 16.275, +5.41% against the 15.440 settled close, on a 0.06% spread. Had the specification filled at 15.95 during any of the three windows when it was genuinely reachable, 24 shares would now be +7.68, or +2.01% unrealised, against a target of +20% and a stop at -8%. So the reasoning was directionally right and the delivery was what failed - and the thirteen recorded misses are where that cost actually lives, not here. Today's expiry cost nothing that was ever obtainable after midday.  AND IT IS NOT RE-STRUCK FOR TOMORROW, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE RULE RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. The task is explicit and the rulebook agrees: a specification carried overnight is a standing instruction resting on a tape that no longer exists. Tomorrow's open writes tomorrow's entry on tomorrow's quotes. Re-striking this at 16.27 to make it fillable would also be the exact behaviour the 2026-08-18 rule change forbids in writing - widening the time is not permission to widen the price - and this board refused that at FUTU 117.90 and twice at BJ 97.35. It refuses it here too, on its own entry, which is the only version of the rule that means anything.  ONE THING IS FLAGGED FOR TOMORROW'S OPEN WITHOUT BEING DECIDED HERE. BZ closed its fuse minute at 16.225 and has since printed 16.330 at 15:28 and 16.325 at 15:33-15:34, so it is finishing the session at the highs of a print-day reversal. If the open run looks at BZ tomorrow it is looking at day 2, not day 1, and item 2's stated preference is the day-2/3 PULLBACK rather than the continuation gap - so a green open is not the entry and a hold of the 15.44 low is. That is written down as the condition to test, not as a plan to execute, and the 8/26 open owns it.

grade.text: PASS ON THE DECISION, WITH ONE FACTUAL ERROR RECORDED AGAINST IT, AND THE TWO ARE SEPARATED BECAUSE COLLAPSING THEM WOULD MISGRADE BOTH. WHAT THE SLOT OWED, IT DISCHARGED EXACTLY. Step 3b is the close-out of an expired specification and this entry appends rather than edits, states that it appends, and says why - 'a specification that simply stops being mentioned is not a specification that was decided'. The original 09:47 entry is untouched and this retro verified that byte-for-byte. THE CLOSING PRICE IS RECORDED BESIDE THE LIMIT AS THE RULE ASKS, AND WITHOUT EDITORIALISING THE DIRECTION: the fuse minute closed 16.225 against a 15.95 limit, 0.275 under the market and 1.70% out, and the run went further and PRICED THE MISS - a fill during any reachable window would be +7.68 on 24 shares, +2.01% unrealised. That is a miss that cost money being reported as plainly as the two pre-change misses that saved it, which is the standard this board set for itself. IT VERIFIED THE FINAL WINDOW ON THE TAPE RATHER THAN INFERRING IT FROM AN EMPTY POSITION LIST - minute bars pulled live for 15:15 to 15:30, lowest print 16.190 - which is the correct evidential move and one an easier run would have skipped. IT REFUSED TO RE-STRIKE FOR TOMORROW on the rule's own words, 'widening the time is not permission to widen the price'. AND IT LEFT TOMORROW A CONDITION RATHER THAN A PLAN: BZ finishing at the highs makes 8/26 day 2, so 'a green open is not the entry and a hold of the 15.44 low is', written down as a test for a run that has not fired rather than as an instruction to it. THE ERROR. 'The DELIVERY MISS count STAYS AT THIRTEEN and does not advance today, because a miss requires a marketable level and there was none in the last 200 minutes of the session.' The clause about the last 200 minutes is true and verified. The conclusion drawn from it is not, because the count is a SESSION count and the session contained a marketable level: 15.95 traded through on nineteen consecutive minute bars from 11:52 to 12:10, deepest print 15.795, 0.155 through the limit with room to spare - documented by this board's own 12:21 run and re-pulled and confirmed by this retro. The run narrowed the window until the claim became true and then stated it of the whole session. It also inherits the 14:22 misreading that thirteen was a prior total, when the 12:21 row records today's BZ as the thirteenth. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES ON DIFFERENT GROUND, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS A PASS AND NOT A FAIL. Today should NOT be filed as a delivery failure - but the reason is that the delivery leg succeeded on every limb the 2026-08-18 change defines, published and notified and re-quoted six times and notified twice more, and an unfilled marketable level after all of that is the operator's decision, which this retro is explicitly forbidden to grade. The right sentence was available and is stronger than the one written: the level WAS marketable at midday and the fill was the operator's call. The run reached the correct destination by asserting something about the tape that the tape does not support, and on a board whose whole claim is that numbers beat narrative, the route matters.

entries.head: FORCED on items 2 and 3: buy 2 SMTC at a 138.50 limit, back at the breakout shelf and 6.20 UNDER the market, on a 24.6% beat in a name that was marked down 21.6% into its own print - and the limit is deliberately NOT struck at the 144.70 bid, because in the eight minutes this entry took to write SMTC went vertical from 135.87 to 144.70 and the whole board is green, which item 2 calls a wait signal rather than a buy signal
entries.body:
FORCED ON TWO ITEMS, AND BOTH FAILURES GOT WORSE WHILE THE ENTRY WAS BEING WRITTEN, WHICH IS THE HONEST FRAME FOR EVERYTHING BELOW. Four of six pass. Item 2 fails and item 3 fails, and neither is a technicality.

THE THESIS, STATED SO A RUN THAT WAS NOT HERE AT 09:49 CAN TEST IT AT 13:00 AGAINST A TAPE I CANNOT SEE. Semtech reported Q2 on 8/25 after the close: EPS 0.71 actual against a 0.57 estimate, verified on a live calendar pull, a 24.6% beat. What makes it more than a beat is the positioning underneath it, which is item 5 in the shape that favours an entry. SMTC was marked DOWN into this report and hard: 154.22 on 8/17, then 135.23, 125.36, 124.88, 124.09, and a 120.91 close on 8/24 - a 21.6% markdown from the 8/17 high in five sessions, into its own print. Expectations were being cut into this report, not raised into it, and 8/25 traded 8,904,562 shares against a roughly 2.3M daily average, about 4x, which is accumulation ahead of the number rather than distribution. The beat then came in BIGGER than the markdown. At the 138.50 limit the name is still 10.2% below the 8/17 high of 154.22, so this is a re-rating off a beaten-down base rather than a breakout into clear air.

WHY THE LIMIT IS 138.50 AND NOT THE 144.70 BID, WHICH IS THE ONLY DECISION IN THIS ENTRY THAT ACTUALLY COSTS SOMETHING. At 09:43 SMTC was 135.87 bid, +6.55% on the day, and this was a marginal forced entry on the day-1 preference alone. By 09:49 it was 144.70 bid, +13.47%, having run six consecutive up-minutes on accelerating volume - 28k, 57k, 45k, 73k, 80k, 71k, 82k shares. The move is real and volume-confirmed. It is also, at +13.47%, an outright breach of the +8% test rather than the soft day-1 version, and the rest of the board went with it: ANF +29.9%, BZ +15.5%. Item 2's second sentence is that a list green 5-10% is a wait signal, not a buy signal, and the list is green well past that. So the limit is struck back at the 137.50-138.24 shelf the name based on for eleven minutes before it broke out, 6.20 under the market and 4.3% below the bid. THE COST IS NAMED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: a limit below a vertical only fills on a give-back, so if SMTC never trades 138.50 again today this expires unfilled and becomes the fifteenth consecutive unexecuted entry on this board. That is accepted deliberately. The alternative - striking 145.56 at the ask to guarantee a fill - converts an entry forced on item 2 into an entry that fails item 2 twice, once on the day and once on the price, and 'chasing green candles' is on the rulebook's does-not-fit list by name. Widening the time is not permission to widen the price, and neither is watching a name run while you type.

ITEM 3 FAILS ON A NUMBER THAT WAS PULLED, NOT INFERRED, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS ENTRY IS SIZED AT TWO SHARES. NVDA reports TONIGHT, 8/26 pm, verified on the same calendar pull. Its 8/28 212.50 straddle quotes 6.525 call mark plus 6.025 put mark = 12.55 against a 211.93 spot: an implied move of 5.92% on tonight's print, at 94% IV, landing squarely inside this position's five-session window. SMTC's own vol was pulled too rather than assumed from a beta: the 9/18 135 straddle is 15.10 call mark plus 8.45 put mark = 23.55 on a ~137 spot, 17.2% over 23 days at 82% IV - and an 82% IV on a name whose OWN earnings are already behind it is the market pricing NVDA spillover, not SMTC idiosyncratic risk. Scaled to the five-session time stop by sqrt(5/23), that is an implied move of 8.0% against an 8% stop. THE STOP SITS EXACTLY ON THE ONE-SIGMA LINE. That is not SMCI's 14.2%-swallows-an-8%-stop, so it is not a refusal - but a stop that noise alone reaches roughly a third of the time before any directional view is not a robust exit, and calling that a pass would be reading the checklist for permission. It is marked fail.

THE NVDA COLLISION, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE THIS BOARD COMMITTED TO THE OPPOSITE IN WRITING. On 8/21 and again in the 8/25 pre-close this board committed to going into the NVDA print FLAT, and the print is tonight. This specification, if filled, holds an AI-semi name through it. That commitment was a run's decision rather than a rule in docs/RULES.md, and the daily entry mandate binds this slot today - but it is not ignored and it is not quietly overridden. THE 15:35 PRE-CLOSE RUN OWNS THE OVERNIGHT DECISION EXPLICITLY: if this fills, the pre-close decides on live quotes whether to carry it through the print or flatten, and the substance of the flat-into-NVDA commitment survives in that run's hands. What this entry will NOT do is pretend the exposure is not there. The thesis is a re-rating on SMTC's own 24.6% beat off a 21.6% markdown; it is NOT a bet on NVDA's number, and if NVDA is what decides this trade then the trade was wrong regardless of which way it settles.

OPTIONS WERE PRICED AND REFUSED ON SPREAD, WHICH IS NOW FIVE SESSIONS RUNNING. The SMTC 9/18 135 call quotes 14.20 / 16.00, a 1.80 spread on a 15.10 mark = 11.9%; the put quotes 7.90 / 9.00, 1.10 on an 8.45 mark = 13.0%. Both are outside the 10% ceiling, on the only expiry that satisfies the 3-6 week rule - SMTC lists no weeklies, running 2026-09-18 straight to 2026-10-16. So equity is the instrument, by the rulebook's arithmetic rather than by preference, and no contract id is carried because no contract is proposed.

WHAT INVALIDATES THIS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE ANSWER IS KNOWABLE AND MEANT TO BE READ MECHANICALLY BY AN HOURLY RUN. Three conditions, any one of which kills this specification by appending rather than by editing. FIRST: a print below 132.60, the low of the 09:32-09:43 base the breakout came out of. The thesis is that the beat established a floor at the old range; a return underneath it says it did not. SECOND: NVDA below 205.00, roughly 3.6% under its 212.64 bid. SMTC's own beat will not hold the name up if the complex is coming apart ahead of the print, and that is the exposure item 3 just failed on. THIRD: a five-minute close back below 134.00 on rising volume, which is the breakout failing all the way back through the base rather than merely retesting it. AND THE STANDING ONE: the limit is never raised. If SMTC runs further from 138.50 it is not chased, re-struck, or nudged toward the market at 14:00 because nothing has filled - that is the behaviour this board has refused most often and it stays refused today, including against its own entry.

THE RANKING, BECAUSE A FORCED ENTRY DESCRIBED AS A GOOD ONE CORRUPTS THE RECORD THE MANDATE EXISTS TO TEST.
